title: Optimal Work Extraction From Finite-time Closed Quantum Dynamics
authors: Shoki Sugimoto, Takahiro Sagawa, And Ryusuke Hamazaki
abstract:
Author(s): Shoki Sugimoto, Takahiro Sagawa, and Ryusuke Hamazaki

Extracting useful work from quantum systems is a fundamental problem in quantum thermodynamics. In scenarios where rapid protocols are desired—whether due to practical constraints or deliberate design choices—a fundamental trade-off between power and efficiency is yet to be established. Here, we inv…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023321] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives fundamental bounds on work extraction from finite-time closed quantum dynamics, revealing a trade-off between power and efficiency.
motivation: Understanding the fundamental limits of work extraction in quantum systems is crucial for designing efficient quantum engines and protocols, especially when time constraints are present.
method: The authors use optimal control theory and quantum thermodynamic principles to analyze work extraction from closed quantum systems undergoing finite-time unitary evolution.
result: They establish a general bound relating the extracted work, the duration of the protocol, and the quantum speed limit, showing that faster protocols incur higher energetic costs.
conclusion: The work provides a fundamental thermodynamic constraint for finite-time quantum processes, with implications for quantum heat engines and information processing.

title: Coherent Control Of Interacting Solid-state Spins Below The Diffraction Limit
authors: Haitong Xu
Mehmet T. Uysal
Łukasz Dusanowski
Adam T. Turflinger
Ashwin K. Boddeti
Joseph Alexander
Jeff D. Thompson
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 26 June 2026;
tldr: Demonstrates coherent control of individual rare-earth ion spins below the diffraction limit, enabling addressability of closely spaced spins for quantum networks.
motivation: Solid-state spins are promising for quantum networks but are often too densely packed to be individually addressed, limiting scalability.
method: Uses optical techniques to achieve sub-diffraction-limit addressing and coherent control of interacting rare-earth dopants in a solid-state host.
result: Achieves single-spin control and coherent manipulation of interacting rare-earth spins, overcoming the diffraction barrier.
conclusion: This work enables scalable quantum network nodes using dense ensembles of solid-state spins with individual addressability.

title: A Photonic Integrated Long-distance Quantum Communication Network
authors: Likang Zhang
Jiawei Pan
Teng-Yun Chen
Zheng-Ping Li
Yichen Lu
Wei Li
Wen-Xin Pan
Wei Ke
Yuyao Guo
Wenwen Li
Sheng-Kai Liao
Cheng-Zhi Peng
Linjie Zhou
Xinlun Cai
Feihu Xu
Jian-Wei Pan
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 19 June 2026;
tldr: A photonic integrated quantum network using twin-field QKD over 540 km fiber with full connectivity between four users.
motivation: To demonstrate a scalable, long-distance quantum communication network using integrated photonics and twin-field QKD.
method: A spine-leaf network architecture with four users connected via a central node, using twin-field QKD at 1.25 GHz clock rate over up to 540 km fiber.
result: Achieved a secret key rate of 9.38 × 10⁻⁹ bit per pulse with full connectivity between any two user pairs.
conclusion: The work shows the feasibility of integrated photonic quantum networks for long-distance secure communication.

title: Analytical Computation Of Entanglement Distribution Time In First-generation Quantum Repeater Chains
authors: Luca Tavanti
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 20 June 2026;
tldr: Analytical model for entanglement distribution time in first-generation quantum repeater chains.
motivation: Understanding the time required to distribute entanglement over long distances is crucial for designing efficient quantum repeater networks.
method: Derives closed-form expressions for the distribution time considering probabilistic entanglement swapping, memory decoherence, and finite resources.
result: Provides analytical formulas that accurately predict the average entanglement distribution time and its variance for various chain lengths and parameters.
conclusion: The analytical model enables rapid optimization of repeater chain parameters without costly simulations, advancing practical quantum network design.

title: Thermodynamic Irreversibility In Optical Bistability
authors: G. Keijsers, R. M. de Boer, B. Verdonschot, K. J. H. Peters, And S. R. K. Rodriguez
abstract:
Author(s): G. Keijsers, R. M. de Boer, B. Verdonschot, K. J. H. Peters, and S. R. K. Rodriguez

We demonstrate thermodynamic irreversibility in the stochastic switching of a coherently driven bistable optical cavity. We present measurements of phase space probability currents evidencing the breaking of detailed balance associated with thermodynamic irreversibility. We also estimate the magnitu…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 253803] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of thermodynamic irreversibility in a bistable optical cavity via phase space probability currents and entropy production estimation.
motivation: To directly observe and quantify thermodynamic irreversibility in a driven-dissipative optical system, linking stochastic switching to non-equilibrium thermodynamics.
method: Measurements of phase space probability currents in a coherently driven bistable optical cavity, with estimation of entropy production rate.
result: Clear evidence of broken detailed balance and finite entropy production, demonstrating irreversibility in the switching dynamics.
conclusion: Optical bistability provides a clean platform for studying non-equilibrium thermodynamics and the thermodynamic cost of information processing in photonic systems.

title: Shake Before Use: Universal Enhancement Of Quantum Thermometry By Unitary Driving
authors: Emanuele Tumbiolo, Lorenzo Maccone, Chiara Macchiavello, Matteo G. A. Paris, And Giacomo Guarnieri
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuele Tumbiolo, Lorenzo Maccone, Chiara Macchiavello, Matteo G. A. Paris, and Giacomo Guarnieri

Quantum thermometry aims at determining temperature with ultimate precision in the quantum regime. Standard equilibrium approaches, limited by the quantum Fisher information given by static energy fluctuations, lose sensitivity outside a fixed temperature window. Nonequilibrium strategies have there…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 250401] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Universal enhancement of quantum thermometry precision via unitary driving, surpassing equilibrium limits.
motivation: Standard equilibrium quantum thermometry loses sensitivity outside a fixed temperature window; nonequilibrium strategies can overcome this.
method: The authors propose a universal unitary driving protocol that enhances the quantum Fisher information for temperature estimation, independent of the system details.
result: The protocol achieves a precision scaling beyond the standard equilibrium bound, with explicit examples demonstrating improvement.
conclusion: Unitary driving provides a general and practical method to improve quantum thermometry, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and sensing.

title: Clifford Hierarchy Stabilizer Codes: Transversal Non-Clifford Gates And Magic States
authors: Ryohei Kobayashi, Guanyu Zhu, And Po-Shen Hsin
abstract:
Author(s): Ryohei Kobayashi, Guanyu Zhu, and Po-Shen Hsin

A fundamental problem in fault-tolerant quantum computation is the tradeoff between universality and dimensionality, exemplified by the Bravyi-König bound for [MATH]-dimensional topological stabilizer codes. In this Letter, we extend topological Pauli stabilizer codes to a broad class of [MATH]-dimensiona…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 250802] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends topological stabilizer codes to higher dimensions to achieve transversal non-Clifford gates and magic state distillation, breaking the Bravyi-König bound.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires universal gate sets, but transversal gates are limited by the Bravyi-König bound. The authors aim to circumvent this by using higher-dimensional codes.
method: They construct Clifford hierarchy stabilizer codes in d dimensions, leveraging the structure of the Clifford hierarchy to design codes with transversal T gates and other non-Clifford gates.
result: They demonstrate that d-dimensional codes can support transversal non-Clifford gates, enabling magic state distillation with improved thresholds and reduced overhead.
conclusion: Higher-dimensional topological stabilizer codes offer a promising route to universal fault-tolerant quantum computation with transversal gates, challenging the conventional limitations.

title: Heat, Work, And Fluctuations In A Driven Quantum Resonator
authors: Riya Baruah, Pedro Portugal, Jun-Zhe Chen (陈俊哲), Joachim Wabnig, And Christian Flindt
abstract:
Author(s): Riya Baruah, Pedro Portugal, Jun-Zhe Chen (陈俊哲), Joachim Wabnig, and Christian Flindt

A central building block of a heat engine is the working fluid, which mediates the conversion of heat into work. In nanoscale heat engines, the working fluid can be a quantum system whose behavior and dynamics are nonclassical. A particularly versatile realization is a quantum resonator, which allow…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064151] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies heat, work, and fluctuations in a driven quantum resonator, a model system for nanoscale heat engines.
motivation: Understanding nonclassical behavior of working fluids in quantum heat engines is crucial for advancing quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors analyze a quantum resonator under periodic driving using full counting statistics and Floquet theory to compute work and heat distributions.
result: They derive fluctuation relations and show that quantum coherence can enhance work extraction beyond classical limits.
conclusion: Quantum resonators can serve as efficient working fluids in nanoscale heat engines, with fluctuations governed by quantum thermodynamic laws.

title: Universal Thermodynamic Uncertainty Relation For Quantum $f$ Divergences
authors: Domingos S. P. Salazar
abstract:
Author(s): Domingos S. P. Salazar

We show that any Petz [MATH] divergence (where [MATH] is operator convex) between quantum states admits a universal [MATH]-mixture representation: the distinguishability of [MATH] from [MATH] is obtained as a positive superposition of quadratic contrasts [MATH], with non-negative weights [MATH] …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064150] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Establishes a universal thermodynamic uncertainty relation for quantum f-divergences, linking distinguishability to thermodynamic cost.
motivation: To derive a general bound on the distinguishability of quantum states in terms of thermodynamic quantities, extending classical thermodynamic uncertainty relations to the quantum regime.
method: Uses Petz f-divergences and operator convex functions to represent distinguishability as a mixture of quadratic contrasts, then applies the quantum Cramér-Rao bound.
result: A universal thermodynamic uncertainty relation for any Petz f-divergence, showing that the distinguishability is bounded by the thermodynamic cost (e.g., entropy production).
conclusion: Provides a unified framework for thermodynamic uncertainty relations in quantum systems, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and information processing.

title: Strong Coupling In A Three-mode Superconducting-spin Hybrid Quantum System
authors: Yingqiu Mao, Han-Yu Ren, Zi-Yi Liu, Yi-Zheng Zhen, Tao Rong, Tao Jiang, Zhuo Chen, Zhe-Heng Yuan, Wen-Hua Qin, Xiaoran Zhang, Xiaobing Liu, Ming Gong, Kae Nemoto, William J. Munro, And Johannes Majer
abstract:
Author(s): Yingqiu Mao, Han-Yu Ren, Zi-Yi Liu, Yi-Zheng Zhen, Tao Rong, Tao Jiang, Zhuo Chen, Zhe-Heng Yuan, Wen-Hua Qin, Xiaoran Zhang, Xiaobing Liu, Ming Gong, Kae Nemoto, William J. Munro, and Johannes Majer

We demonstrate strong coupling in a solid-state hybrid quantum system comprising a fixed-frequency coplanar-waveguide resonator, a superconducting transmon qubit, and an ensemble of nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond. Frequency-domain spectroscopy reveals a characteristic three-mode avoided crossin…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023343] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates strong coupling in a three-mode hybrid system comprising a superconducting resonator, transmon qubit, and NV center ensemble.
motivation: Hybrid quantum systems combining superconducting circuits with spin ensembles are promising for quantum information processing, but achieving strong coupling in multi-mode configurations is challenging.
method: Frequency-domain spectroscopy is used to observe a three-mode avoided crossing, indicating coherent coupling between the resonator, transmon, and NV ensemble.
result: Clear evidence of strong coupling is observed, with coupling strengths exceeding decoherence rates.
conclusion: This work establishes a solid-state platform for multi-mode hybrid quantum systems, enabling future studies in quantum information and thermodynamics.

title: Detecting Quantum Noise Of A Solid-state Spin Ensemble With Dispersive Measurement
authors: Mikhail Mamaev, Jayameenakshi Venkatraman, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ania C. Bleszynski Jayich, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Mikhail Mamaev, Jayameenakshi Venkatraman, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ania C. Bleszynski Jayich, and Aashish A. Clerk

We theoretically explore protocols for measuring the spin polarization of an ensemble of solid-state spins, with precision at or below the standard quantum limit. Such measurements in the solid state are challenging, as standard approaches based on optical fluorescence are often limited by poor read…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023331] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes dispersive measurement protocols to detect spin polarization of solid-state spin ensembles with precision at or below the standard quantum limit.
motivation: Solid-state spin ensembles are promising for quantum memories and sensors, but optical fluorescence readout is often inefficient; dispersive measurement offers a non-destructive alternative.
method: The authors theoretically analyze dispersive measurement schemes using cavity or circuit QED techniques, modeling the spin ensemble as a collective spin coupled to a readout resonator.
result: They show that with optimized parameters, the measurement can achieve sub-SQL sensitivity and extract information about spin polarization and noise.
conclusion: Dispersive measurement is a viable route for high-precision readout of solid-state spin ensembles, enabling applications in quantum sensing and memory.

title: Experimental Measurement And A Physical Interpretation Of Quantum Shadow Enumerators
authors: Daniel Miller, Kyano Levi, Lukas Postler, Alex Steiner, Lennart Bittel, Gregory A. L. White, Yifan Tang, Eric J. Kuehnke, Antonio A. Mele, Sumeet Khatri, Lorenzo Leone, Jose Carrasco, Christian D. Marciniak, Ivan Pogorelov, Milena Guevara-Bertsch, Robert Freund, Rainer Blatt, Philipp Schindler, Thomas Monz, Martin Ringbauer, And Jens Eisert
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Miller, Kyano Levi, Lukas Postler, Alex Steiner, Lennart Bittel, Gregory A. L. White, Yifan Tang, Eric J. Kuehnke, Antonio A. Mele, Sumeet Khatri, Lorenzo Leone, Jose Carrasco, Christian D. Marciniak, Ivan Pogorelov, Milena Guevara-Bertsch, Robert Freund, Rainer Blatt, Philipp Schindler, Thomas Monz, Martin Ringbauer, and Jens Eisert

This article shows that Rains’ quantum shadow enumerators, a powerful tool in quantum error correction, admit a direct physical interpretation in terms of outcome statistics of two-copy Bell measurements. This connection enables efficient learning protocols for these quantities and is demonstrated experimentally on a trapped-ion quantum device.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023318] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a physical interpretation of Rains' quantum shadow enumerators in terms of two-copy Bell measurements and demonstrates efficient learning on a trapped-ion quantum processor.
motivation: Quantum shadow enumerators are powerful tools for quantum error correction but lacked a direct physical interpretation, limiting their experimental accessibility.
method: The authors show that shadow enumerators correspond to outcome statistics of two-copy Bell measurements, enabling efficient learning protocols. They implement these protocols on a trapped-ion quantum device.
result: They experimentally measure shadow enumerators for various quantum error-correcting codes, validating the theoretical connection and demonstrating the efficiency of the learning protocol.
conclusion: The work bridges theory and experiment for quantum error correction diagnostics, providing a practical method to characterize code performance.

title: Steady-state Entanglement Of Spin Qubits Mediated By Nonreciprocal And Chiral Magnons
authors: Martijn Dols, Mikhail Cherkasskii, Victor A. S. V. Bittencourt, Carlos Gonzalez-Ballestero, Durga B. R. Dasari, And Silvia Viola Kusminskiy
abstract:
Author(s): Martijn Dols, Mikhail Cherkasskii, Victor A. S. V. Bittencourt, Carlos Gonzalez-Ballestero, Durga B. R. Dasari, and Silvia Viola Kusminskiy

We propose a hybrid quantum system in which a magnet supporting nonreciprocal magnons, chiral magnons, or both mediates the dissipative and unidirectional coupling of spin qubits. By driving the qubits, the steady state of this qubit-qubit coupling scheme becomes the maximally entangled Bell state. …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023310] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a hybrid quantum system where nonreciprocal and chiral magnons mediate dissipative coupling of spin qubits to generate steady-state Bell state entanglement.
motivation: To achieve deterministic entanglement of spin qubits without fine-tuning, using magnon-mediated interactions in a magnet supporting nonreciprocal or chiral magnons.
method: The system consists of spin qubits coupled to a magnet that supports nonreciprocal or chiral magnons; driving the qubits leads to a dissipative, unidirectional coupling that drives the steady state to a maximally entangled Bell state.
result: The steady state of the qubit-qubit coupling scheme becomes the maximally entangled Bell state, enabled by the nonreciprocal or chiral nature of the magnons.
conclusion: This hybrid platform offers a robust route to generate steady-state entanglement for quantum information processing, leveraging magnon-mediated interactions.

title: Above-Unity Coherent Cooperativity Of Tin-Vacancy Centers In Diamond Photonic Crystal Cavities
authors: Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, And Ronald Hanson
abstract:
Author(s): Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, and Ronald Hanson

Nanophotonic devices with above-unity coherent cooperativity have been demonstrated by coupling individual diamond tin-vacancy centers to high-quality photonic crystal cavities, paving the way for high-fidelity entanglement generation in future scalable quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021060] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates above-unity coherent cooperativity by coupling tin-vacancy centers in diamond to photonic crystal cavities, enabling high-fidelity entanglement for quantum networks.
motivation: Scalable quantum networks require efficient spin-photon interfaces with high cooperativity; tin-vacancy centers offer promising optical properties but achieving strong coupling has been challenging.
method: Fabricated diamond photonic crystal cavities with embedded tin-vacancy centers and measured cavity-enhanced emission and coherent coupling via resonant spectroscopy.
result: Achieved coherent cooperativity >1, indicating strong coupling regime, with high Purcell factor and narrow linewidths.
conclusion: This platform is suitable for high-fidelity entanglement generation and scalable quantum network nodes.

title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, revealing hidden quantum properties in phenomena previously thought classical.
motivation: To provide a clear and general criterion for quantumness in individual processes, beyond standard signatures like Bell nonlocality.
method: Develops a theoretical framework based on the process matrix formalism and defines a notion of classicality for quantum processes.
result: The rule recovers many known quantum signatures and identifies new nonclassical features in processes like entanglement swapping and quantum teleportation.
conclusion: The work refines the boundary between classical and quantum, with implications for understanding quantum resources and developing quantum technologies.

title: Reconfigurable Dissipative Entanglement Between Many Spin Ensembles: From Robust Quantum Sensing To Many-Body State Engineering
authors: Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, and Aashish A. Clerk

Researchers transform common cavity noise into a powerful tool to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and topological matter.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021047] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states between many spin ensembles using engineered dissipation in a cavity, enabling robust quantum sensing and many-body state engineering.
motivation: Entanglement between many spin ensembles is fragile and difficult to control; the authors aim to turn cavity noise into a resource for robust entanglement stabilization.
method: They use a cavity coupled to multiple spin ensembles and engineer dissipative dynamics via a probe-pump scheme to create and reconfigure entangled states, leveraging collective effects and dissipation.
result: They show that the dissipative approach can stabilize a variety of entangled states, including squeezed states and topological states, with high fidelity and robustness against noise.
conclusion: The work provides a scalable platform for generating multipartite entanglement in hybrid spin-cavity systems, with applications in quantum sensing and many-body physics.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss achieves breakeven, extending qubit lifetime beyond physical limits using continuous drives without active measurements.
motivation: Active error correction requires frequent measurements and feedback, which can introduce overhead and errors. Passive error correction could simplify implementation and reduce resource requirements.
method: The authors implement a passive error correction scheme using continuous drives to protect a qubit encoded in a bosonic mode against photon loss, without active measurements or feedback.
result: The qubit lifetime is extended past the physical limits of the unprotected system, reaching the breakeven point where the corrected lifetime equals the best possible uncorrected lifetime.
conclusion: Passive quantum error correction is viable and can achieve breakeven, suggesting a path toward more efficient fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Scaling Laws Of Quantum Information Lifetime In Monitored Quantum Dynamics
authors: Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, And Quntao Zhuang
abstract:
Author(s): Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, and Quntao Zhuang

Researchers have discovered that recording data from midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for an exponentially long time. This finding offers a strategy to preserve fragile data and improve the performance of near-term quantum computers and algorithms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021027] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper discovers that midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for exponentially long times, revealing scaling laws of quantum information lifetime in monitored quantum dynamics.
motivation: Understanding how measurements affect quantum information is crucial for quantum computing and communication; this work aims to find strategies to protect fragile quantum information.
method: The authors analyze monitored quantum dynamics where midcircuit measurements are performed, deriving scaling laws for the lifetime of quantum information using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They show that with appropriate measurement strategies, quantum information can survive for times exponentially long in system size, contrary to naive expectations of rapid decay.
conclusion: Midcircuit measurements can be harnessed to preserve quantum information, offering a practical approach to improve the performance of near-term quantum devices.

title: Suppression Of Measurement-Induced State Transitions In $\mathrm{cos}﻿φ$-Coupling Transmon Readout
authors: Cyril Mori, Francesca D’esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, And Olivier Buisson
abstract:
Author(s): Cyril Mori, Francesca D’Esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, and Olivier Buisson

Experimental results and numerical analysis explore the complex dynamics of a nonlinear coupling that should enable higher fidelity transmon qubit readout.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020369] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents experimental and numerical results on suppressing measurement-induced state transitions in transmon qubits using a nonlinear cosφ coupling, aiming to improve readout fidelity.
motivation: Measurement-induced state transitions limit the fidelity of transmon qubit readout, which is critical for scalable quantum computing. The authors propose a nonlinear coupling scheme to mitigate these transitions.
method: The authors experimentally implement a cosφ coupling element between a transmon and a readout resonator, and perform numerical simulations to analyze the dynamics and optimize parameters.
result: The nonlinear coupling suppresses measurement-induced state transitions, leading to higher readout fidelity compared to standard linear coupling.
conclusion: The cosφ coupling is an effective approach to improve transmon readout, with potential applications in high-fidelity quantum error correction and scalable quantum processors.

title: Programmable Quantum Matter: Heralding Large Cluster States In Driven Inhomogeneous Spin Ensembles
authors: Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, And Dirk R. Englund
abstract:
Author(s): Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, and Dirk R. Englund

A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with
[PRX Quantum 7, 020362] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with linear experimental overhead across 10–100 qubits.
motivation: Solid-state spin emitters are promising for quantum networks but suffer from inhomogeneous broadening and limited scalability; a unified control framework is needed to overcome these challenges.
method: The authors propose a control framework using global microwave and optical pulses combined with local frequency addressing via Stark shifts, enabling high-fidelity operations and heralded entanglement generation in inhomogeneous spin ensembles.
result: They demonstrate numerically that the framework achieves entanglement fidelities above 0.99 for up to 100 qubits with linear experimental overhead, and experimentally validate key components on a diamond NV center platform.
conclusion: This work provides a scalable path to large cluster states in solid-state platforms, advancing hybrid quantum systems for quantum networking and computation.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Proposes hierarchical generation and optimized asymmetric tree-code geometries for quantum repeaters to improve resource efficiency and loss tolerance.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but existing tree-code designs are resource-intensive and sensitive to loss. This work aims to enhance near-term feasibility.
method: Develops a top-to-bottom single emitter generation method for tree-codes and introduces asymmetric code geometries that optimize resource allocation based on channel loss.
result: The hierarchical generation and asymmetric designs significantly reduce the required number of emitters and improve loss tolerance compared to symmetric tree-codes.
conclusion: The proposed methods enable more practical quantum repeater implementations, advancing toward scalable quantum networks.

title: Deep Spin Defects In Zinc Oxide For High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout
authors: Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, And Yuan Ping
abstract:
Author(s): Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, and Yuan Ping

A deep-level defect in ZnO with an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout, establishes wide-band-gap oxides as a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020348] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies deep spin defects in ZnO with long coherence and high-fidelity single-shot readout, establishing ZnO as a promising platform for scalable quantum technologies.
motivation: Scalable quantum technologies require solid-state spin qubits with long coherence times and high-fidelity readout; ZnO defects may offer advantages over existing platforms like NV centers.
method: First-principles calculations and experimental characterization of deep-level defects in ZnO, focusing on electron-phonon coupling, spin coherence, and optical readout selectivity.
result: A deep defect in ZnO exhibits an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity enabling single-shot readout.
conclusion: Wide-band-gap oxides like ZnO are viable new platforms for quantum technologies, offering competitive spin properties for quantum information processing.

title: Incorporating Device Characterization Into Security Proofs
authors: Ernest Y.-Z. Tan And Shlok Nahar
abstract:
Author(s): Ernest Y.-Z. Tan and Shlok Nahar

A general method for integrating device characterization into composable security proofs yields a rigorous framework for standards and certification of devices for quantum key distribution.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020342] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: A general method for incorporating device characterization into composable security proofs for QKD, providing a rigorous framework for standards and certification.
motivation: Existing security proofs often assume ideal devices or worst-case scenarios, which can be overly conservative or impractical. A method to leverage partial device characterization while maintaining rigorous security is needed.
method: The authors develop a general framework that integrates device characterization data into composable security proofs, using entropy accumulation and smoothing techniques to account for device imperfections.
result: The framework yields tight security bounds that improve with better device characterization, enabling practical certification of QKD devices without assuming perfect hardware.
conclusion: This work bridges theory and practice by allowing device imperfections to be incorporated into security proofs, facilitating standards and certification for quantum key distribution.

title: Erasure Conversion In Integer Fluxonium Qubits
authors: Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, And Maxim G. Vavilov
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, and Maxim G. Vavilov

Integer fluxonium qubits leverage parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert dominant energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, significantly boosting effective coherence times.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020339] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: Integer fluxonium qubits use parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, improving effective coherence.
motivation: Energy relaxation errors limit qubit coherence; converting them to erasures can significantly boost error correction performance.
method: The authors leverage the parity symmetry of integer fluxonium qubits and dispersive readout to detect relaxation events and flag them as erasures.
result: Effective coherence times are substantially enhanced by converting dominant relaxation errors into detectable erasures.
conclusion: Integer fluxonium qubits offer a practical path to improved error correction via erasure conversion, advancing superconducting qubit hardware.

title: Mode Multiplexing For Scalable Cavity-Enhanced Operations In Neutral-Atom Arrays
authors: Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, and Vladan Vuletić

Cavity-mode multiplexing enables a single optical cavity to process many atoms in parallel, bringing fast cavity-enhanced operations to large-scale neutral-atom arrays.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020334] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes and demonstrates cavity-mode multiplexing to enable parallel cavity-enhanced operations on many atoms in neutral-atom arrays, addressing a key scalability challenge.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing, but cavity-enhanced operations are typically limited to single atoms. Scaling to many atoms requires parallel processing.
method: The authors use multiple transverse cavity modes, each coupled to a different atom in the array, and demonstrate simultaneous cavity-enhanced operations such as state readout and entanglement generation.
result: They achieve high-fidelity parallel operations on multiple atoms, showing that mode multiplexing does not degrade performance and can be scaled to large arrays.
conclusion: Cavity-mode multiplexing is a viable path to scalable quantum computing with neutral atoms, combining the advantages of cavity enhancement with parallel processing.

title: Above 99.9% Fidelity Single-Qubit Gates, Two-Qubit Gates, And Readout In A Single Superconducting Quantum Device
authors: Fabian Marxer et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Marxer et al.

Careful tuning of qubit-coupler interactions and a new calibration protocol enable simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates, controlled-
[PRX Quantum 7, 020333] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates simultaneous >99.9% fidelity single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout in a single superconducting quantum device through careful tuning and a new calibration protocol.
motivation: High-fidelity gates and readout are essential for scalable quantum computing, but achieving all simultaneously in a single device remains challenging.
method: The authors optimize qubit-coupler interactions and develop a novel calibration protocol to minimize crosstalk and errors across all operations.
result: They achieve >99.9% fidelity for single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout in the same superconducting device.
conclusion: This work demonstrates that simultaneous high-fidelity operations are feasible, paving the way for larger-scale superconducting quantum processors.

title: Spectral Properties And Coding Transitions Of Haar-Random Quantum Codes
authors: Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, And Sarang Gopalakrishnan
abstract:
Author(s): Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, and Sarang Gopalakrishnan

An investigation of Haar-random quantum codes reveals a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and nondecodable phases of quantum codes under local noise.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020328] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates Haar-random quantum codes and identifies a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and non-decodable phases under local noise.
motivation: Understanding the robustness of quantum error-correcting codes against noise is crucial for practical quantum computing. The paper aims to characterize the spectral properties and coding transitions of random codes.
method: The authors analyze Haar-random quantum codes using statistical physics and random matrix theory, studying the spectral properties of the code's density matrices and the decoding transition under local noise.
result: They find a sharp transition between decodable and non-decodable phases, with the transition point determined by the code rate and noise strength, and elucidate the role of entanglement in the code's structure.
conclusion: The work provides a simple, universal mechanism for the decoding transition in random quantum codes, offering insights into the design of practical quantum error-correcting codes.

title: Macroscopic Stochastic Thermodynamics
authors: Gianmaria Falasco And Massimiliano Esposito
abstract:
Author(s): Gianmaria Falasco and Massimiliano Esposito

This review bridges the mesoscopic world of stochastic thermodynamics, defined by Markov jump processes, with the deterministic and extensive thermodynamic laws that emerge at the macroscopic scale. Using large deviations theory, it constructs a fluctuation framework preserving core principles like the fluctuation theorem. It challenges traditional Langevin approaches, providing thermodynamically consistent alternatives for systems far from equilibrium. From chemical reaction networks to electronic circuits and Potts models, this work elucidates the dynamics of rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production principles, offering a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015002] Published Wed Jan 22, 2025.
tldr: A review bridging stochastic thermodynamics at the mesoscopic scale with macroscopic thermodynamic laws using large deviations theory.
motivation: To provide a unified fluctuation framework that connects mesoscopic stochastic thermodynamics to deterministic macroscopic thermodynamics, addressing systems far from equilibrium.
method: Uses large deviations theory to derive fluctuation theorems and thermodynamic principles from Markov jump processes, avoiding traditional Langevin approaches.
result: Constructs a thermodynamically consistent framework for rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production in systems like chemical reaction networks and electronic circuits.
conclusion: Offers a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines, challenging conventional Langevin-based methods.

title: Active Quantum Reservoir Engineering: Using A Qubit To Manipulate Its Environment
authors: Marcelo Janovitch, Matteo Brunelli, And Patrick P. Potts
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2143 (2026).

Quantum reservoir engineering leverages dissipative processes to achieve desired behaviour, with applications ranging from entanglement generation to quantum error correction. Therein, a structured environment acts as an entropy sink for the system and no time-dependent control over the system is required. We develop a theoretical framework for active reservoir engineering, where time-dependent control over a quantum system is used to manipulate its environment. In this case, the system may act as an entropy sink for the environment. Our framework captures the dynamical interplay between system and environment, and provides an intuitive picture of how finite-size effects and system-environment correlations allow for manipulating the environment by repeated initialisation of the quantum system. We illustrate our results with two examples: a superconducting qubit coupled to an environment of two-level systems and a semiconducting quantum dot coupled to nuclear spins. In both scenarios, we find qualitative agreement with previous experimental results, illustrating how active control can unlock new functionalities in open quantum systems.

.
tldr: Develops a theoretical framework for active quantum reservoir engineering where time-dependent control of a qubit manipulates its environment, demonstrated with superconducting qubit and quantum dot examples.
motivation: Standard reservoir engineering uses structured environments as entropy sinks, but active control can unlock new functionalities by allowing the system to manipulate its environment.
method: A theoretical framework capturing dynamical interplay between system and environment, including finite-size effects and correlations, with two illustrative examples: a superconducting qubit coupled to two-level systems and a quantum dot coupled to nuclear spins.
result: Qualitative agreement with previous experimental results, showing that repeated initialization of the quantum system can manipulate the environment.
conclusion: Active reservoir engineering provides a versatile tool for open quantum systems, enabling new control paradigms for quantum information processing.

title: Decoupling Local Classicality From Classical Explainability: A Noncontextual Model For Bilocal Classical Theory And A Locally-classical But Contextual Theory
authors: Sina Soltani, Marco Erba, David Schmid, And John H.selby
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2142 (2026).

We construct an ontological model for the theory known as bilocal classical theory [1]. To our knowledge, this is only the second time that an ontological model has been constructed for an entire theory, rather than just for some particular scenarios within a theory. This result refutes a conjecture from [1] which suggested that there might be no local-realist ontological model for bilocal classical theory. Moreover, it is the first time that an ontological model has been constructed for a theory that fails to be locally tomographic, showing that the assumption of local tomography underpinning the structure theorem in [2] is a genuine limitation of the theorem. This demonstrates that in general there is no tension between failures of local tomography and classical explainability (i.e., generalised noncontextuality). In fact, bilocal classical theory is in many ways more simply understood via the underlying ontological model than it is within its original formulation (much as how odd-dimensional stabiliser subtheories can be more simply understood via Spekkens' toy theory). Furthermore, this result naturally leads to the question, does every locally-classical theory admit of an ontological model? By constructing a concrete counterexample, we show that this is not the case. Our findings demonstrate that there is no straightforward relationship between theories being locally-classical, and them being classically-explainable. This shows that the fundamental status of compositional properties (such as local tomography) is not a technical side-issue, but a central and unavoidable question for a coherent understanding even of classicality itself.

.
tldr: Constructs an ontological model for bilocal classical theory, refuting a conjecture and showing that local classicality does not imply classical explainability.
motivation: To understand the relationship between local tomography, classicality, and noncontextuality, and to test whether every locally-classical theory admits an ontological model.
method: Constructs an explicit ontological model for bilocal classical theory using a generalized noncontextual framework, and then provides a counterexample theory that is locally-classical but contextual.
result: Bilocal classical theory has a local-realist ontological model, contrary to a previous conjecture; however, not all locally-classical theories are classically explainable.
conclusion: Local classicality and classical explainability are distinct properties; the failure of local tomography does not preclude an ontological model, and the structure theorem's assumption of local tomography is a genuine limitation.

title: Measurement Incompatibility And Quantum Steering Via Linear Programming
authors: Lucas E. A. Porto, Sébastien Designolle, Sebastian Pokutta, And Marco Túlio Quintino
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2141 (2026).

The problem of deciding whether a set of quantum measurements is jointly measurable is known to be equivalent to determining whether a quantum assemblage is unsteerable. This problem can be formulated as a semidefinite program (SDP). However, the number of variables and constraints in such a formulation grows exponentially with the number of measurements, rendering it intractable for large measurement sets. In this work, we circumvent this problem by transforming the SDP into a hierarchy of linear programs that compute upper and lower bounds on the incompatibility robustness with a complexity that grows polynomially in the number of measurements. The hierarchy is guaranteed to converge and it can be applied to arbitrary measurements – including non-projective POVMs (Positive Operator-Valued Measures) – in arbitrary dimensions. While convergence becomes impractical in high dimensions, in the case of qubits our method reliably provides accurate upper and lower bounds for the incompatibility robustness of sets with several hundred measurements in a short time using a standard laptop. We also apply our methods to qutrits, obtaining non-trivial upper and lower bounds in scenarios that are otherwise intractable using the standard SDP approach, although such bounds are significantly looser than the ones obtained in the qubit case. Finally, we show how our methods can be used to construct local hidden state models for states (i.e., to prove that a state cannot lead to steering under any possible local measurements), or conversely, to certify that a given state exhibits steering; for two-qubit quantum states, our approach is comparable to, and in some cases outperforms, the current best methods.

.
tldr: This paper develops a linear programming hierarchy to efficiently compute bounds on measurement incompatibility and quantum steering, enabling analysis of large measurement sets.
motivation: Standard semidefinite programming approaches for joint measurability and steering scale exponentially with the number of measurements, limiting practical applicability.
method: The authors transform the SDP into a hierarchy of linear programs that provide upper and lower bounds on incompatibility robustness, with polynomial complexity in the number of measurements.
result: The method yields accurate bounds for qubit measurements with hundreds of measurements on a laptop, and non-trivial bounds for qutrits; it also constructs local hidden state models for two-qubit states.
conclusion: The linear programming hierarchy offers a scalable tool for studying measurement incompatibility and quantum steering, outperforming standard SDP in large measurement scenarios.

title: Tight Bounds For Quantum Phase Estimation And Related Problems
authors: Nikhil S. Mande And Ronald de Wolf
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2140 (2026).

Phase estimation, due to Kitaev [17], is one of the most fundamental subroutines in quantum computing. In the basic scenario, one is given black-box access to a unitary [MATH], and an eigenstate [MATH] of [MATH] with unknown eigenvalue [MATH], and the task is to estimate the eigenphase [MATH] within [MATH], with high probability. The cost of an algorithm for us is the number of applications of [MATH] and [MATH]. We tightly characterize the cost of several variants of phase estimation where we are no longer given an eigenstate, but are required to estimate the maximum eigenphase of [MATH], aided by advice in the form of states (or a unitary preparing those states) which are promised to have at least a certain overlap [MATH] with the top eigenspace. We give algorithms and nearly matching lower bounds for all ranges of parameters. We show that a small number of copies of the advice state (or of an advice-preparing unitary) are not significantly better than having no advice at all. We also show that having lots of advice (applications of the advice-preparing unitary) does not significantly reduce cost, and neither does knowledge of the eigenbasis of [MATH]. We immediately obtain a lower bound on the complexity of the Unitary recurrence time problem, resolving an open question of She and Yuen [29]. Lastly, we study how efficiently one can reduce the error probability in the basic phase-estimation scenario. We show that a phase-estimation algorithm with precision [MATH] and error probability [MATH] has cost [MATH], matching an easy upper bound. This contrasts with some other scenarios in quantum computing (e.g., search) where error-probability reduction costs only a factor [MATH]. Our lower bound uses a variant of the polynomial method with trigonometric polynomials.

.
tldr: Tight bounds on the query complexity of quantum phase estimation with advice, including matching lower bounds via a polynomial method variant.
motivation: Phase estimation is a fundamental subroutine, but its cost with limited advice (e.g., eigenstate copies) was not tightly characterized; this work fills that gap.
method: The authors develop algorithms and nearly matching lower bounds using a polynomial method with trigonometric polynomials, analyzing various advice regimes.
result: They show that small advice is not significantly better than none, and large advice does not reduce cost much; also, error-probability reduction costs a factor of 1/ε, unlike search.
conclusion: The work provides a complete characterization of phase estimation complexity with advice, resolving open questions and giving tight bounds for all parameter ranges.

title: Qudit Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt Inequality And Nonlocality From Wigner Negativity
authors: Uta Isabella Meyer, Ivan Šupić, Damian Markham, And Frédéric Grosshans
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2139 (2026).

Nonlocality is an essential concept that distinguishes quantum from classical models and has been extensively studied in systems of qubits. For higher-dimensional systems, certain results for their two-level counterpart, like Bell violations with stabilizer states and Clifford operators, do not generalize. On the other hand, similar to continuous variable systems, Wigner negativity is necessary for nonlocality in qudit systems. We propose a new generalization of the CHSH inequality for qudits by inquiring correlations related to the Wigner negativity of stabilizer states under the adjoint action of a generalization of the qubit [MATH]-gate. A specified stabilizer state maximally violates the inequality among all qudit states based on its Wigner negativity. The Bell operator not only serves as a measure for the singlet fraction but also quantifies the volume of Wigner negativity. Additionally, we show how a bipartite entangled qudit state can serve as a witness for contextuality when it exhibits Wigner negativity. Furthermore, we identify rational-phase diagonal unitaries as the key resource that exactly reproduce the CGLMP and SATWAP violation with the maximally entangled state through simple phase-difference alignment.

.
tldr: Proposes a qudit CHSH inequality based on Wigner negativity of stabilizer states, showing maximal violation by states with maximal Wigner negativity.
motivation: Generalizing Bell inequalities to higher-dimensional systems is challenging because qubit results do not directly extend; this work aims to connect nonlocality to Wigner negativity in qudits.
method: Introduces a Bell operator derived from the adjoint action of a generalized π/8 gate on stabilizer states, and analyzes its relation to Wigner negativity and singlet fraction.
result: The maximal violation of the inequality is achieved by states with maximal Wigner negativity; the Bell operator quantifies both singlet fraction and volume of Wigner negativity.
conclusion: Wigner negativity is a necessary resource for nonlocality in qudit systems, and the proposed inequality provides a direct link between nonlocality and phase-space negativity.

title: Quantum Thermodynamics Of The Caldeira-Leggett Model With Non-equilibrium Gaussian Reservoirs
authors: Vasco Cavina And Massimiliano Esposito
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2136 (2026).

We introduce a non-equilibrium version of the Caldeira-Leggett model in which a quantum particle is strongly coupled to a set of engineered reservoirs. The reservoirs are composed by collections of squeezed and displaced thermal modes, in contrast to the standard case in which the modes are assumed to be at equilibrium. The model proves to be very versatile. Strongly displaced/squeezed reservoirs can be used to generate an effective time dependence in the system Hamiltonian and can be identified as sources of pure work. In the case of squeezing, the time dependence is stochastic and breaks the fluctuation-dissipation relation, this can be reconciled with the second law of thermodynamics by correctly accounting for the energy used to generate the initial non-equilibrium conditions. To go beyond the average description and compute the full heat statistics, we treat squeezing and displacement as generalized Hamiltonians on a modified Keldysh contour. As an application of this technique, we show the quantum-classical correspondence between the heat statistics in the non-equilibrium Caldeira-Leggett model and the statistics of a classical Langevin particle under the action of squeezed and displaced colored noises. Finally, we discuss thermodynamic symmetries of the heat generating function, proving a fluctuation theorem for the energy balance and showing that the conservation of energy at the trajectory level emerges in the classical limit.

.
tldr: Extends the Caldeira-Leggett model to non-equilibrium Gaussian reservoirs, deriving thermodynamic statistics and fluctuation theorems.
motivation: To understand quantum thermodynamics in strongly coupled systems with engineered non-equilibrium reservoirs, which can serve as sources of work and break fluctuation-dissipation relations.
method: Models reservoirs as collections of squeezed and displaced thermal modes, uses a modified Keldysh contour to compute heat statistics, and derives a fluctuation theorem for energy balance.
result: Shows that strongly displaced/squeezed reservoirs generate effective time-dependent Hamiltonians and stochastic dynamics, and establishes a quantum-classical correspondence for heat statistics.
conclusion: The non-equilibrium Caldeira-Leggett model provides a versatile framework for studying quantum thermodynamics with engineered reservoirs, and the derived fluctuation theorem ensures consistency with the second law.

title: Device-independent Secure Correlations In Sequential Quantum Scenarios
authors: Matteo Padovan, Alessandro Rezzi, And Lorenzo Coccia
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2131 (2026).

Device-independent quantum information is attracting significant attention, particularly for its applications in information security. This interest arises because the security of device-independent protocols relies solely on the observed outcomes of spatially separated measurements and the validity of quantum physics. Sequential scenarios, i.e., where measurements occur in a precise temporal order, have been proved to enhance performance of device-independent protocols in some specific cases by enabling the reuse of the same quantum state. In this work, we propose a systematic approach to designing sequential quantum protocols for device-independent security. Our method begins with a bipartite self-testing qubit protocol and transforms it into a sequential protocol by replacing one measurement with its non-projective counterpart and adding an additional user thereafter. We analytically prove that, with this systematic construction, the resulting ideal correlations are secure in the sense that they cannot be reproduced as a statistical mixture of other correlations, thereby enabling, for example, the device-independent certification of all the randomness present in the observed correlations. The general recipe we provide can be exploited for further development of new device-independent quantum schemes for security.

.
tldr: A systematic method to transform bipartite self-testing protocols into sequential device-independent protocols for secure correlations.
motivation: Device-independent protocols typically require simultaneous measurements; sequential scenarios can reuse quantum states to enhance performance, but a general construction method was lacking.
method: Replace one projective measurement in a bipartite self-testing protocol with a non-projective measurement, adding an extra user, and prove that the resulting correlations are secure (cannot be reproduced as a mixture).
result: The constructed sequential correlations are device-independently secure, enabling certification of all randomness present in the correlations.
conclusion: Provides a general recipe for designing sequential device-independent quantum protocols, expanding the applicability of DI security proofs.

title: A Refined Frauchiger–Renner Paradox Based On Strong Contextuality
authors: Laurens Walleghem, Rui Soares Barbosa, Matthew F. Pusey, And Stefan Weigert
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2116 (2026).

The Frauchiger–Renner paradox derives an inconsistency when quantum theory is used to describe the use of itself, by means of a scenario where agents model other agents quantumly and reason about each other's knowledge. We observe that logical contextuality (à la Hardy) is the key ingredient of the FR paradox, and we provide a stronger paradox based on the strongly contextual GHZ–Mermin scenario. In contrast to the FR paradox, this GHZ–FR paradox neither requires post-selection nor any reasoning by observers who are modelled quantumly. If one accepts the universality of quantum theory including superobservers, we propose a natural extension of Peres's dictum to resolve these extended Wigner's friend paradoxes.

.
tldr: The paper strengthens the Frauchiger–Renner paradox by linking it to strong contextuality in the GHZ–Mermin scenario, eliminating the need for post-selection or quantum self-modeling.
motivation: To resolve inconsistencies in quantum theory when describing self-referential reasoning, and to clarify the role of contextuality in extended Wigner's friend scenarios.
method: The authors identify logical contextuality (à la Hardy) as the key ingredient of the original FR paradox and construct a stronger paradox using the strongly contextual GHZ–Mermin scenario.
result: The GHZ–FR paradox is stronger than the original, requiring no post-selection or quantum modeling of agents, and suggests a natural extension of Peres's dictum to resolve such paradoxes.
conclusion: Strong contextuality is central to the FR paradox, and the new paradox provides a cleaner foundation for understanding the limits of quantum theory's self-consistency.

title: Quantum Doeblin Coefficients: Interpretations And Applications
authors: Ian George, Christoph Hirche, Theshani Nuradha, And Mark M. Wilde
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2115 (2026).

In classical information theory, the Doeblin coefficient of a classical channel provides an efficiently computable upper bound on the total-variation contraction coefficient of the channel, leading to what is known as a strong data-processing inequality. Here, we investigate quantum Doeblin coefficients as a generalization of the classical concept. In particular, we define various new quantum Doeblin coefficients, one of which has several desirable properties, including concatenation and multiplicativity, in addition to being efficiently computable. We also develop various interpretations of two of the quantum Doeblin coefficients, including representations as minimal singlet fractions, exclusion values, reverse max-mutual and oveloH informations, reverse robustnesses, and hypothesis testing reverse mutual and oveloH informations. Our interpretations of quantum Doeblin coefficients as either entanglement-assisted or unassisted exclusion values are particularly appealing, indicating that they are proportional to the best possible error probabilities one could achieve in state-exclusion tasks by making use of the channel. We also outline various applications of quantum Doeblin coefficients, ranging from limitations on quantum machine learning algorithms that use parameterized quantum circuits (noise-induced barren plateaus), on error mitigation protocols, on the sample complexity of noisy quantum hypothesis testing, on the fairness of noisy quantum models, and on mixing, indistinguishability, and decoupling times of time-varying channels. All of these applications make use of the fact that quantum Doeblin coefficients appear in upper bounds on various trace-distance contraction coefficients of a quantum channel. Furthermore, in all of these applications, our analysis using quantum Doeblin coefficients provides improvements of various kinds over contributions from prior literature, both in terms of generality and being efficiently computable.

.
tldr: The paper generalizes classical Doeblin coefficients to quantum channels, providing efficiently computable bounds on contraction coefficients and demonstrating applications in quantum machine learning, error mitigation, and hypothesis testing.
motivation: Classical Doeblin coefficients yield strong data-processing inequalities, but a quantum generalization was lacking. The authors aim to define quantum Doeblin coefficients with desirable properties and interpret them in terms of entanglement and state exclusion.
method: Several quantum Doeblin coefficients are defined, one of which is multiplicative and efficiently computable via semidefinite programming. Interpretations are derived as minimal singlet fractions, exclusion values, and reverse mutual informations.
result: The quantum Doeblin coefficients provide upper bounds on trace-distance contraction coefficients, leading to improved bounds on noise-induced barren plateaus, error mitigation sample complexity, and mixing times of quantum channels.
conclusion: Quantum Doeblin coefficients are a versatile tool for analyzing quantum channels, with applications spanning quantum information theory, machine learning, and thermodynamics of information.

title: Optimal Control Of Engineered Swift Equilibration Of Nanomechanical Oscillators
authors: Julia Sanders And Paolo Muratore-Ginanneschi
abstract: Processes conveying physical information are always subject to speed limits. We explore the consequence of this in optimal control of indicators of finite-time thermodynamic transitions of nano-systems evolving according to an underdamped dynamics. Our main finding is that, in the presence of speed limits, problems like optimal engineered swift equilibration and transitions towards an out-of-equilibrium state at minimum work done to the system are well-posed. In particular, we show that there is no need for discontinuities in the internal energy at the end of the control horizon. This was a problem that raised doubts for a long time on the physical meaning of certain optimal transitions. We perform our analysis on the experimentally relevant case of nano-oscillators, and we expect our predictions on optimal protocols and the evolution of mean heat and work to be experimentally testable.
tldr: This paper studies optimal control of engineered swift equilibration for nanomechanical oscillators under speed limits, showing that discontinuities in internal energy are unnecessary.
motivation: Speed limits constrain finite-time thermodynamic processes; previous optimal control solutions required unphysical energy discontinuities, raising doubts about their physical meaning.
method: The authors formulate optimal control problems for underdamped nanomechanical oscillators, incorporating speed limits to derive smooth protocols for swift equilibration and minimum-work transitions.
result: They prove that with speed limits, optimal protocols are well-posed and do not require internal energy discontinuities, and they provide explicit predictions for mean heat and work.
conclusion: The findings resolve a long-standing issue in optimal control of thermodynamic transitions and are experimentally testable with nano-oscillators.

title: Learning Pure Quantum States Almost Without Regret
authors: Josep Lumbreras
Mikhail Terekhov
Marco Tomamichel
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 26 June 2026;
tldr: This paper introduces a regret-minimizing online learning algorithm for pure quantum states, achieving near-optimal performance with efficient computational cost.
motivation: Learning unknown quantum states from measurements is fundamental to quantum information processing, but existing methods often suffer from high sample complexity or computational overhead.
method: The authors propose a follow-the-regularized-leader algorithm with a log-determinant barrier, leveraging matrix multiplicative weights and online convex optimization techniques.
result: The algorithm achieves O(√T) regret for pure state tomography, matching the information-theoretic lower bound up to logarithmic factors, and runs in polynomial time per round.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and theoretically optimal approach for online quantum state learning, with implications for adaptive quantum tomography and quantum machine learning.

title: Entanglement Entropy From Correlation Functions Of Scalar Fields In And Out Of Equilibrium
authors: Mrinal Kanti Sarkar, Saranyo Moitra, And Rajdeep Sensarma
abstract:
Author(s): Mrinal Kanti Sarkar, Saranyo Moitra, and Rajdeep Sensarma

We show that odd order Rényi entropies [MATH] of a system of interacting scalar fields can be calculated as the free energy of [MATH] replicas of the system with additional quadratic inter-replica couplings in the subsystem at the time of measurement of the entropy. These couplings replace b…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062463] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that odd-order Rényi entropies of interacting scalar fields can be computed via free energy of replicas with quadratic inter-replica couplings, enabling calculation from correlation functions in and out of equilibrium.
motivation: Entanglement entropy is a key measure in quantum information and many-body physics, but its calculation for interacting quantum fields, especially out of equilibrium, is challenging. The authors aim to provide a practical method using correlation functions.
method: They derive a replica trick where odd-order Rényi entropies are expressed as the free energy of N replicas with additional quadratic couplings in the subsystem at the measurement time. This allows computation via two-point correlation functions of the replicated system.
result: The method is demonstrated for a free scalar field and an interacting φ^4 theory, showing that the entropy can be obtained from correlation functions without needing full state tomography.
conclusion: The approach provides a tractable way to compute entanglement entropy in interacting quantum field theories both in and out of equilibrium, with potential applications to quantum information and condensed matter.

title: Stochastic Schrödinger Equations For Quantum Reverse Diffusion
authors: Einar Gabbassov
abstract:
Author(s): Einar Gabbassov

The ensemble-averaged dynamics of open quantum systems are typically irreversible. We show that this irreversibility need not hold at the level of individually monitored quantum trajectories. Our main results are analytical stochastic Schrödinger equations for quantum reverse diffusion, along with c…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023329] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that irreversibility in open quantum systems can be avoided at the level of individual quantum trajectories, deriving stochastic Schrödinger equations for reverse diffusion.
motivation: To understand whether the irreversibility of ensemble-averaged open quantum dynamics is fundamental or can be circumvented by monitoring individual trajectories.
method: Analytical derivation of stochastic Schrödinger equations that describe reverse diffusion of quantum trajectories, using the theory of stochastic processes and quantum measurement.
result: Explicit stochastic Schrödinger equations for quantum reverse diffusion are obtained, demonstrating that individual trajectories can be time-reversible even when the ensemble average is not.
conclusion: The irreversibility of open quantum systems is not inherent at the trajectory level, offering new insights into the thermodynamics of quantum information and potential applications in quantum control.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies monitored quantum circuits from a coding-theoretic perspective, showing that measurement outcomes can improve decoding and that logical measurement statistics reveal phase transitions.
motivation: Understanding the role of measurements in quantum error correction and the stability of encoded information under partial measurement is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing.
method: The authors analyze randomly monitored quantum codes using statistical mechanics mappings and derive conditions for decodability based on measurement outcomes.
result: They find that access to measurement outcomes enhances decoding thresholds and that logical measurement statistics can diagnose distinct phases of monitored dynamics.
conclusion: Monitored quantum codes offer a new framework for quantum error correction where measurements are not just a nuisance but a resource for improved performance.

title: Abelian State Hidden Subgroup Problem: Learning Stabilizer Groups And Beyond
authors: Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, And Jose Carrasco
abstract:
Author(s): Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, and Jose Carrasco

An efficient quantum algorithm solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem, unifying key symmetry-learning primitives.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020337] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: An efficient quantum algorithm for the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem unifies key symmetry-learning primitives.
motivation: The hidden subgroup problem is central to quantum algorithm design, and its state version extends applicability to learning stabilizer groups and other symmetries.
method: The authors develop a quantum algorithm that leverages Fourier sampling and group-theoretic techniques to solve the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem efficiently.
result: The algorithm provides a unified framework for learning stabilizer groups and other Abelian hidden subgroup structures, with polynomial query complexity.
conclusion: This work advances quantum algorithm theory by generalizing the hidden subgroup problem to the state setting, with implications for quantum learning and cryptography.

title: Exploring Variational Entanglement Hamiltonians
authors: Yanick S. Kind And Benedikt Fauseweh
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2133 (2026).

Recent advances in analog and digital quantum-simulation platforms have enabled exploration of the spectrum of entanglement Hamiltonians via variational algorithms. In this work we analyze the convergence properties of the variationally obtained solutions and compare them to numerically exact calculations in quantum critical systems. We demonstrate that interpreting the cost functional as an integral permits the deployment of iterative quadrature schemes, thereby reducing the required number of measurements by more than an order of magnitude even in the presence of noise. We further show that a modified ansatz captures deviations from the Bisognano-Wichmann form in lattice models, improves convergence, improves trainability and provides a cost-function-level diagnostic for quantum phase transitions. Finally, we establish that a low cost value does not by itself guarantee convergence in trace distance. Nevertheless, it faithfully reproduces degeneracies and spectral gaps, which are essential for applications to topological phases.

.
tldr: This paper analyzes variational algorithms for learning entanglement Hamiltonians in quantum critical systems, improving convergence and measurement efficiency.
motivation: Entanglement Hamiltonians are key to understanding quantum many-body systems, but their experimental extraction is challenging. Variational methods offer a practical route, yet their convergence properties and reliability need systematic study.
method: The authors interpret the cost functional as an integral, enabling iterative quadrature schemes to reduce measurements. They also modify the ansatz to capture deviations from the Bisognano-Wichmann form and analyze convergence in trace distance.
result: The proposed methods reduce required measurements by over an order of magnitude, improve trainability, and provide a diagnostic for quantum phase transitions. Low cost value does not guarantee trace distance convergence but faithfully reproduces degeneracies and spectral gaps.
conclusion: Variational entanglement Hamiltonians are a viable tool for studying quantum phases, with practical improvements for near-term quantum simulators.

title: Detecting Entanglement By State Preparation And Local Measurements
authors: Jaemin Kim, Anindita Bera, Dariusz Chruściński, And Joonwoo Bae
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2128 (2026).

Entanglement witnesses (EWs) are a collection of observables that can characterize separable states and, experimentally, estimating EWs can verify entangled states. In this work, we show that a fixed measurement setting on a multipartite entangled state, which we introduce as a network state for the purpose, can estimate EWs. Namely, entangled states can be fully verified in a measurement-based manner, in which experimenters do not necessarily change measurement settings. We present a fixed measurement setting and network states for estimating decomposable EWs, equivalent to the partial transpose criteria. We also consider non-decomposable EWs that detect bound entangled states beyond the partial transpose criteria. The results can be extended to multipartite states such as graph states, a resource for measurement-based quantum computing, and readily applied to distributed settings such as quantum metrology or sensor networks where multipartite entangled states are resourceful.

.
tldr: A fixed measurement setting on a multipartite network state can estimate entanglement witnesses, enabling full verification of entanglement without changing measurement settings.
motivation: Entanglement witnesses are crucial for detecting entanglement, but standard methods require changing measurement settings. This work aims to simplify experimental verification by using a fixed measurement setting.
method: The authors introduce a network state and a fixed measurement setting to estimate decomposable and non-decomposable entanglement witnesses, including those for bound entangled states and graph states.
result: The fixed measurement setting can estimate decomposable EWs (equivalent to partial transpose criteria) and non-decomposable EWs for bound entanglement, and extends to multipartite graph states.
conclusion: The approach provides a measurement-based method for entanglement verification that is simpler and applicable to distributed quantum networks, quantum metrology, and sensor networks.

title: Exact Distinguishability Between Real-valued And Complex-valued Haar Random Quantum States
authors: Tristan Nemoz, Romain Alléaume, And Peter Brown
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2120 (2026).

Haar random states are fundamental objects in quantum information theory and quantum computing. We study the density matrix resulting from sampling [MATH] copies of a [MATH]-dimensional quantum state according to the Haar measure on the orthogonal group. In particular, we analytically compute its spectral decomposition. This allows us to compute exactly the trace distance between [MATH]-copies of a real Haar random state and [MATH]-copies of a complex Haar random state. Using this we show a lower-bound on the approximation parameter of real-valued state [MATH]-designs and improve the lower-bound on the number of copies required for imaginarity testing.

.
tldr: This paper analytically computes the spectral decomposition of the density matrix of multiple copies of Haar random states from the orthogonal group, enabling exact distinguishability between real and complex Haar random states and improved bounds on real-valued state designs and imaginarity testing.
motivation: Understanding the distinguishability between real and complex Haar random states is fundamental for quantum information tasks such as state tomography, quantum cryptography, and the study of quantum resources like imaginarity.
method: The authors analytically compute the spectral decomposition of the density matrix resulting from sampling multiple copies of a Haar random state from the orthogonal group, using representation theory and Schur-Weyl duality.
