SignificanceHigh-energy electron beams are powerful tools for examining materials and biological systems, but it remains unclear how strongly they can interact with individual quantum systems in solids. Unlocking this interaction could enable electron-...
tldr: This paper explores the interaction between high-energy electron beams and solid-state spins (NV centers) for quantum sensing of electron beams.
motivation: Understanding how electron beams interact with individual quantum systems in solids could enable new sensing modalities for electron microscopy and beam characterization.
method: The authors theoretically and experimentally investigate the coupling between free electrons and NV centers in diamond, using spin-dependent fluorescence to detect electron-induced spin changes.
result: They demonstrate that electron beams can coherently manipulate NV center spins and achieve spin readout with high sensitivity, paving the way for quantum-enhanced electron microscopy.
conclusion: Solid-state spins can serve as sensitive quantum probes for electron beams, enabling new approaches to beam diagnostics and imaging with quantum-enhanced resolution.

title: A Context-aware Gate Set Tomography: Improving The Self-consistent Characterization Of Trapped-ion Universal Gate Sets By Leveraging non-Markovianity
authors: P. Viñas
A. Bermudez
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 26 June 2026;
tldr: A context-aware gate set tomography method that leverages non-Markovianity to improve self-consistent characterization of trapped-ion universal gate sets.
motivation: Standard gate set tomography assumes Markovian noise, but trapped-ion systems often exhibit non-Markovian effects that degrade characterization accuracy.
method: The authors extend gate set tomography to incorporate non-Markovian noise by using a context-aware framework that accounts for temporal correlations in the noise.
result: The method yields more accurate and self-consistent estimates of gate fidelities and error rates compared to standard tomography in the presence of non-Markovian noise.
conclusion: Leveraging non-Markovianity improves the reliability of quantum gate characterization, which is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing with trapped ions.

title: Design And Optimization Of Adaptive Diversity Schemes In Quantum Mimo Channels
authors: Shehbaz Tariq
Symeon Chatzinotas
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 24 June 2026;
tldr: This paper proposes and optimizes adaptive diversity schemes for quantum MIMO channels to improve communication reliability and capacity.
motivation: Quantum MIMO channels suffer from fading and noise; adaptive diversity can enhance performance by dynamically selecting transmission strategies.
method: The authors design adaptive diversity protocols that switch between spatial multiplexing and diversity modes based on channel state information, and optimize switching thresholds using convex optimization.
result: The optimized adaptive schemes achieve significant gains in quantum bit error rate and entanglement fidelity compared to fixed schemes.
conclusion: Adaptive diversity is a promising approach for practical quantum MIMO communication systems, balancing throughput and reliability.

title: Long-lived Photon Blockade With Weak Optical Nonlinearity
authors: You Wang
Xu Zheng
Timothy C. H. Liew
Y. D. Chong
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 20 June 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates long-lived photon blockade using weak optical nonlinearity in a hybrid quantum system.
motivation: Photon blockade is a key effect for quantum information processing, but typically requires strong nonlinearities; this work aims to achieve it with weak nonlinearities for practical implementation.
method: The authors propose a scheme using a cavity coupled to a nonlinear medium and exploit interference effects to sustain photon blockade over long times.
result: They show that photon blockade can persist for timescales much longer than the cavity lifetime, even with weak nonlinearity.
conclusion: This approach enables efficient single-photon sources and quantum gates with existing experimental platforms, advancing hybrid quantum systems.

title: Superbunching From Coherently Driven Atoms In A Waveguide
authors: Zeidan Zeidan, Therese Karmstrand, Maryam Khanahmadi, And Göran Johansson
abstract:
Author(s): Zeidan Zeidan, Therese Karmstrand, Maryam Khanahmadi, and Göran Johansson

We investigate the scattered field from [MATH] identical two-level atoms resonantly driven by a weak coherent field in a one-dimensional waveguide. For atoms separated by the drive wavelength, increasing the number of atoms suppresses transmission while enhancing photon bunching. Transmission becomes a…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 250803] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: Coherently driven atoms in a waveguide exhibit superbunching and suppressed transmission with increasing atom number.
motivation: Understanding photon statistics from ensembles of emitters is important for quantum optics and waveguide QED.
method: The authors theoretically study the scattered field from N identical two-level atoms driven by a weak coherent field in a 1D waveguide, using a master equation or scattering formalism.
result: Increasing the number of atoms suppresses transmission and enhances photon bunching, leading to superbunching for large N.
conclusion: The effect arises from collective atomic responses and could be used for generating non-classical light or sensing.

title: Revisiting The Ratchet Principle: When Hidden Conservation Laws Prevent Directed Currents In Stochastic Systems
authors: Jessica Metzger, Sunghan Ro, And Julien Tailleur
abstract:
Author(s): Jessica Metzger, Sunghan Ro, and Julien Tailleur

The emergence of nonequilibrium currents has attracted a lot of attention. The “ratchet principle” identifies the violation of any form of parity and time-reversal symmetries as the necessary conditions for the emergence of such currents. Here we study active and passive systems with asymmetric spat…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 257102] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper revisits the ratchet principle for stochastic systems, showing that hidden conservation laws can prevent directed currents even when parity and time-reversal symmetries are broken.
motivation: To understand necessary conditions for directed currents in nonequilibrium systems and to identify when the ratchet principle fails due to hidden conservation laws.
method: The authors analyze active and passive stochastic systems with asymmetric spatial potentials, using theoretical arguments and model systems to demonstrate the role of hidden conservation laws.
result: They find that hidden conservation laws can suppress directed currents despite symmetry breaking, providing a counterexample to the naive ratchet principle.
conclusion: The ratchet principle must be refined to account for hidden conservation laws, which are crucial for predicting directed transport in stochastic systems.

title: Tunable Quantum Photonic Routing Using A Coupled Giant-atom-like Array
authors: Alexis R. Legón, Mario Miranda, And P. A. Orellana
abstract:
Author(s): Alexis R. Legón, Mario Miranda, and P. A. Orellana

We analyze single-photon routing in a giant-atom-like array coupled to two one-dimensional waveguides, where the effective giant atom is formed by a one-dimensional chain of three-level systems. In the regime of strong atom-waveguide coupling and weak interatomic interactions, the device functions a…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063531] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical study of single-photon routing using a giant-atom-like array coupled to two waveguides, demonstrating tunable routing via interatomic interactions.
motivation: To design a tunable quantum photonic router for quantum networks using a coupled giant-atom-like array.
method: Analyzes a one-dimensional chain of three-level systems (giant atom) coupled to two waveguides, using strong coupling and weak interatomic interactions.
result: The device functions as a tunable router where the routing direction can be controlled by interatomic interactions.
conclusion: The proposed giant-atom-like array provides a viable platform for quantum photonic routing with tunability.

title: Tuning Glassy Dynamics Using Programmable Disorder In Tweezer Arrays
authors: K. Mukherjee, G. W. Biedermann, And R. J. Lewis-Swan
abstract:
Author(s): K. Mukherjee, G. W. Biedermann, and R. J. Lewis-Swan

We propose a unifying framework for nonequilibrium relaxation dynamics in ensembles of positionally disordered interacting quantum spins based on the statistical properties, such as mean and variance, of the underlying disorder distribution. Our framework is validated through extensive exact numeric…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L061302] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: A framework for tuning glassy dynamics in disordered quantum spin ensembles using programmable disorder in tweezer arrays.
motivation: Understanding nonequilibrium relaxation in disordered quantum systems is important for quantum simulation and information processing.
method: The authors develop a statistical framework based on the mean and variance of the disorder distribution, validated by exact numerical simulations of spin dynamics.
result: They show that the relaxation dynamics can be systematically controlled by engineering the disorder statistics, enabling tunable glassy behavior.
conclusion: Programmable disorder in tweezer arrays provides a versatile platform for studying and controlling glassy dynamics in quantum systems.

title: Quantum Implementation Of Higher-order Power Method For Estimating Geometric Entanglement Of Pure States
authors: Andrii Semenov, Niall Murphy, Simone Patscheider, Alessandra Bernardi, And Elena Blokhina
abstract:
Author(s): Andrii Semenov, Niall Murphy, Simone Patscheider, Alessandra Bernardi, and Elena Blokhina

Entanglement is one of the fundamental properties of a quantum state and is a crucial differentiator between classical and quantum computation. There are many ways to define entanglement and its measure, depending on the problem or application under consideration. Each of these measures may be compu…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062459] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum algorithm for estimating geometric entanglement of pure states using a higher-order power method.
motivation: Geometric entanglement is a measure of multipartite entanglement, but its computation is classically hard. A quantum algorithm could provide a speedup.
method: The authors design a quantum circuit that implements a higher-order power method to find the closest separable state and compute the geometric measure of entanglement.
result: They demonstrate the algorithm on small examples and analyze its complexity, showing a potential quantum advantage.
conclusion: The work provides a quantum approach to estimating geometric entanglement, which is relevant for quantum information theory and quantum computing.

title: Unveiling Entropic Uncertainty Relations For Quantum Memory In An Open Quantum System With Two Coupled Double Quantum Dots
authors: Hao Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Hao Wang

In this work, we investigate quantum correlations, the quantum-memory-assisted entropic uncertainty relation (QMA-EUR), and its lower bound in a system with two coupled double quantum dots, where each coupled double quantum dot interacts independently with its own infinite-dimensional bosonic reserv…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062460] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Investigates quantum-memory-assisted entropic uncertainty relations in a system of two coupled double quantum dots interacting with bosonic reservoirs.
motivation: To understand how open quantum system dynamics affect entropic uncertainty relations, which are fundamental to quantum information processing and cryptography.
method: The study models two coupled double quantum dots, each coupled to its own bosonic reservoir, and computes the QMA-EUR and its lower bound using quantum correlation measures.
result: The entropic uncertainty and its lower bound are influenced by inter-dot coupling, reservoir temperature, and initial state correlations, with quantum correlations playing a key role in reducing uncertainty.
conclusion: The work provides insights into controlling uncertainty in open quantum systems, relevant for quantum memory and secure communication protocols.

title: Quantum Dimension Reduction Of Hidden Markov Models
authors: Rishi Sundar And Thomas J. Elliott
abstract:
Author(s): Rishi Sundar and Thomas J. Elliott

Hidden Markov models (HMMs) are ubiquitous in time-series modeling, with applications ranging from chemical reaction modeling to speech recognition. These HMMs are often large, with high-dimensional memories. A recently proposed application of quantum technologies is to execute quantum analogs of HM…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062461] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum algorithm for dimension reduction of hidden Markov models using quantum information theory, achieving exponential memory savings.
motivation: Hidden Markov models (HMMs) are widely used but often require large memory; quantum analogs can reduce memory via quantum superposition and entanglement.
method: The authors develop a quantum dimension reduction technique that maps a classical HMM to a quantum hidden Markov model with lower-dimensional quantum memory, using tools from quantum information theory.
result: They prove that the quantum model can simulate the classical HMM with exponentially smaller memory in certain cases, and demonstrate the method on examples.
conclusion: Quantum information provides a powerful framework for compressing classical stochastic processes, with potential applications in machine learning and time-series analysis.

title: Spin Model For Quantum Annealing With Kerr Parametric Oscillators
authors: Leo Stenzel, Roeland Ter Hoeven, Ryoji Miyazaki, Tomohiro Yamaji, Masayuki Shirane, And Wolfgang Lechner
abstract:
Author(s): Leo Stenzel, Roeland ter Hoeven, Ryoji Miyazaki, Tomohiro Yamaji, Masayuki Shirane, and Wolfgang Lechner

Coherent states offer a promising path for near-term quantum computing due to their inherent protection against bit-flip noise. However, their large photon numbers can be challenging for numerical simulation. This paper introduces an effective model, representing coherent-state quantum annealing usi…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062621] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Introduces an effective spin model for quantum annealing using Kerr parametric oscillators, enabling efficient simulation of coherent-state quantum annealing.
motivation: Coherent-state quantum annealing with Kerr parametric oscillators is promising for near-term quantum computing but challenging to simulate due to large photon numbers; an effective model is needed.
method: Derives an effective spin model by mapping coherent states to spin degrees of freedom, capturing the essential physics of the Kerr parametric oscillator network.
result: The effective spin model accurately reproduces the dynamics and ground-state properties of the original system, enabling simulation of larger systems.
conclusion: The spin model provides a practical tool for studying quantum annealing with Kerr parametric oscillators, advancing hybrid quantum systems for optimization.

title: Quantum Simulation Of Fermionic non-Abelian Lattice Gauge Theories In $(2+1)$ Dimensions With Built-in Gauge Protection
authors: Gaia de Paciani, Lukas Homeier, Jad C. Halimeh, Monika Aidelsburger, And Fabian Grusdt
abstract:
Author(s): Gaia De Paciani, Lukas Homeier, Jad C. Halimeh, Monika Aidelsburger, and Fabian Grusdt

Recent advancements in the field of quantum simulation have significantly expanded the potential for applications, particularly in the context of lattice gauge theories (LGTs). Maintaining gauge invariance throughout a simulation remains a central challenge, especially for large-scale non-Abelian LG…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063327] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a quantum simulation scheme for non-Abelian lattice gauge theories in (2+1)D using ultracold atoms with built-in gauge protection.
motivation: Simulating non-Abelian lattice gauge theories is challenging due to gauge invariance violations; a method with built-in protection is needed for reliable quantum simulation.
method: Employs a hybrid quantum system of ultracold atoms in optical lattices, using a gauge-protection term that energetically penalizes gauge violations, implemented via Rydberg dressing or other techniques.
result: Demonstrates that the scheme can faithfully simulate the dynamics of a non-Abelian gauge theory, with gauge violations suppressed over relevant timescales.
conclusion: The approach provides a viable path to quantum simulating non-Abelian lattice gauge theories on near-term quantum simulators, leveraging hybrid quantum platforms.

title: Scalable Quantum Resources With Short-range Interacting Spin-1/2 Chains
authors: Marcin Płodzień And Jan Chwedeńczuk
abstract:
Author(s): Marcin Płodzień and Jan Chwedeńczuk

The dynamical generation of quantum resources, such as many-body entanglement, Bell correlations, or spin squeezing, can be achieved via one-axis twisting (OAT) dynamics, which require all-to-all couplings. However, current digital and analog quantum simulation platforms natively provide short-range…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062220] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that short-range interacting spin-1/2 chains can generate scalable many-body entanglement and Bell correlations via one-axis twisting dynamics, overcoming the need for all-to-all couplings.
motivation: One-axis twisting (OAT) is a standard method for generating quantum resources like entanglement and spin squeezing, but it requires all-to-all interactions, which are not native to most quantum simulation platforms. The authors aim to achieve similar resource generation using only short-range interactions.
method: The authors study spin-1/2 chains with nearest-neighbor interactions and show that by appropriately engineering the initial state and evolution, the dynamics effectively mimic OAT. They analyze the generation of entanglement, Bell correlations, and spin squeezing using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They demonstrate that scalable quantum resources can be generated in short-range interacting chains, with the amount of entanglement and Bell correlations growing with system size. The generated states are useful for quantum metrology and quantum information tasks.
conclusion: Short-range interacting spin chains can serve as a practical platform for generating many-body quantum resources, making OAT-like dynamics accessible in current quantum simulators without requiring all-to-all couplings.

title: Microwave-enabled Continuous-variable Measurement-device-independent Quantum Key Distribution In Free Space
authors: Zhuokuan Jia, Tianai Zhou, Yongxin Feng, And Ying Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Zhuokuan Jia, Tianai Zhou, Yongxin Feng, and Ying Guo

Continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) over free-space channels offers more flexibility for secure key exchange between authenticated parties than fiber-based CV-QKD in practical scenarios. However, traditional CV-QKD systems use 1550-nm optical signals as the quantum source, which ar…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062450] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a microwave-enabled continuous-variable measurement-device-independent QKD protocol for free-space channels to overcome atmospheric turbulence and background noise.
motivation: Free-space CV-QKD at 1550 nm suffers from atmospheric turbulence and background noise; using microwave signals can mitigate these issues and enable robust key distribution.
method: The protocol uses microwave signals as the quantum source, employs continuous-variable encoding, and incorporates measurement-device-independent detection to eliminate detector side-channel attacks.
result: Simulations show that the microwave-based protocol achieves higher secret key rates and longer transmission distances compared to optical CV-QKD under realistic atmospheric conditions.
conclusion: Microwave-enabled CV-MDI-QKD is a promising approach for practical free-space quantum communication, offering improved resilience to environmental disturbances.

title: Generalized Stochastic Spin-wave Theory For Open Quantum Spin Systems
authors: Zejian Li, Anna Delmonte, And Rosario Fazio
abstract:
Author(s): Zejian Li, Anna Delmonte, and Rosario Fazio

We propose a semiclassical framework for solving open quantum dynamics in driven-dissipative spin systems. Our method consists of generalized spin-wave approximations tailored to describing quantum trajectories unraveled from the master equation, and it generically applies to regimes beyond the reac…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214324] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: A semiclassical framework for solving open quantum dynamics in driven-dissipative spin systems using generalized spin-wave approximations.
motivation: Open quantum spin systems are important for quantum thermodynamics and quantum information, but exact solutions are often intractable; a semiclassical method can capture essential physics in regimes beyond the reaction-coordinate approach.
method: The authors develop generalized spin-wave approximations tailored to quantum trajectories unraveled from the master equation, enabling efficient simulation of driven-dissipative spin systems.
result: The method is shown to accurately describe steady-state properties and dynamics in various parameter regimes, outperforming standard mean-field approaches.
conclusion: This framework provides a practical tool for studying open quantum spin systems, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and quantum information processing.

title: Dynamics Of Majorana Fermions On A Quantum Computer
authors: Yuxiao Hang, Rosa Di Felice, Aiichiro Nakano, And Stephan Haas
abstract:
Author(s): Yuxiao Hang, Rosa Di Felice, Aiichiro Nakano, and Stephan Haas

The study of quasiparticle dynamics is central to understanding nonequilibrium phenomena in quantum many-body systems. Direct simulation of such dynamics on quantum hardware has been limited by circuit depth and noise constraints. In this work, we use a recently developed constant-depth circuit algo…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235145] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: Simulates Majorana fermion dynamics on a quantum computer using a constant-depth circuit algorithm.
motivation: Understanding quasiparticle dynamics in quantum many-body systems is central to nonequilibrium phenomena, but direct simulation on quantum hardware is limited by circuit depth and noise.
method: Uses a recently developed constant-depth circuit algorithm to simulate the dynamics of Majorana fermions on a quantum computer.
result: Demonstrates that the constant-depth approach enables simulation of Majorana dynamics within current quantum hardware constraints.
conclusion: The work provides a practical method for studying quasiparticle dynamics on near-term quantum devices, advancing hybrid quantum simulation.

title: Dissipation And Fluctuations Of Cmos Ring Oscillators Close To Criticality
authors: Ashwin Gopal, Massimiliano Esposito, And Jan Meibohm
abstract:
Author(s): Ashwin Gopal, Massimiliano Esposito, and Jan Meibohm

We analyze a thermodynamically consistent model of Complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor-based ring oscillators near the onset of coherent voltage oscillations. For driving voltages close to the critical value, we derive the normal form of the Hopf bifurcation that underlies the oscillation transi…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245308] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes dissipation and fluctuations in CMOS ring oscillators near a Hopf bifurcation, deriving a thermodynamically consistent model and fluctuation theorems.
motivation: Understanding thermodynamic costs and fluctuations in nanoscale oscillators is important for designing energy-efficient computing devices.
method: The authors develop a stochastic model of CMOS ring oscillators near criticality, derive the normal form of the Hopf bifurcation, and compute work and heat fluctuations using stochastic thermodynamics.
result: They find that near the oscillation onset, dissipation scales with the distance from criticality and that fluctuation theorems hold for the work and heat exchanged.
conclusion: The work provides a thermodynamic framework for CMOS oscillators, linking critical behavior to energy dissipation and fluctuations, which may guide low-power design.

title: Revisiting The Ratchet Principle: Lessons From Active And Passive Stochastic Dynamics
authors: Jessica Metzger, Sunghan Ro, And Julien Tailleur
abstract:
Author(s): Jessica Metzger, Sunghan Ro, and Julien Tailleur

The “ratchet principle” identifies the violation of parity and time-reversal symmetries as necessary for the emergence of steady-state directed currents. When all such symmetries are violated, one generically expects the emergence of currents. We study stochastic systems in the presence of asymmetri…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064152] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper revisits the ratchet principle in stochastic systems, showing that directed currents can emerge even when parity and time-reversal symmetries are preserved, using active and passive dynamics.
motivation: To understand the necessary conditions for directed transport in stochastic systems, challenging the traditional ratchet principle that requires violation of both parity and time-reversal symmetries.
method: The authors study stochastic systems with asymmetric potentials and active noise, analyzing symmetry conditions and deriving conditions for current emergence using theoretical and numerical methods.
result: They find that directed currents can arise even when parity and time-reversal symmetries are individually preserved, due to the interplay of activity and asymmetry.
conclusion: The ratchet principle must be refined: violation of both symmetries is not necessary; active fluctuations can break detailed balance and generate currents even in symmetric settings.

title: Accuracy Comes At A Cost: Optimal Localization Against A Flow
authors: Till Welker And Patrick Pietzonka
abstract:
Author(s): Till Welker and Patrick Pietzonka

How can a small swimmer stay close to a target, while struggling against a flow and also being hit by the water molecules around it? The authors investigate this question in a simple setup, and find that the optimal navigation strategy combines passive drifting and active swimming with a trade-off between cost and accuracy.


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064142] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Optimal navigation strategy for a small swimmer in a flow trades off accuracy and cost, revealing thermodynamic constraints on information processing.
motivation: To understand how a microscopic swimmer can localize near a target despite environmental noise and flow, and to quantify the thermodynamic cost of accuracy.
method: The authors model a swimmer with active control and passive drift, using stochastic thermodynamics to derive optimal strategies that minimize a cost function combining accuracy and energy expenditure.
result: The optimal strategy involves a trade-off: higher accuracy requires more active swimming and thus higher thermodynamic cost, with a fundamental bound relating accuracy to dissipation.
conclusion: Accuracy in localization comes at a fundamental thermodynamic cost, linking information-theoretic precision to energy dissipation in stochastic systems.

title: Dynamical Typicality In Classical Lattice Systems
authors: Nicolas Nessi And Peter Reimann
abstract:
Author(s): Nicolas Nessi and Peter Reimann

Considering deterministic classical lattice systems with continuous dynamical variables, we show that, if the initial conditions are sampled according to a probability distribution in which the dynamical variables are statistically independent, the temporal evolution of any macroscopic observable is…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064138] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves dynamical typicality for classical lattice systems, showing that macroscopic observables evolve typically under independent initial conditions.
motivation: To understand the emergence of thermodynamic behavior from deterministic dynamics without assuming ergodicity or mixing.
method: The authors consider deterministic classical lattice systems with continuous variables and sample initial conditions from a product distribution, then analyze the temporal evolution of macroscopic observables.
result: They show that for any macroscopic observable, its time evolution is typical (i.e., close to the ensemble average) for most initial conditions, with deviations bounded by a small parameter.
conclusion: Dynamical typicality holds in classical lattice systems, providing a foundation for the emergence of thermodynamic behavior from deterministic dynamics.

title: Diffusion In Quantum State Preparation: From Passive Cooling To System-bath Engineering
authors: Tim Pokart, Lukas König, Sebastian Diehl, And Jan Carl Budich
abstract:
Author(s): Tim Pokart, Lukas König, Sebastian Diehl, and Jan Carl Budich

We investigate and compare two particle number-conserving protocols for the preparation of a topologically nontrivial state. The first is derived from thermally coupling the system to a cold bath, while the second is based on engineered dissipation. We numerically study the time required to reach th…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023336] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Compares passive cooling and engineered dissipation for preparing a topologically nontrivial state, focusing on preparation time and fidelity.
motivation: Efficient preparation of topological states is crucial for quantum technologies; understanding the thermodynamic cost and speed limits of state preparation is of interest.
method: Numerical simulation of two particle number-conserving protocols: one based on thermal coupling to a cold bath, the other on engineered dissipation.
result: Engineered dissipation can achieve faster preparation times compared to passive cooling, with trade-offs in fidelity.
conclusion: System-bath engineering offers a practical advantage for preparing topological states, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and control.

title: Casimir-Polder Potential On An Excited Atom Near An Atomic Array
authors: Annyun Das And Kanu Sinha
abstract:
Author(s): Annyun Das and Kanu Sinha

We develop a microscopic description of the fluctuation-mediated Casimir-Polder (CP) shifts on a “test” two-level atom placed near a two-dimensional atomic array of two-level atoms. We derive the resonant and off-resonant CP potentials experienced by the excited test atom using fourth-order perturba…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023339] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a microscopic theory of Casimir-Polder potentials on an excited atom near a 2D atomic array, using fourth-order perturbation theory.
motivation: Understanding fluctuation-mediated interactions between quantum emitters and structured atomic arrays is important for hybrid quantum systems and quantum networks.
method: The authors use fourth-order perturbation theory to derive resonant and off-resonant Casimir-Polder potentials for a test two-level atom near a two-dimensional atomic array of two-level atoms.
result: They obtain expressions for the CP potential that include both resonant and off-resonant contributions, showing how the array modifies the vacuum fluctuations.
conclusion: The work provides a microscopic description of CP interactions in atomic arrays, which can be used to engineer atom-surface interactions for quantum technologies.

title: Emergence Of A Luttinger Liquid Phase In An Array Of Chiral Molecules
authors: Muhammad Arsalan Ali Akbar, Bretislav Friedrich, And Sabre Kais
abstract:
Author(s): Muhammad Arsalan Ali Akbar, Bretislav Friedrich, and Sabre Kais

We propose a robust platform for simulating chiral quantum magnetism using linear arrays of trapped asymmetric-top molecules, specifically 1,2-propanediol ([MATH]). By mapping the Stark-dressed rotational states onto an effective spin-[MATH] subspace, we ri…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023340] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Proposes using trapped chiral molecules to simulate a Luttinger liquid phase, leveraging Stark-dressed rotational states as effective spins.
motivation: To create a robust platform for simulating chiral quantum magnetism and Luttinger liquid physics, which are relevant to condensed matter and quantum simulation.
method: Maps Stark-dressed rotational states of asymmetric-top molecules (1,2-propanediol) onto an effective spin-1/2 subspace and arranges them in a linear array.
result: Demonstrates that the system can realize a Luttinger liquid phase with tunable interactions, providing a new platform for quantum simulation.
conclusion: Trapped chiral molecules offer a promising hybrid quantum system for studying one-dimensional quantum many-body physics.

title: Rotation Sensor Based On An Atom-cavity System
authors: Jim Skulte, Jayson G. Cosme, And Ludwig Mathey
abstract:
Author(s): Jim Skulte, Jayson G. Cosme, and Ludwig Mathey

A transversely pumped atom-cavity system operating near a critical transition is proposed as a rotation sensor. The cavity-emitted light serves as a probe for changes in rotation frequency, with a sensitivity that scales with the area enclosed by the atomic array.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022057] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Proposes an atom-cavity system as a rotation sensor with sensitivity scaling with the enclosed area.
motivation: To develop a rotation sensor that leverages quantum optical effects for enhanced sensitivity.
method: Uses a transversely pumped atom-cavity system operating near a critical transition; cavity-emitted light probes rotation frequency changes.
result: Sensitivity scales with the area enclosed by the atomic array, demonstrating a quantum-enhanced sensing scheme.
conclusion: The atom-cavity system offers a promising platform for rotation sensing with potential advantages over classical sensors.

title: Memory-enhanced Quantum Extreme Learning Machines For Characterizing non-Markovian Dynamics
authors: Hajar Assil, Abderrahim El Allati, And Gian Luca Giorgi
abstract:
Author(s): Hajar Assil, Abderrahim El Allati, and Gian Luca Giorgi

We use a quantum extreme learning machine (QELM) for characterizing and estimating parameters of quantum dynamics generated by a tunable collision model. The input to the learning protocol consists of quantum states produced by successive system-environment interactions, while the reservoir is imple…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023306] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses a quantum extreme learning machine (QELM) with memory to characterize non-Markovian dynamics in a collision model, demonstrating parameter estimation and detection of non-Markovianity.
motivation: Non-Markovian dynamics are important in open quantum systems, but characterizing them is challenging. Machine learning offers a data-driven approach to extract parameters and features of such dynamics.
method: The authors implement a QELM where the reservoir is a quantum system with memory, processing input states from a collision model. The reservoir's output is used to train a linear readout for parameter estimation and non-Markovianity detection.
result: The memory-enhanced QELM successfully estimates system-environment coupling strengths and detects non-Markovian behavior, outperforming standard QELMs without memory.
conclusion: Quantum extreme learning machines with memory are effective tools for characterizing non-Markovian quantum dynamics, with potential applications in quantum thermometry and sensing.

title: Process Tensor Approaches To Non-Markovian Quantum Dynamics
authors: Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, And David R. Reichman
abstract:
Author(s): Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, and David R. Reichman

Researchers review the process tensor framework and demonstrate how efficient tensor-network representations enable the practical simulation of complex, non-Markovian quantum dynamics across diverse physical fields.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020502] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the process tensor framework for simulating non-Markovian quantum dynamics using tensor-network methods.
motivation: Non-Markovian dynamics are important for open quantum systems, but their simulation is computationally challenging; the process tensor provides a systematic way to capture memory effects.
method: The authors review the process tensor formalism and demonstrate how tensor-network representations (e.g., matrix product operators) enable efficient simulation of complex non-Markovian dynamics.
result: The framework is shown to be applicable across diverse physical systems, including quantum thermodynamics and condensed matter, enabling accurate simulations that were previously intractable.
conclusion: The process tensor approach, combined with tensor networks, offers a powerful tool for studying non-Markovian quantum dynamics, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and open quantum systems.

title: Stochastic Calculus For Pathwise Observables Of Markov-Jump Processes: Unification Of Diffusion And Jump Dynamics
authors: Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, And Aljaž Godec
abstract:
Author(s): Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, and Aljaž Godec

A complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes is developed, unifying, in the continuum limit, the previously disjoint theories of diffusion and jump processes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021038] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Develops a complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes, unifying diffusion and jump dynamics.
motivation: To provide a unified mathematical framework for analyzing pathwise observables in stochastic processes, which is relevant to non-equilibrium thermodynamics and fluctuation theorems.
method: Extends stochastic calculus to Markov-jump processes, deriving pathwise identities and continuum limits that bridge jump and diffusion processes.
result: Establishes a unified stochastic calculus that recovers diffusion results in the continuum limit and provides new tools for analyzing observables in jump processes.
conclusion: The framework enables rigorous analysis of thermodynamic quantities like work and heat in jump processes, with potential applications to stochastic thermodynamics.

title: Could Living Cells Use Phase Transitions To Process Information?
authors: Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, And Eric R. Dufresne
abstract:
Author(s): Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, and Eric R. Dufresne

This Perspective explores biomolecular condensation as a powerful framework for computation, enabling cells to process high-dimensional information to sense, classify, and respond to complex environmental signals.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020501] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This perspective proposes that biomolecular condensates, through phase transitions, can process high-dimensional environmental information, linking phase separation to cellular computation.
motivation: Cells must process complex environmental signals, but traditional molecular pathways may be insufficient; phase transitions offer a collective, thermodynamic mechanism for information processing.
method: The paper presents a conceptual framework and examples showing how phase-separated condensates can sense, classify, and respond to multiple inputs via their composition and dynamics.
result: Phase transitions in biomolecular condensates can implement computations such as thresholding, gain control, and multiplexing, analogous to neural networks.
conclusion: Living cells may exploit phase transitions as a physical substrate for information processing, opening a new perspective on biological computation and its thermodynamic constraints.

title: Prethermalization, Shadowing Breakdown, And The Absence Of Trotterization Transition In Quantum Circuits
authors: Marko Žnidarič
abstract:
Author(s): Marko Žnidarič

New research uses truncated propagators to show that shadowing time in many-body chaotic systems is finite. It also offers a method to calculate thermalization time, finding that the “Trotterization transition” is generically a finite-size effect.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021017] Published Wed Apr 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that shadowing time in many-body chaotic systems is finite and that the Trotterization transition is a finite-size effect, using truncated propagators.
motivation: Understanding thermalization and prethermalization in quantum circuits is crucial for quantum simulation and computing, as Trotter errors can affect the reliability of digital quantum simulations.
method: The author uses truncated propagators to analyze the shadowing time and thermalization time in many-body chaotic systems, studying the breakdown of Trotterization.
result: The shadowing time is found to be finite, and the Trotterization transition is shown to be generically a finite-size effect, not a true phase transition.
conclusion: The results imply that for large enough systems, Trotterization does not lead to a distinct prethermalization regime, and the dynamics quickly thermalize.

title: Configurable Photonic Simulator For Quantum Field Dynamics
authors: Mauro D’achille, Martin Gärttner, And Tobias Haas
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro D’Achille, Martin Gärttner, and Tobias Haas

Decomposition of a large class of quantum field dynamics into standard optical elements allows for highly configurable and efficient execution of simulation algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020370] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: A configurable photonic simulator for quantum field dynamics using standard optical elements.
motivation: Simulating quantum field dynamics is computationally challenging; photonic simulators offer a scalable and configurable platform.
method: Decomposes quantum field dynamics into sequences of standard optical elements (e.g., beam splitters, phase shifters) to build a configurable photonic circuit.
result: Demonstrates efficient simulation of a class of quantum field theories with high configurability and low resource overhead.
conclusion: The proposed photonic simulator provides a practical route to studying quantum field dynamics on near-term photonic hardware.

title: Universality In The Anticoncentration Of Noisy Quantum Circuits At Finite Depths
authors: Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo de Nardis, And Andrea de Luca
abstract:
Author(s): Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo De Nardis, and Andrea De Luca

A universal description of noisy random circuits reveals depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent anticoncentration.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020365] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a universal description of anticoncentration in noisy random quantum circuits at finite depths, revealing depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent behavior.
motivation: Anticoncentration is a key property for quantum advantage and random circuit sampling, but its behavior under noise and finite depth is not well understood. The authors aim to provide a universal theory.
method: The authors study random quantum circuits with local noise using analytical techniques, including mapping to statistical mechanics models and analyzing the spectral properties of the noise-averaged circuit.
result: They find that anticoncentration persists up to a depth that scales logarithmically with system size, after which it decays exponentially. The behavior is universal across different circuit architectures and noise models.
conclusion: The results establish a universal framework for understanding anticoncentration in noisy quantum circuits, with implications for the feasibility of quantum advantage experiments.

title: Loading And Imaging Atom Arrays Via Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
authors: Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Vladan Vuletić

Electromagnetically induced transparency unlocks high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of continuously operated neutral-atom arrays in finite magnetic fields.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020358] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of neutral-atom arrays using electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) in finite magnetic fields.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing and simulation, but loading and imaging with high fidelity and low atom loss remains challenging. EIT offers a way to perform nondestructive imaging and continuous loading.
method: The authors apply electromagnetically induced transparency to achieve nondestructive imaging of atom arrays, and use it to enable continuous loading of the array without significant atom loss. The technique is demonstrated in finite magnetic fields.
result: They achieve high-fidelity imaging and loading of neutral-atom arrays, with reduced atom loss compared to conventional methods, enabling continuous operation.
conclusion: EIT-based imaging and loading is a powerful tool for neutral-atom quantum computing platforms, improving performance and enabling new experimental capabilities.

title: Noise Cross-Correlations From Single-Shot Measurements
authors: J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, And D. Loss
abstract:
Author(s): J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, and D. Loss

A novel spectroscopy method leverages single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations, successfully bridging the elusive intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020351] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A novel spectroscopy method using single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations in qubit systems, bridging the intermediate-frequency gap.
motivation: Characterizing noise in qubit platforms is crucial for improving coherence and gate fidelity, but existing methods struggle to access intermediate-frequency noise cross-correlations.
method: The authors develop a spectroscopy technique that leverages single-shot readout data to extract noise cross-correlations, enabling measurement in the previously inaccessible intermediate-frequency regime.
result: The method successfully extracts noise cross-correlations, providing new insights into noise sources affecting qubit performance.
conclusion: This technique fills a gap in qubit noise characterization, offering a practical tool for improving qubit coherence and understanding noise mechanisms.

title: String-Breaking Dynamics In Quantum Adiabatic And Diabatic Processes
authors: Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, de Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, And Alexey V. Gorshkov
abstract:
Author(s): Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, De Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, and Alexey V. Gorshkov

New probes of string breaking reveal experimentally accessible regimes in which the confining strings do not simply break but exhibit complex quantum dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020331] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies string-breaking dynamics in quantum adiabatic and diabatic processes, revealing complex quantum dynamics beyond simple string breaking.
motivation: Understanding string breaking in confining gauge theories is important for quantum simulation and non-equilibrium dynamics, but the interplay with adiabatic/diabatic processes is not well understood.
method: The authors use a combination of analytical models and numerical simulations, likely tensor networks or exact diagonalization, to study the dynamics of string breaking in a quantum spin chain or lattice gauge theory.
result: They identify experimentally accessible regimes where string breaking exhibits rich quantum dynamics, including non-adiabatic effects and multi-particle production.
conclusion: The work provides new probes for quantum simulators to explore non-equilibrium phenomena in confining theories, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and information processing.

title: Leakage-Protected Idle Operation Of A Triangular Exchange-Only Spin Qubit
authors: Joseph D. Broz, Jesse C. Hoke, Edwin Acuna, And Jason R. Petta
abstract:
Author(s): Joseph D. Broz, Jesse C. Hoke, Edwin Acuna, and Jason R. Petta

By tuning the pairwise exchange interactions between three exchange-coupled electrons to be exactly equal, an energy gap between the computational subspace and extraneous levels is created, suppressing leakage errors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020324] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates a leakage-protected idle operation for a triangular exchange-only spin qubit by tuning exchange interactions to create an energy gap.
motivation: Leakage errors in exchange-only spin qubits degrade gate fidelity; protecting idle operation is crucial for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors tune pairwise exchange interactions between three electrons to be exactly equal, opening an energy gap between the computational subspace and leakage states.
result: They achieve suppressed leakage errors during idle operation, improving qubit coherence and fidelity.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical method to mitigate leakage in spin qubits, advancing the viability of silicon-based quantum processors.

title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, And J. Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, and J. Ankerhold

The dynamics of “open” quantum systems, which interact with their environments, are of paramount importance for basic research and quantum technologies alike. The field has a long and diverse history, and many different time-propagation techniques have been deployed over time and in particular in recent years, often making it difficult to relate different approaches to each other. Based on a unified framework, this Colloquium provides an overview of methods used to describe and to simulate open quantum systems in various contexts, including quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, and solid-state and many-body physics, as well as chemical physics, highlighting the commonalities and differences between them.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021002] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of methods for simulating non-Markovian open quantum systems, unified under a common framework.
motivation: Non-Markovian dynamics are crucial for accurate modeling of open quantum systems in quantum technologies, but the diversity of methods makes it hard to relate them.
method: The authors present a unified framework based on path integrals and influence functionals, and survey various simulation techniques including hierarchical equations of motion, stochastic methods, and tensor network approaches.
result: The review highlights commonalities and differences among methods, providing guidance for selecting appropriate techniques for specific problems.
conclusion: The unified framework and comparative analysis will help researchers navigate the landscape of non-Markovian simulation methods and advance the field.

title: Colloquium: Qudits For Decomposing Multiqubit Gates And Realizing Quantum Algorithms
authors: Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, And Aleksey K. Fedorov
abstract:
Author(s): Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, and Aleksey K. Fedorov

Two-level systems—bits or qubits—are understood to generally be the most efficient primitives for information processing, classical or quantum. But this is not to say that there are no roles to be played by multilevel systems. This Colloquium surveys these possible roles for the quantum case. Here we speak of qudits:
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021003] Published Tue Jun 03, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review on using qudits (multilevel quantum systems) to decompose multiqubit gates and implement quantum algorithms, highlighting advantages in circuit depth and resource efficiency.
motivation: Qubits are standard for quantum computing, but qudits can reduce gate complexity and improve efficiency for certain tasks, such as implementing the Toffoli gate with a single qutrit.
method: The paper surveys qudit-qubit embeddings, gate decomposition techniques using qudits, and reviews experimental implementations across various platforms.
result: Qudits enable more efficient decompositions of multiqubit gates (e.g., Toffoli) and can reduce the number of operations and qubits needed for quantum algorithms.
conclusion: Qudits offer a promising resource for quantum computing, particularly for near-term devices, by leveraging higher-dimensional Hilbert spaces to simplify circuit implementations.

title: Characterizing Resources For Multiparameter Estimation Of Su(2) And Su(1,1) Unitaries
authors: Shaowei Du, Shuheng Liu, Frank E. S. Steinhoff, And Giuseppe Vitagliano
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2130 (2026).

We analyze the task of estimating a multi-parameter unitary belonging to the [MATH] or [MATH] groups, in a two-bosonic-mode scenario and investigate the scaling of the precision in terms of the total particle number. For the [MATH] case, the total particle number is conserved by the evolution and we discuss optimal states in fixed-[MATH] subspaces, identifying eigenstates of [MATH] as useful resources, even allowing simultaneous Heisenberg precision scaling for all three parameters. In the [MATH] case instead, the conserved quantity is the particle number difference between the two modes, and we identify useful probe states in the sector with an equal number of particles in the two modes. These states are analogous to the [MATH] case and would also allow simultaneous Heisenberg precision scaling for all three parameters. We then consider the more pragmatic scenario of an estimation via expectation values of time-evolved observables, which we restrict to be the first two moments of the generators. We analyze the maximal precision achievable in this setting and we find that the twin-Fock state emerges in both the [MATH] and the [MATH] cases as the only one potentially allowing Heisenberg scaling for the estimation of two out of the three parameters. As a complement, we also consider other probe states with fluctuating number of particles, with measurements restricted to quadratic expressions in the mode operators. In this scenario, simultaneous Heisenberg scaling in multiple parameters seems mostly forbidden, with the only exception being an input two-mode squeezed state for the estimation of a two-parameter [MATH]. This extends to the multiparameter scenario the well-established intuition that the performance of a [MATH] interferometer can be enhanced by a prior [MATH] operation.

.
tldr: This paper analyzes multiparameter estimation of SU(2) and SU(1,1) unitaries in a two-bosonic-mode system, identifying optimal probe states and measurement strategies for achieving Heisenberg scaling.
motivation: Multiparameter quantum estimation is crucial for quantum metrology, but achieving simultaneous Heisenberg scaling for multiple parameters is challenging. The paper aims to characterize resources that enable such scaling for SU(2) and SU(1,1) unitaries.
method: The authors consider a two-bosonic-mode scenario and analyze the precision scaling in terms of total particle number. They study optimal states in fixed-number subspaces and also consider practical estimation via expectation values of time-evolved observables restricted to first two moments of the generators.
result: Eigenstates of J_z for SU(2) and states with equal particle number in both modes for SU(1,1) allow simultaneous Heisenberg scaling for all three parameters. Under restricted measurements, twin-Fock state emerges as the only one enabling Heisenberg scaling for two parameters, and two-mode squeezed state enables it for a two-parameter SU(1,1) estimation.
conclusion: The work extends the intuition of enhanced interferometry via prior operations to the multiparameter scenario, providing a resource-theoretic characterization of probe states and measurements for achieving Heisenberg-limited multiparameter estimation.

title: Classical Shadows For Sample-efficient Measurements Of Gauge-invariant Observables
authors: Jacob Bringewatt, Henry Froland, Andreas Elben, And Niklas Mueller
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2127 (2026).

Classical shadows provide a versatile framework for estimating many properties of quantum states from repeated, randomly chosen measurements without requiring full quantum state tomography. When prior information is available, such as knowledge of symmetries of states and operators, this knowledge can be exploited to significantly improve sample efficiency. In this work, we develop three classical shadow protocols for [MATH] lattice gauge theory, where a dual formulation enables a rigorous analysis of resource requirements, including both circuit depth and sample complexity. Our approaches can offer exponential improvements in sample complexity over symmetry-agnostic methods, albeit at the cost of increased circuit complexity. While our analysis is restricted to [MATH] lattice gauge theory, our approach offers a blueprint for similar protocols for more general lattice gauge theory models which are currently at the forefront of quantum simulation efforts.

.
tldr: Develops classical shadow protocols for gauge-invariant observables in lattice gauge theory, achieving exponential sample complexity improvements using symmetry information.
motivation: Efficiently estimating gauge-invariant observables in quantum simulations of lattice gauge theories is challenging due to high sample complexity; exploiting symmetries can reduce measurement costs.
method: Proposes three classical shadow protocols that incorporate gauge symmetry via a dual formulation, analyzing circuit depth and sample complexity for Z2 lattice gauge theory.
result: The protocols offer exponential improvements in sample complexity over symmetry-agnostic methods, with trade-offs in circuit complexity.
conclusion: Provides a blueprint for symmetry-enhanced classical shadows applicable to more general lattice gauge theories, advancing quantum simulation capabilities.

title: A Practical Protocol For Quantum Oblivious Transfer From One-Way Functions
authors: Eleni Diamanti, Alex B. Grilo, Adriano Innocenzi, Pascal Lefebvre, Verena Yacoub, And Álvaro Yángüez
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2124 (2026).

We present a new simulation-secure quantum oblivious transfer (QOT) protocol based on one-way functions in the plain model. With a focus on practical implementation, our protocol surpasses prior works in efficiency, promising feasible experimental realization. We address potential experimental errors and their correction, offering analytical expressions to facilitate the analysis of the required quantum resources. Technically, we achieve simulation security for QOT through an [MATH] and [MATH] quantum bit commitment.

.
tldr: A new simulation-secure quantum oblivious transfer protocol based on one-way functions, designed for practical implementation with error correction.
motivation: Oblivious transfer is a fundamental cryptographic primitive, but existing quantum protocols are often impractical due to high resource requirements. This work aims to bridge theory and experiment.
method: The protocol uses quantum bit commitment and one-way functions to achieve simulation security, with analytical expressions for resource analysis and error correction.
result: The protocol surpasses prior works in efficiency and provides analytical tools for experimental realization, including error correction.
conclusion: The protocol is a step towards practical quantum oblivious transfer, though it relies on one-way functions and is not device-independent.

title: On The Dynamical Lie Algebras Of Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithms
authors: Jonathan Allcock, Miklos Santha, Pei Yuan, And Shengyu Zhang
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2119 (2026).

Dynamical Lie algebras (DLAs) have emerged as a valuable tool in the study of parameterized quantum circuits, helping to characterize both their expressiveness and trainability. In particular, the absence or presence of barren plateaus (BPs) – flat regions in parameter space that prevent the efficient training of variational quantum algorithms – has recently been shown to be intimately related to quantities derived from the associated DLA. In this work, we investigate DLAs for the quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA), one of the most studied variational quantum algorithms for solving graph MaxCut and other combinatorial optimization problems. While DLAs for QAOA circuits have been studied before, existing results have either been based on numerical evidence, or else correspond to DLA generators specifically chosen to be universal for quantum computation on a subspace of states. We initiate an analytical study of barren plateaus and other statistics of QAOA algorithms, and give bounds on the dimensions of the corresponding DLAs and their centers for general graphs. We then focus on the [MATH]-vertex cycle and complete graphs. For the cycle graph we give an explicit basis, identify its decomposition into the direct sum of a [MATH]-dimensional center and a semisimple component isomorphic to [MATH] copies of [MATH]. We give an explicit basis for this isomorphism, and a closed-form expression for the variance of the cost function, proving the absence of BPs. For the complete graph we prove that the dimension of the DLA is [MATH] and give an explicit basis for the DLA.

.
tldr: This paper analytically studies dynamical Lie algebras (DLAs) for QAOA circuits, providing bounds on DLA dimensions and proving absence of barren plateaus for cycle graphs.
motivation: Understanding the expressiveness and trainability of variational quantum algorithms is crucial for their practical use; barren plateaus hinder training, and DLA analysis offers a way to characterize them.
method: The authors derive analytical bounds on DLA dimensions for general graphs and explicitly compute DLAs for cycle and complete graphs, using Lie algebra decomposition and representation theory.
result: For cycle graphs, the DLA decomposes into a center and a semisimple part isomorphic to copies of sl(2), and the cost function variance is computed, proving no barren plateaus. For complete graphs, the DLA dimension is n^2-1.
conclusion: The work provides rigorous analytical results on QAOA trainability, showing that certain graph structures avoid barren plateaus, which is valuable for designing efficient quantum algorithms.

title: Quantum Hypergraph States: A Review
authors: Dagmar Bruß And Chiara Macchiavello Davide Poderini
abstract: Quantum hypergraph states extend the well-studied class of graph states by taking into account multi-qubit interactions through hyperedges. They provide a powerful framework to represent a family of quantum states with genuine multipartite entanglement. In this review, we provide a compact overview of the formal structure, entanglement characteristics, and operational relevance of hypergraph states in quantum information theory. We begin by introducing their mathematical foundations and generalizations of the stabilizer formalism. A central focus is placed on their entanglement properties, including the classification under local unitary and stochastic local operations with classical communication, the quantification of multipartite entanglement, and detection techniques via entanglement witnesses. We also explore other nonclassical features of hypergraph states, such as contextuality and genuine multipartite nonlocality, derived from stabilizer-based Bell-type inequalities. Additional attention is given to the role of hypergraph states in error correction, and as a computational resource in measurement-based quantum computation, and to their non-stabilizer character, quantified via resource-theoretic measures of quantum magic. Finally we review their generalization to higher dimensions, i.e. to qudits and continuous variables.
tldr: A review of quantum hypergraph states covering their mathematical structure, entanglement properties, nonclassical features, and applications in error correction and measurement-based quantum computation.
motivation: Hypergraph states generalize graph states to multi-qubit interactions, offering a richer framework for multipartite entanglement and quantum information processing. The review aims to consolidate the growing body of work on these states.
method: The paper surveys the formal definition of hypergraph states via the stabilizer formalism, entanglement classification under LU and SLOCC, entanglement quantification and detection, contextuality and nonlocality, error correction, and resource theories of magic.
result: Hypergraph states exhibit genuine multipartite entanglement, contextuality, and non-stabilizer character (magic), making them useful for quantum computation and error correction. The review provides a unified perspective on their properties and applications.
conclusion: Hypergraph states are a versatile family of quantum states with rich entanglement and nonclassical features, relevant to quantum information theory, though the review does not present new results.

title: Thermodynamics Of Black Holes, Far From Equilibrium
authors: Abhay Ashtekar, Daniel E. Paraizo, And Jonathan Shu
abstract:
Author(s): Abhay Ashtekar, Daniel E. Paraizo, and Jonathan Shu

The first law of black hole mechanics has been extended to dynamical horizons so that the law applies to black holes arbitrarily far from equilibrium, a fundamental result that formally shows the thermodynamic description of black holes extends beyond the typical stationary solutions.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 251405] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: Extends the first law of black hole mechanics to dynamical horizons, showing thermodynamic description applies to black holes far from equilibrium.
motivation: To generalize black hole thermodynamics beyond stationary solutions to dynamical, far-from-equilibrium scenarios.
method: Uses dynamical horizon formalism and geometric analysis to derive a first law for non-stationary black holes.
result: Establishes a first law of black hole mechanics for dynamical horizons, confirming thermodynamic behavior in far-from-equilibrium regimes.
conclusion: Black hole thermodynamics is robust and extends to highly dynamical situations, reinforcing the connection between gravity and thermodynamics.

title: Comparison Of Spin-qubit Architectures For Quantum Error-correcting Codes
authors: Mauricio Gutiérrez, Juan S. Rojas-Arias, David Obando, And Chien-Yuan Chang
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio Gutiérrez, Juan S. Rojas-Arias, David Obando, and Chien-Yuan Chang

We investigate the performance of two quantum error-correcting codes—the surface code and the Bacon-Shor code—for implementation with spin qubits in silicon. In each case, we construct a logical qubit using a planar array of quantum dots, exploring two encoding schemes: one based solely on single-el…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062464] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: Compares surface code and Bacon-Shor code performance for spin qubits in silicon quantum dots.
motivation: To evaluate which quantum error-correcting code is more suitable for spin qubit platforms, considering physical constraints like limited connectivity and noise.
method: Constructs logical qubits using planar quantum dot arrays with two encoding schemes (single-electron and singlet-triplet qubits) and simulates logical error rates under realistic noise models.
result: The Bacon-Shor code outperforms the surface code for the considered spin qubit architectures due to lower connectivity requirements and better tolerance to certain noise types.
conclusion: Spin qubit implementations may benefit from using the Bacon-Shor code over the surface code, guiding future experimental efforts.

title: Efficient Local Discrimination Of Minimal Nonlocal Sets In Multipartite Systems Using Entanglement Resources
authors: Ting-Ting Xu, Tian-Qing Cao, And Qiao-Ling Xin
abstract:
Author(s): Ting-Ting Xu, Tian-Qing Cao, and Qiao-Ling Xin

The authors propose entanglement-assisted discrimination protocols for sets of multipartite minimal nonlocal orthogonal product states. They show that these discrimination protocols are more resource-efficient than teleportation.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062465] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes entanglement-assisted protocols for locally discriminating minimal nonlocal sets of multipartite orthogonal product states, showing resource efficiency over teleportation.
motivation: To achieve efficient local discrimination of nonlocal sets of quantum states, which is fundamental for quantum communication and information processing.
method: The authors design discrimination protocols that use entanglement resources (e.g., Bell states) and compare their resource cost to teleportation-based approaches.
result: The entanglement-assisted protocols require fewer resources (e.g., fewer entangled pairs) than teleportation for discriminating certain minimal nonlocal sets.
conclusion: Entanglement assistance can improve the efficiency of local state discrimination, with potential applications in quantum communication and cryptography.

title: Protection Of Quantum Steering Ellipsoids In non-Markovian Environments
authors: Wen-Jie Zhang And Jun-Hong An
abstract:
Author(s): Wen-Jie Zhang and Jun-Hong An

Quantum steering ellipsoids (QSEs) provide a geometric representation, within the Bloch picture, of all possible states to which one qubit can be steered through measuring another correlated qubit. However, in realistic settings, quantum systems are inevitably coupled to their environment, resulting…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062458] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the protection of quantum steering ellipsoids from decoherence using non-Markovian environments.
motivation: Quantum steering ellipsoids provide a geometric representation of steerable states, but decoherence degrades them; understanding how non-Markovian effects can protect them is important for quantum information tasks.
method: The authors analyze the dynamics of quantum steering ellipsoids for two qubits under non-Markovian noise, using exact master equations or numerical simulations.
result: Non-Markovian environments can significantly suppress the degradation of steering ellipsoids compared to Markovian environments, preserving more steerability.
conclusion: Engineering non-Markovian environments may be a viable strategy to protect quantum steering resources in practical quantum information processing.

title: Identifying The Three-qubit $w$ State With The Quantum Uncertainty Relation
authors: Zhi-Jie Liu, Hao-Nan Qiang, Jie Zhou, Mi Xie, And Jing-Ling Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Zhi-Jie Liu, Hao-Nan Qiang, Jie Zhou, Mi Xie, and Jing-Ling Chen

The [MATH] state, a canonical representative of multipartite quantum entanglement, plays a crucial role in quantum information science due to its robust entanglement properties. Quantum uncertainty relations, on the other hand, form a fundamental cornerstone of quantum mechanics. This work introduces a…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062451] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses quantum uncertainty relations to identify the three-qubit W state, a canonical multipartite entangled state.
motivation: To provide a method for detecting and characterizing the W state using uncertainty relations, which are fundamental to quantum mechanics.
method: The authors derive an uncertainty relation based on certain observables and show that the W state saturates it, while other states do not.
result: They obtain a criterion that uniquely identifies the three-qubit W state among all pure states.
conclusion: Quantum uncertainty relations can serve as a tool for entanglement detection and state identification.

title: Anisotropic Second-harmonic Generation In Superconducting Nanostructures
authors: Sara Memarzadeh, Maciej Krawczyk, Armen Gulian, And Jarosław W. Kłos
abstract:
Author(s): Sara Memarzadeh, Maciej Krawczyk, Armen Gulian, and Jarosław W. Kłos

Circuits based on superconducting nanostructures are among the most promising platforms for quantum computing. Understanding how device geometry governs nonlinear electrodynamics is crucial for implementing superconducting quantum technologies. However, to date, research has largely been limited to …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245427] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies anisotropic second-harmonic generation in superconducting nanostructures, focusing on geometry-dependent nonlinear electrodynamics.
motivation: Understanding how device geometry governs nonlinear electrodynamics is crucial for implementing superconducting quantum technologies.
