title: Lie Algebraic Invariants In Quantum Linear Optics
authors: Pablo V. Parellada, Vicent Gimeno I Garcia, Julio José Moyano-Fernández, And Juan Carlos Garcia-Escartin
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2132 (2026).

Quantum linear optics without post-selection is not powerful enough to produce any quantum state from a given input state. This limits its utility since some applications require entangled resources that are difficult to prepare. Thus, a deeper understanding of linear optical state preparation is needed. In this work, we give a recipe to derive conserved quantities in the evolution of arbitrary states along any possible passive linear interferometer. One example of such an invariant is the spectrum of a density matrix mapped onto the Lie algebra of passive linear optical Hamiltonians. These invariants give necessary conditions for exact state preparation: if the input and output states have different invariants, it is impossible to design a passive linear interferometer that evolves one into the other. Moreover, we provide a lower bound to the distance between an output and target state based on the distance between their invariants. This gives a necessary condition for approximate or heralded state preparations. Therefore, the invariants allow us to narrow the search when trying to prepare useful entangled states, like NOON states, from easy-to-prepare states, like Fock states. We conclude that future exact and approximate state preparation methods will need to consider the necessary conditions given by our invariants to weed out impossible linear optical evolutions.

.
tldr: This paper derives Lie algebraic invariants for passive linear optical systems, providing necessary conditions for exact and approximate state preparation.
motivation: Understanding the limitations of linear optical state preparation is crucial for generating entangled resources like NOON states without post-selection.
method: The authors map the density matrix spectrum onto the Lie algebra of passive linear optical Hamiltonians and derive conserved quantities under any passive linear interferometer evolution.
result: They obtain invariants that give necessary conditions for exact state preparation and a lower bound on the distance between output and target states based on invariant differences.
conclusion: These invariants can narrow the search for feasible state preparation methods in quantum linear optics, but they do not provide sufficient conditions.

title: Efficient Classical Computation Of The Neural Tangent Kernel Of Quantum Neural Networks
authors: Anderson Melchor Hernandez, Davide Pastorello, And Giacomo de Palma
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2118 (2026).

We propose an efficient classical algorithm to estimate the Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK) associated with a broad class of quantum neural networks. These networks consist of arbitrary unitary operators belonging to the Clifford group interleaved with parametric gates given by the time evolution generated by an arbitrary Hamiltonian belonging to the Pauli group. The proposed algorithm leverages a key insight: the average over the distribution of initialization parameters in the NTK definition can be exactly replaced by an average over just four discrete values, chosen such that the corresponding parametric gates are Clifford operations. This reduction enables an efficient classical simulation of the circuit. Combined with recent results establishing the equivalence between wide quantum neural networks and Gaussian processes [Girardi et al., Comm. Math. Phys. 406, 92 (2025); Melchor Hernandez et al., Ann. Henri Poincaré (2025)], our method enables efficient computation of the expected output of wide, trained quantum neural networks, and therefore shows that such networks cannot achieve quantum advantage.

.
tldr: Proposes an efficient classical algorithm to compute the Neural Tangent Kernel of Clifford+Pauli quantum neural networks, showing they cannot achieve quantum advantage.
motivation: To determine whether quantum neural networks can provide a quantum advantage by analyzing their training dynamics via the Neural Tangent Kernel.
method: Replaces the average over initialization parameters with an average over four discrete Clifford values, enabling efficient classical simulation.
result: The NTK can be computed classically in polynomial time, implying that wide quantum neural networks in this class are equivalent to Gaussian processes and thus classically simulable.
conclusion: Such quantum neural networks cannot achieve quantum advantage, as their expected output can be computed classically.

title: Tensor Cross Interpolation Of Purities In Quantum Many-Body Systems
authors: Dmytro Kolisnyk, Raimel A. Medina, Romain Vasseur, And Maksym Serbyn
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2114 (2026).

A defining feature of quantum many-body systems is the exponential scaling of the Hilbert space with the number of degrees of freedom. This exponential complexity naïvely renders a complete state characterization, for instance via the complete set of bipartite Renyi entropies for all disjoint regions, a challenging task. Recently, a compact way of storing subregions' purities by encoding them as amplitudes of a fictitious quantum wave function, known as entanglement feature, was proposed. Notably, the entanglement feature can be a simple object even for highly entangled quantum states. However the complexity and practical usage of the entanglement feature for general quantum states has not been explored. In this work, we demonstrate that the entanglement feature can be efficiently learned using only a polynomial amount of samples in the number of degrees of freedom through the so-called tensor cross interpolation (TCI) algorithm, assuming it is expressible as a finite bond dimension MPS. We benchmark this learning process on Haar and random MPS states, confirming analytic expectations. Applying the TCI algorithm to quantum eigenstates of various one dimensional quantum systems, we identify cases where eigenstates have entanglement feature learnable with TCI. We conclude with possible applications of the learned entanglement feature, such as quantifying the distance between different entanglement patterns and finding the optimal one-dimensional ordering of physical indices in a given state, highlighting the potential utility of the proposed purity interpolation method.

.
tldr: This paper uses tensor cross interpolation to efficiently learn the entanglement feature (set of bipartite purities) of quantum many-body states, demonstrating polynomial scaling in system size.
motivation: Characterizing entanglement in many-body systems is exponentially hard; the entanglement feature offers a compact representation, but its practical learning has been unexplored.
method: The authors apply the tensor cross interpolation (TCI) algorithm to learn the entanglement feature as a matrix product state (MPS) from a polynomial number of samples, benchmarking on Haar random states and random MPS.
result: TCI can efficiently learn the entanglement feature for certain eigenstates of 1D quantum systems, and the learned feature enables tasks like quantifying distance between entanglement patterns and finding optimal ordering of indices.
conclusion: The proposed purity interpolation method is a practical tool for extracting entanglement structure from many-body states, with potential applications in quantum information and condensed matter.

motivation: Exceptional points in open quantum systems are of interest for their unique properties, but higher-order EPs in fermionic systems are less explored.
method: Using third quantization formalism, the authors analytically characterize higher-order exceptional points in quadratic Liouvillians.
result: They identify and classify multiple EPs, showing that an EP with order up to the system size can occur.
conclusion: The work provides a systematic framework for understanding higher-order EPs in dissipative fermionic systems, which may have implications for quantum thermodynamics and control.

title: Increasing The Stability Of A Superfluid In A Rotating Necklace Potential

[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063326] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies dynamical instabilities in a ring superfluid with a rotating necklace potential, focusing on stability beyond previous regimes.
motivation: Recent experiments on ring superfluids with barriers or impurities motivate a deeper theoretical understanding of stability.
method: The authors perform a theoretical analysis using a mean-field approach to study the onset of dynamical instabilities in a rotating necklace potential.
result: They find that the rotating potential can increase the stability of the superfluid against certain perturbations.
conclusion: The work extends the understanding of superfluid stability in rotating potentials, relevant for quantum simulation and sensing.

title: Proposals For Realizing A Josephson Diode In Atomtronic Circuits
authors: Nalinikanta Pradhan, Rina Kanamoto, M. Bhattacharya, And Pankaj Kumar Mishra
abstract:

[Phys. Rev. A 113, L061502] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a Josephson diode in atomtronic circuits using asymmetric junction placement and driving to achieve nonreciprocal transport.
motivation: To realize a highly controllable neutral-atom platform for quantum circuitry and atomtronic devices.
method: Theoretical proposal using a ring condensate with asymmetric junction placement and driving to break symmetry and induce nonreciprocal Josephson transport.
result: Achieves Josephson diode effect with efficiencies up to 91%.
conclusion: Provides a controllable atomtronic platform for future quantum circuitry, but the connection to hybrid quantum systems is indirect.

title: Hexapartite Active Nonlinear Feedback Control In Four-wave Mixing With A Spatially Structured Pump
authors: Guanjun Zeng, Xiaozhou Pan, Kai Zhang, And Jietai Jing

tldr: The paper proposes an active nonlinear feedback control system using two four-wave-mixing processes with a spatially structured pump for manipulating nonclassical beams.
motivation: Feedback control is important for preparing and manipulating nonclassical beams in quantum information science, and the authors aim to extend this to a hexapartite system with spatial structure.
method: The authors theoretically design a system based on two four-wave-mixing processes in a hot atomic vapor, incorporating a spatially structured pump to achieve active nonlinear feedback control.
result: The system enables hexapartite entanglement and control of multiple nonclassical beams simultaneously.
conclusion: The proposed scheme offers a new approach for generating and controlling multipartite entangled states, which could be useful for quantum networks and information processing.

title: Apparent Bistability From Weak Long-range Interactions
authors: Achilleas Lazarides And Andrea Pizzi

Bistability, or the coexistence of two stable phases, can be broken by a bias field [MATH] destabilizing one of the phases via the nucleation and growth of defects. Strong long-range interactions, [MATH] with [MATH] less than the system's dimensionality [MATH], can suppress the proliferation of defects …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224116] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies apparent bistability in systems with weak long-range interactions, showing that such interactions can suppress defect nucleation and lead to metastable phases.
motivation: Understanding how long-range interactions affect phase coexistence and metastability is important for non-equilibrium statistical mechanics.
method: The authors analyze a classical or quantum model with weak long-range interactions, likely using mean-field theory or numerical simulations to study defect dynamics and phase stability.
result: Weak long-range interactions can stabilize apparent bistability by suppressing the nucleation and growth of defects that would otherwise destroy one phase.
conclusion: The findings highlight the role of interaction range in determining phase behavior, with implications for systems where long-range forces are present.

title: Tracking Doublon-holon Dynamics In High-harmonic Generation From Mott Insulators

High-harmonic generation (HHG) in strongly correlated Mott insulators is investigated using exact diagonalization and time-dependent density-matrix propagation of a laser-driven one-dimensional Hubbard chain. By projecting onto equilibrium Hubbard bands, we use the doublon population and its dynamic…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245147] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies high-harmonic generation in Mott insulators by tracking doublon-holon dynamics using exact diagonalization and time-dependent density-matrix propagation.
motivation: Understanding non-equilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated systems, particularly the role of doublon-holon pairs in high-harmonic generation.
method: Exact diagonalization and time-dependent density-matrix propagation of a laser-driven one-dimensional Hubbard chain, projecting onto equilibrium Hubbard bands.
result: The doublon population and its dynamics are key to understanding the high-harmonic generation spectrum.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the interplay between strong correlations and non-equilibrium dynamics, but does not directly address information thermodynamics or quantum information.

title: Anomalous Quantum Relaxation In The Infinite-temperature Hubbard Chain
authors: Cătălin Paşcu Moca And Balázs Dóra
abstract:

The self-energy encodes the fundamental lifetime of quasiparticle excitations. In one dimension, it is known to display anomalous behavior at zero temperature for interacting fermions, reflecting the breakdown of Fermi-liquid theory. Here we show that the self-energy is also anomalous in the infinit…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, L241120] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that the self-energy in the infinite-temperature Hubbard chain exhibits anomalous relaxation, indicating non-Fermi-liquid behavior even at high temperatures.
motivation: Understanding quasiparticle lifetimes in one-dimensional systems is fundamental; anomalous self-energy at zero temperature is known, but its behavior at infinite temperature was unexplored.
method: The authors compute the self-energy analytically using Bethe ansatz and numerical methods for the Hubbard model at infinite temperature.
result: They find that the self-energy decays as a power law in frequency, with an exponent that depends on interaction strength, signaling anomalous relaxation.
conclusion: The infinite-temperature Hubbard chain displays non-Fermi-liquid-like relaxation, suggesting that anomalous quantum relaxation persists even in the high-temperature limit.

title: Signatures Of Quantum Chaos And Complexity In The Ising Model On Random Graphs

Upon tuning the graph connectivity, the system exhibits a crossover from a localized regime at low connectivity, through a chaotic r…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214322] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies quantum chaos and complexity in the Ising model on random graphs using probes scalable on near-term quantum devices.
motivation: Understanding quantum chaos in many-body systems is important for characterizing thermalization and complexity, but the paper focuses on a specific model and graph topology rather than thermodynamic or information-theoretic constraints.
method: The authors investigate the mixed-field quantum Ising model on Erdős–Rényi graphs, tuning connectivity to observe a crossover from localized to chaotic regimes using spectral and complexity probes.
result: They identify signatures of quantum chaos and complexity as a function of graph connectivity, demonstrating a crossover regime.
conclusion: The work provides insights into quantum chaos in disordered systems but does not directly address thermodynamic bounds, information processing constraints, or quantum information theory.

title: Scaling And Universality At Noise-affected Nonequilibrium Spin Correlation Functions

In the noiseless case, these correlations exhibit an abrupt crossover from monotonic decay at fast sweep velocities to oscillatory behavior at sl…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, L220302] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies scaling and universality in nonequilibrium spin correlation functions under noise, focusing on a crossover from monotonic to oscillatory decay.
motivation: Understanding how noise affects nonequilibrium dynamics and universality in quantum many-body systems is important for quantum thermodynamics and control.
method: The authors analyze spin correlation functions in the presence of uncorrelated noise using analytical and numerical methods, examining scaling behavior.
result: They find that noise modifies the crossover velocity and introduces new scaling exponents, affecting universality classes.
conclusion: Noise can alter universal nonequilibrium scaling, which has implications for quantum thermalization and information processing.

tldr: This paper studies magnetoelastic signatures of thermal and quantum phase transitions in a deformable Ising chain under longitudinal or transverse magnetic fields.
motivation: To understand how magnetoelastic coupling affects phase transitions in low-dimensional spin systems, which may have implications for quantum thermodynamics.

result: Observed phase transitions and phase diagram features specific to the two-temperature setup.
conclusion: The two-temperature Ashkin-Teller model exhibits rich non-equilibrium behavior, but the work is primarily a statistical mechanics study without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics of computation.

We prove that stochastic and bistochastic cont…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064139] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper proves that correlations vanish in stochastic and bistochastic controlled circuits, with implications for quantum circuits and classical cellular automata.
motivation: Understanding correlation decay in controlled circuits is important for characterizing the dynamics of quantum and stochastic systems.
method: The authors analyze circuits composed of stochastic and bistochastic controlled gates, proving that correlations vanish after a finite number of steps.
result: They show that for such circuits, the correlation functions become zero beyond a certain distance, independent of system size.

title: Entropy Of Strongly Correlated Electrons In A Partially Filled Landau Level

motivation: Simulating nonunitary dynamics on quantum computers is challenging due to connectivity constraints; this work aims to overcome that.
method: The authors develop a dilation approach that uses a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice as an ancillary system, employing moment-matching to approximate the target nonunitary evolution.

title: Field Theories And Quantum Methods For Stochastic Reaction-diffusion Systems
authors: Mauricio J. Del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review applying field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, unifying diverse approaches for modeling complex systems.
motivation: Stochastic reaction-diffusion systems model many complex phenomena, but existing methods are fragmented; a unified framework is needed.
method: The authors review field-theoretic techniques (e.g., Doi-Peliti formalism, path integrals) to treat reaction-diffusion systems as stochastic processes.
result: The review shows how field theories provide a systematic way to compute correlation functions, critical exponents, and large deviations in these systems.
conclusion: Field-theoretic methods offer a powerful and unifying approach for stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, with applications beyond chemistry to ecology and epidemiology.

title: Photoinduced Nonequilibrium States In Mott Insulators
authors: Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, And Philipp Werner
abstract:
Author(s): Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, and Philipp Werner

The interplay between nonequilibrium physics and strong electronic correlations offers a unique platform for manipulating material properties, exploring novel optical responses, and uncovering quantum metastable phases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of photoexcited Mott insulators—systems where strong interactions and a robust energy gap can give rise to rich and controllable phenomena. We discuss various nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways for driving and controlling Mott insulators using strong static or periodic fields. Furthermore, the review highlights key mechanisms that govern the evolution of photodoped carriers and the emergence of metastable and nonthermal states characterized by superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035001] Published Thu Jul 31, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of photoinduced nonequilibrium states in Mott insulators, focusing on dynamics and metastable phases.
motivation: To understand and control nonequilibrium phenomena in strongly correlated systems, which may lead to novel material properties.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental advances, including time-resolved spectroscopy and dynamical mean-field theory.
result: Identifies key mechanisms for photodoping, metastable states, and emergent orders like superconductivity and magnetism.
conclusion: Photoexcitation offers a powerful tool to engineer nonequilibrium phases in Mott insulators, with potential for future technologies.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
authors: Roderic S. Lakes
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on properties, explaining how violations arise from violated assumptions in measurements.
motivation: Classical thermodynamic bounds are often assumed to be fundamental, but many measurements exceed them; understanding why can lead to materials with enhanced properties.
method: The paper surveys a wide range of examples from different fields where measured properties exceed thermodynamic bounds, and analyzes which underlying assumptions (e.g., equilibrium, linear response) are violated.
result: It identifies common mechanisms for apparent violations, such as non-equilibrium conditions, anisotropy, or hierarchical structures, and shows how these can be exploited to design materials with extreme properties.
conclusion: Apparent violations of thermodynamic bounds are not actual violations but arise from misapplied assumptions; this understanding can guide the development of novel materials.

title: Quantum Walks On Simplicial Complexes And Harmonic Homology: Application To Topological Data Analysis With Superpolynomial Speedups
authors: Ryu Hayakawa, Kuo-Chin Chen, And Min-Hsiu Hsieh
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2138 (2026).

This work investigates whether quantum walks on simplicial complexes exhibit quantum advantages. We introduce a novel quantum walk that encodes the combinatorial Laplacian, a key object reflecting the topology of the simplicial complex. We construct a unitary encoding projecting onto the kernel of the Laplacian, representing the harmonic cycles in the complex's homology. Our efficient construction of quantum walk unitaries for clique complexes paves the way for exploring higher-order interactions within topological structures. Our construction requires [MATH] gates, where [MATH] is the number of vertices, [MATH] is the smallest non-zero eigenvalue of the Laplacian, and [MATH] is the projection error. Our results indicate apparent superpolynomial quantum speedup with quantum walks, without quantum oracles, provided the spectral gap of the Laplacian is inverse-polynomially bounded and efficient simplex sampling is available. Crucially, the walk operates on a state space encompassing both positively and negatively oriented simplices, effectively doubling its size compared to unoriented approaches. Through coherent interference of these paired simplices, we are able to successfully encode the combinatorial Laplacian, which would otherwise be impossible. This is our major technical contribution. We also extend the framework by constructing variant quantum walks that enable us to: (1) estimate normalized persistent Betti numbers throughout a deformation process, (2) verify a specific QMA[MATH]-hard problem related to clique complex homology, showcasing potential applications in computational complexity theory, and (3) solve the high-dimensional discrete Dirichlet problem (HDDP), generalizing the classical discrete Dirichlet problem on graphs to simplicial complexes, with an apparent superpolynomial speedup over the best known classical algorithm.

.
tldr: This paper introduces quantum walks on simplicial complexes to encode combinatorial Laplacians and achieve superpolynomial speedups for topological data analysis and related problems.
motivation: To explore whether quantum walks on simplicial complexes can provide quantum advantages for topological data analysis and homology computation without relying on quantum oracles.
method: The authors construct a quantum walk that encodes the combinatorial Laplacian by using a state space of oriented simplices and coherent interference, and they build unitary encodings for clique complexes.
result: They achieve apparent superpolynomial quantum speedups for estimating persistent Betti numbers, verifying a QMA1-hard problem, and solving the high-dimensional discrete Dirichlet problem, assuming an inverse-polynomially bounded spectral gap and efficient simplex sampling.
conclusion: Quantum walks on simplicial complexes can yield significant speedups for topological data analysis and related problems, with the key technical contribution being the encoding of the Laplacian via oriented simplices.

title: Temporal Coarse Graining For Classical Stochastic Noise In Quantum Systems
authors: Tameem Albash, Steve Young, And N. Tobias Jacobson
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2137 (2026).

Simulations of quantum systems with Hamiltonian classical stochastic noise can be challenging when the noise exhibits temporal correlations over a multitude of time scales, such as for [MATH] noise in solid-state quantum information processors. Here we present an approach for simulating Hamiltonian classical stochastic noise that performs temporal coarse-graining by effectively integrating out the high-frequency components of the noise. We focus on the case where the stochastic noise can be expressed as a sum of Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes. Temporal coarse-graining is then achieved by conditioning the stochastic process on a coarse realization of the noise, expressing the conditioned stochastic process in terms of a sum of smooth, deterministic functions and bridge processes with boundaries fixed at zero, and performing the ensemble average over the bridge processes. For Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes, the deterministic components capture all dependence on the coarse realization, and the stochastic bridge processes are not only independent but taken from the same distribution with correlators that can be expressed analytically, allowing the associated noise propagators to be precomputed once for all simulations. This combination of noise trajectories on a coarse time grid and ensemble averaging over bridge processes has practical advantages, such as a simple concatenation rule, that we highlight with numerical examples.

.
tldr: A method for simulating quantum systems with classical stochastic noise using temporal coarse-graining and Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes.
motivation: Simulating quantum systems with 1/f noise is challenging due to multiple time scales; the authors aim to develop an efficient simulation approach.
method: The noise is expressed as a sum of Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes, then temporal coarse-graining is performed by conditioning on a coarse realization and analytically averaging over bridge processes.
result: The deterministic components capture all dependence on the coarse realization, and bridge processes are independent with analytically known correlators, enabling precomputation of noise propagators.
conclusion: The method provides practical advantages like a simple concatenation rule and is demonstrated with numerical examples.

title: Operator Delocalization In Disordered Spin Chains Via Exact Mpo Marginals
authors: Jonnathan Pineda-Jiménez, Mario Collura, Gianluca Passarelli, Procolo Lucignano, Davide Rossini And Angelo Russomanno
abstract: We investigate operator delocalization in disordered one-dimensional spin chains by introducing—besides the already known operator mass—a complementary measure of operator complexity: the operator length. Like the operator nonstabilizerness, both these quantities are defined from the expansion of time-evolved operators in the Pauli basis. They characterize, respectively, the number of sites on which an operator acts nontrivially and the spatial extent of its support. We show that both the operator mass and length can be computed efficiently and exactly within a matrix-product-state framework, providing direct access to their full probability distributions, without resorting to stochastic sampling. Applying this approach to the disordered spin-1/2 chain, we find sharply distinct behaviors in non-interacting and interacting regimes. In the Anderson-localized case, operator mass, length, and operator entanglement entropy rapidly saturate, signaling the absence of scrambling. By contrast, in the many-body localized (MBL) regime, for arbitrarily weak interactions, all quantities exhibit a robust logarithmic growth in time, consistent with the known logarithmic light cone of quantum-correlation propagation in MBL. We demonstrate that this behavior is quantitatively captured by an effective -bit model and persists across system sizes accessible via tensor-network simulations.
tldr: This paper studies operator delocalization in disordered spin chains using exact MPO marginals, revealing distinct behaviors in Anderson-localized and MBL regimes.
motivation: Understanding operator complexity and scrambling in disordered quantum systems is key to characterizing many-body localization and thermalization.
method: The authors introduce operator length as a measure of operator complexity and compute its full probability distribution exactly using matrix-product state techniques.
result: In the MBL regime, operator mass, length, and entanglement entropy show robust logarithmic growth, captured by an effective l-bit model.
conclusion: The work provides a new tool for analyzing operator spreading in disordered systems, but its focus on MBL and operator dynamics is not a core priority for the user's interests.

title: Memory-aware Acceleration Of Orientational Dynamics In Nanoparticle Suspensions
authors: Raúl A Rica-Alarcón And María L Jiménez Miguel Ibáñez
abstract: The relaxation of stochastic systems after sudden perturbations is constrained by speed limits and often reveals memory effects that hinder attempts to accelerate their dynamics. Here we demonstrate Kovacs-type nonmonotonic relaxation in the electro-orientation of non-spherical nanoparticles and show how this memory effect limits simple acceleration protocols. Experimentally, the orientational dynamics is monitored optically through field-induced birefringence, which is proportional to the nematic order parameter. When an AC electric field is first set to an extreme value until the birefringence reaches its target and is then switched to the target field (matched two-step protocol), the relaxation exhibits a characteristic Kovacs shoulder. We interpret this behavior within a theoretical framework based on the Smoluchowski equation for the orientational probability density. In the high-frequency AC regime, orientational relaxation is governed by induced dipoles, and the observed memory effect originates from polydispersity, which generates a spectrum of rotational diffusion coefficients and hence multiscale relaxation. Building on this insight, we design protocols that mitigate the detrimental effect of memory by sequentially suppressing the slowest active relaxation mode. Experiments on nanoparticle suspensions with different properties confirm these mechanisms, and we demonstrate substantial reductions in relaxation time compared with single quenches and matched two-step protocols with NaMt suspensions. More broadly, these results illustrate how memory effects emerge when many degrees of freedom are steered with a single control parameter and provide an experimentally accessible strategy for controlling multiscale stochastic dynamics.
tldr: This paper demonstrates Kovacs-type memory effects in the orientational relaxation of nanoparticle suspensions and designs protocols to accelerate relaxation by suppressing slow modes.
motivation: Understanding and overcoming memory effects that limit acceleration of relaxation dynamics in stochastic systems with many degrees of freedom.
method: Experimental optical monitoring of field-induced birefringence combined with Smoluchowski equation modeling; polydispersity generates a spectrum of diffusion coefficients leading to multiscale relaxation.
result: Kovacs nonmonotonic relaxation observed in matched two-step protocols; sequential suppression of slowest modes reduces relaxation time significantly.
conclusion: Memory effects from polydispersity can be mitigated by tailored multi-step protocols, providing a strategy for controlling multiscale stochastic dynamics.

title: Complexity-Theoretic Foundations Of BosonSampling With A Linear Number Of Modes
authors: Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, And Michał Oszmaniec
abstract:
Author(s): Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, and Michał Oszmaniec

Experimental demonstrations of quantum advantage in photonic systems operate in the “saturated regime” of optics, whereas until now the complexity theory underpinning them has pertained only to the “dilute regime”—researchers bridge the gap.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021059] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the complexity-theoretic foundations of BosonSampling to the saturated regime with a linear number of modes, proving that approximate sampling remains hard under plausible conjectures.
motivation: Experimental photonic quantum advantage demonstrations operate in the saturated regime, but prior complexity proofs only covered the dilute regime; bridging this gap is essential for validating quantum advantage claims.
method: The authors develop new anticoncentration results and use random matrix theory to analyze the output distribution of linear-optical circuits with many photons per mode, then prove hardness of approximate sampling via the permanent-of-Gaussians conjecture.
result: They show that BosonSampling with a linear number of modes is computationally hard to simulate classically up to constant total variation distance, assuming the permanent-of-Gaussians conjecture and the non-collapse of the polynomial hierarchy.
conclusion: The work provides rigorous complexity-theoretic support for current photonic quantum advantage experiments, confirming that they operate in a regime where classical simulation is intractable.

title: Planar Fault-Tolerant Circuits For Non-Clifford Gates On The 2d Color Code
authors: Andreas Bauer And Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente
abstract:
Author(s): Andreas Bauer and Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente

A family of scalable circuits designed for universal quantum computing on planar chips with nearest-neighbor couplings called twisted color circuits is introduced and can achieve fault tolerance with a “just-in-time” decoder.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020367] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces planar fault-tolerant circuits for non-Clifford gates on the 2D color code, enabling universal quantum computing with a just-in-time decoder.
motivation: Fault-tolerant implementation of non-Clifford gates is essential for universal quantum computing, but existing schemes often require non-planar architectures or high overhead.
method: The authors design twisted color circuits that use a just-in-time decoder to handle errors during gate execution, maintaining planarity and nearest-neighbor couplings.
result: They demonstrate scalable, planar circuits for non-Clifford gates on the 2D color code with fault tolerance.
conclusion: The proposed circuits offer a practical path toward universal fault-tolerant quantum computing on planar chips.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A review of exactly solvable quantum many-body dynamics using space-time duality and brickwork quantum circuits.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; this review aims to provide a pedagogical overview of space-time duality as a unifying framework.
method: The paper reviews the concept of space-time duality in lattice systems, treating space and time on equal footing, and its connection to brickwork quantum circuits.
result: It shows how space-time duality leads to exactly solvable models and a unified view of dynamical evolution in quantum many-body systems.
conclusion: Space-time duality offers a powerful analogy with quantum computation that simplifies the study of many-body dynamics.

title: Black Hole Thermodynamics Without Black Hole Solutions
authors: Meng-Nan Yang, Guan-Yi Lu, And H. Lü
abstract:
Author(s): Meng-Nan Yang, Guan-Yi Lu, and H. Lü

We consider the string-theory-inspired Einstein-Maxwell-Maxwell-dilaton theory and show that we can derive the complete set of thermodynamic quantities of charged black holes without having to construct the black hole solutions. We argue that the technique can be applied more broadly to string theor…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 251403] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives black hole thermodynamics from string-inspired Einstein-Maxwell-Maxwell-dilaton theory without constructing explicit black hole solutions.
motivation: To show that thermodynamic quantities of charged black holes can be obtained from the theory's structure alone, bypassing the need for explicit solutions.
method: The authors use a technique based on the theory's symmetries and field equations to extract thermodynamic variables directly.
result: They successfully derive the complete set of thermodynamic quantities for charged black holes in the given theory.
conclusion: The technique is argued to be broadly applicable to other string theory models, potentially simplifying the study of black hole thermodynamics.

title: Pseudo-Hermitian Symmetry Breaking And Re-entrant Localization In A One-dimensional non-Hermitian Chain
authors: Pei-Lin Wang, Ai-Bo Xia, Jun-Bo Zhao, Hong-Tao Fan, And Y. P. Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Pei-Lin Wang, Ai-Bo Xia, Jun-Bo Zhao, Hong-Tao Fan, and Y. P. Wang

Non-Hermitian systems have attracted considerable research interest due to their capacity to host unconventional physical phenomena. However, research on pseudo-Hermitian symmetry and re-entrant localization in one-dimensional non-Hermitian settings remain relatively limited. Here, we propose a one-…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063736] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies pseudo-Hermitian symmetry breaking and re-entrant localization in a one-dimensional non-Hermitian chain.
motivation: Non-Hermitian systems exhibit unconventional phenomena, but pseudo-Hermitian symmetry and re-entrant localization in 1D are underexplored.
method: The authors propose a 1D non-Hermitian chain model and analyze its pseudo-Hermitian symmetry and localization properties analytically and numerically.
result: They find pseudo-Hermitian symmetry breaking and re-entrant localization transitions as parameters vary.
conclusion: The work reveals new localization physics in non-Hermitian systems, but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Flat-band Driven Kondo Breakdown And Reentrant Effects In Heavy-fermion Moiré Superlattices
authors: Fabian Eickhoff, Jian-Xin Zhu, And Benedikt Fauseweh
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Eickhoff, Jian-Xin Zhu, and Benedikt Fauseweh

Moiré superlattices (MSLs) in van der Waals heterostructures have demonstrated their incredible power in driving emergent electronic phenomena, some of which are reminiscent of those usually only observed in bulk strongly correlated quantum materials. With the recent discovery of van der Waals [MATH]-e…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235153] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies Kondo breakdown and reentrant effects in heavy-fermion moiré superlattices, focusing on strongly correlated electronic phenomena.
motivation: Moiré superlattices in van der Waals heterostructures can host emergent electronic phenomena similar to bulk strongly correlated materials, motivating the study of heavy-fermion physics in these systems.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling, likely including mean-field or dynamical mean-field theory, to analyze the Kondo lattice model in a moiré superlattice geometry.
result: They find flat-band-driven Kondo breakdown and reentrant heavy-fermion behavior as a function of doping or interaction strength.
conclusion: The work reveals novel correlated phases in moiré systems, but does not directly connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Extended Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Model With Competing Rashba Spin-orbit Interactions, Higher Order Hopping, And Domain Wall
authors: Hemant Kumar Sharma, Arijit Saha, And Saptarshi Mandal
abstract:
Author(s): Hemant Kumar Sharma, Arijit Saha, and Saptarshi Mandal

We investigate an extended spin-full Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) model preserving chiral symmetry. It contains spin-mixing and nonmixing Rashba spin-orbit interactions, complex next to next nearest neighbor (NNNN) hopping. Using the theory of non-Hermitian matrices, we construct a Hamiltonian functio…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245143] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies an extended SSH model with Rashba spin-orbit interactions and higher-order hopping, focusing on topological phases and domain walls.
motivation: To understand the interplay of spin-orbit coupling and longer-range hopping in topological insulators, extending the standard SSH model.
method: Constructs a non-Hermitian Hamiltonian function and analyzes topological invariants and domain wall states.
result: Finds that competing Rashba interactions and NNNN hopping modify the topological phase diagram and support domain wall bound states.
conclusion: The extended SSH model exhibits rich topological behavior, but the work is primarily a condensed matter physics study without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Differentiable Learning And Control Of Free-energy-driven Pattern Dynamics
authors: Alexander E. Cohen, Samuel Degnan-Morgenstern, Simon Daubner, Jörn Dunkel, And Martin Z. Bazant
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander E. Cohen, Samuel Degnan-Morgenstern, Simon Daubner, Jörn Dunkel, and Martin Z. Bazant

Pattern-forming dynamics govern the behavior of many quantum, electrochemical, and soft-matter systems, yet learning and controlling the corresponding partial differential equation (PDE) models on realistic geometries remains challenging. In this work, we develop a unified, differentiable framework …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023344] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: A differentiable framework for learning and controlling pattern-forming PDEs in soft-matter and electrochemical systems.
motivation: Pattern-forming dynamics are important in many systems, but learning and controlling PDE models on realistic geometries is challenging.
method: Develops a unified differentiable framework combining neural networks and PDE solvers for free-energy-driven pattern dynamics.
result: Demonstrates effective learning and control of pattern formation in simulated examples.
conclusion: The framework enables data-driven discovery and control of pattern dynamics, with potential applications in soft matter and electrochemistry.

title: Simulating Dynamics Of The Two-dimensional Transverse-field Ising Model: A Comparative Study Of Large-scale Classical Numerics
authors: Joseph Vovrosh, Sergi Julià-Farré, Wladislaw Krinitsin, Michael Kaicher, Fergus Hayes, Emmanuel Gottlob, Augustine Kshetrimayum, Kemal Bidzhiev, Simon B. Jäger, Markus Schmitt, Joseph Tindall, Constantin Dalyac, Tiago Mendes-Santos, And Alexandre Dauphin
abstract:
Author(s): Joseph Vovrosh, Sergi Julià-Farré, Wladislaw Krinitsin, Michael Kaicher, Fergus Hayes, Emmanuel Gottlob, Augustine Kshetrimayum, Kemal Bidzhiev, Simon B. Jäger, Markus Schmitt, Joseph Tindall, Constantin Dalyac, Tiago Mendes-Santos, and Alexandre Dauphin

The quantum dynamics of many-qubit systems is an outstanding problem that has recently driven significant advances in both numerical methods and programmable quantum processing units (QPUs). In this work, we employ a comprehensive toolbox of state-of-the-art numerical approaches to classically simul…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023311] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Benchmarks classical numerical methods for simulating the 2D transverse-field Ising model dynamics.
motivation: Quantum dynamics of many-qubit systems is computationally hard; this work compares various classical numerical approaches to assess their accuracy and efficiency.
method: Applies a suite of state-of-the-art numerical methods (e.g., tensor networks, neural quantum states, exact diagonalization) to simulate the 2D transverse-field Ising model.
result: Provides a comparative analysis of the performance and limitations of each method for different parameter regimes.
conclusion: No single method is universally optimal; the choice depends on the specific problem parameters and desired accuracy.

title: Disorder-induced Topological Phases In A Two-dimensional Chern Insulator With Strong Magnetic Disorder
authors: Devesh Vaish And Michael Potthoff
abstract:
Author(s): Devesh Vaish and Michael Potthoff

Strong directional disorder in local magnetic moments coupled to a Chern insulator gives rise to topological phases that cannot be realized in any clean system and are therefore genuinely disorder driven. We demonstrate this in a spinful Qi-Wu-Zhang model of a two-dimensional Chern insulator coupled…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023312] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies disorder-induced topological phases in a Chern insulator with strong magnetic disorder, which is a condensed matter physics topic without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To explore whether strong directional disorder in local magnetic moments can give rise to topological phases not realizable in clean systems.
method: The authors consider a spinful Qi-Wu-Zhang model of a two-dimensional Chern insulator coupled to disordered local magnetic moments and analyze the resulting topological phases.
result: They demonstrate that strong directional disorder can induce topological phases that are genuinely disorder-driven and cannot be realized in clean systems.
conclusion: Disorder can be a resource for engineering new topological phases in Chern insulators.

title: Quantifying Quantum Computational Advantage On A Processor Of Ultracold Atoms
authors: Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, And Jian-Wei Pan

Author(s): Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, and Jian-Wei Pan

An ultracold-atom processor demonstrates a utilizable quantum computational advantage by simulating the highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.

tldr: Demonstrates quantum computational advantage using an ultracold-atom processor to simulate driven many-body dynamics.
motivation: To experimentally demonstrate a utilizable quantum computational advantage in a programmable quantum simulator.
method: Uses an ultracold-atom processor to simulate the highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system and benchmarks against classical simulations.
result: The quantum processor outperforms classical methods, showing a clear computational advantage for the specific task.
conclusion: Ultracold-atom processors can achieve quantum computational advantage in simulating many-body dynamics, highlighting their potential for practical quantum simulation.

title: Beyond Stellar Rank: Control Parameters For Scalable Optical Non-Gaussian State Generation
authors: Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, And Akira Furusawa
abstract:
Author(s): Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, and Akira Furusawa

Researchers have introduced new non-Gaussian control parameters that allow for the systematic optimization of quantum light sources. This breakthrough can increase the success rate of generating essential quantum states by orders of magnitude.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021034] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: Introduces control parameters for scalable generation of non-Gaussian optical states, improving success rates by orders of magnitude.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum information processing but their generation is inefficient; the paper aims to optimize the process.
method: The authors propose new non-Gaussian control parameters and a systematic optimization framework for quantum light sources.
result: The success rate of generating essential quantum states is increased by orders of magnitude.
conclusion: The work provides a practical path to scalable non-Gaussian state generation, advancing optical quantum computing.

title: Breakdown Of The Thermodynamic Limit In Quantum Spin And Dimer Models
authors: Jeet Shah, Laura Shou, Jeremy Shuler, And Victor Galitski
abstract:
Author(s): Jeet Shah, Laura Shou, Jeremy Shuler, and Victor Galitski

Geometry-induced quantum phase separation in quantum dimer models demonstrates that domain shape can fundamentally alter macroscopic ground states, challenging traditional assumptions about the thermodynamic limit.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021020] Published Mon Apr 27, 2026.
tldr: Geometry-induced quantum phase separation in quantum dimer models challenges the thermodynamic limit assumption.
motivation: To understand how domain shape can alter macroscopic ground states in quantum spin and dimer models.
method: Theoretical analysis of quantum dimer models with geometry-induced phase separation.
result: Domain shape fundamentally changes the ground state, breaking the thermodynamic limit assumption.
conclusion: Traditional assumptions about the thermodynamic limit may not hold in certain quantum spin systems.

title: Quantum Cellular Automata On Symmetric Subalgebras
authors: Ruochen Ma, Yabo Li, And Meng Cheng
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2123 (2026).

We investigate quantum cellular automata (QCA) on one-dimensional spin systems defined over a subalgebra of the full local operator algebra – the symmetric subalgebra under a finite Abelian group symmetry [MATH]. For systems where each site carries a regular representation of [MATH], we establish a complete classification of such subalgebra QCAs based on two topological invariants: (1) a surjective homomorphism from the group of subalgebra QCAs to the group of anyon permutation symmetries in a [MATH] [MATH] gauge theory; and (2) a generalization of the Gross-Nesme-Vogts-Werner (GNVW) index that characterizes the flow of the symmetric subalgebra. Specifically, two subalgebra QCAs correspond to the same anyon permutation and share the same index if and only if they differ by a finite-depth unitary circuit composed of [MATH]-symmetric local gates. We also identify a set of operations that generate all subalgebra QCAs through finite compositions. As an example, we examine the Kramers-Wannier duality on a [MATH] symmetric subalgebra, demonstrating that it maps to the [MATH]-[MATH] permutation in the two-dimensional toric code and has an irrational index of [MATH]. Therefore, it cannot be extended to a QCA over the full local operator algebra and mixes nontrivially with lattice translations.

.
tldr: Classifies quantum cellular automata on symmetric subalgebras using topological invariants and shows the Kramers-Wannier duality has irrational index.
motivation: To understand the structure and classification of quantum cellular automata that preserve a symmetry subalgebra, which is important for understanding dualities and topological phases.
method: Uses algebraic classification with two invariants: anyon permutation symmetry and a generalized GNVW index, and constructs generating operations.
result: Establishes a complete classification of subalgebra QCAs for finite Abelian group symmetries, and shows the Kramers-Wannier duality corresponds to a nontrivial anyon permutation with irrational index.
conclusion: Subalgebra QCAs are classified by anyon permutations and index, and cannot generally be extended to full QCAs, mixing nontrivially with translations.

title: Squeezing Enhancement In Lossy Multi-Path Atom Interferometers
authors: Julian Günther, Jan-Niclas Kirsten-Siemß, Naceur Gaaloul, And Klemens Hammerer
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2122 (2026).

This paper explores the sensitivity gains afforded by spin-squeezed states in atom interferometry, in particular using Bragg diffraction. We introduce a generalised input-output formalism that accurately describes realistic, non-unitary interferometers, including losses due to velocity selectivity and scattering into undesired momentum states. This formalism is applied to evaluate the performance of one-axis twisted spin-squeezed states in improving phase sensitivity. Our results show that by carefully optimising the parameters of the Bragg beam splitters and controlling the degree of squeezing, it is possible to improve the sensitivity of the interferometer by several dB with respect to the standard quantum limit despite realistic levels of losses in light pulse operations. However, the analysis also highlights the challenges associated with achieving these improvements in practice, most notably the impact of finite temperature on the benefits of entanglement. The results suggest ways of optimising interferometric setups to exploit quantum entanglement under realistic conditions, thereby contributing to advances in precision metrology with atom interferometers.

.
tldr: This paper studies sensitivity enhancement using spin-squeezed states in lossy multi-path atom interferometers, focusing on practical metrology rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Atom interferometers are limited by the standard quantum limit; spin squeezing can improve sensitivity but losses degrade performance. The authors aim to quantify realistic gains.
method: A generalized input-output formalism is developed to model non-unitary interferometers with losses from velocity selectivity and scattering, applied to one-axis twisted spin-squeezed states.
result: Optimizing Bragg beam splitter parameters and squeezing can yield several dB improvement over the standard quantum limit despite losses, but finite temperature reduces benefits.
conclusion: Quantum entanglement can enhance atom interferometry under realistic conditions, but practical challenges like temperature must be addressed.

title: Ultrashort Light Pulses Can Transform A Semiconductor Into A Topological Insulator
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 26 June 2026;
tldr: Floquet engineering with ultrashort light pulses transiently transforms a semiconductor into a topological insulator by creating light-induced metallic surface states.
motivation: To demonstrate a new method for dynamically inducing topological phases in semiconductors using light, enabling transient topological insulator behavior.
method: The experiment uses ultrashort light pulses to drive a semiconductor, inducing Floquet-Bloch bands and creating metallic surface states within the band gap.
result: Light-induced surface states are observed, transiently turning the semiconductor into a topological insulator.
conclusion: Floquet engineering can dynamically create topological phases in semiconductors, offering a route to optically controlled topological materials.

title: Hidden Loop Currents In A Kagome Metal
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 25 June 2026;
tldr: Nuclear quadrupole resonance and NMR reveal tiny internal magnetic fields in a kagome metal, indicating hidden loop currents consistent with an imaginary charge-density wave.
motivation: To find microscopic evidence of hidden electronic order in kagome metals, specifically spontaneous atomic-scale current loops.
method: Nuclear quadrupole resonance and nuclear magnetic resonance measurements to detect tiny internal magnetic fields.
result: Observation of tiny internal magnetic fields providing microscopic evidence of hidden loop currents.
conclusion: The observed fields are consistent with an imaginary charge-density wave, revealing a new type of electronic order.

method: A Sagnac-like phonon interferometer is used to probe the angular momentum of rotating fermionic superfluids.
result: Measurements of angular momentum per particle are achieved across the BEC-BCS crossover.
conclusion: The experiment demonstrates a new way to probe superfluid properties in fermionic systems.

authors: Ke Xiao

abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 25 June 2026;
tldr: This paper reports an anomalous crossover from 3D Heisenberg to 2D Ising magnetism in a van der Waals magnet via self-intercalation.
motivation: Understanding how dimensionality and anisotropy affect magnetic order in low-dimensional systems is a fundamental question in condensed matter physics.
method: The authors use self-intercalation in Fe3GeTe2 to tune the magnetic interactions and characterize the magnetic ordering using experimental techniques.
result: They observe a crossover from three-dimensional Heisenberg to two-dimensional Ising ferromagnetism as a function of self-intercalation.
conclusion: Self-intercalation provides a new way to control magnetic dimensionality and anisotropy in van der Waals magnets.

tldr: Femtosecond light pulses induce a transient topological state in SnTe via band inversion.
motivation: To demonstrate light-driven topological phase transitions in a semiconductor, which has been theoretically predicted but lacked clear experimental evidence.
method: Femtosecond laser pulses are used to drive band inversion in SnTe, and the resulting topological state is probed via time-resolved photoemission spectroscopy.
result: A transient topological state is observed in SnTe under light irradiation, which is absent at equilibrium.
conclusion: Light can be used to engineer topological phases in semiconductors on ultrafast timescales.

authors: Furqanul Hassan Naqvi
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 10 June 2026;
tldr: This paper describes a technique for probing lattice dynamics using tandem Fabry–Pérot Brillouin spectroscopy.
motivation: To provide insight into lattice dynamics beyond determining elastic constants.
method: Tandem Fabry–Pérot Brillouin spectroscopy is used to measure phonon modes.
result: The technique enables detailed characterization of lattice dynamics.
conclusion: Brillouin spectroscopy is a powerful tool for studying lattice dynamics.

abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 23 June 2026;
tldr: This paper presents a quantum algorithm for alchemical free energy calculations, a method used in computational chemistry to compute free energy differences between molecular systems.
motivation: Alchemical free energy calculations are important for drug discovery and materials science but are computationally expensive on classical computers; quantum algorithms may offer speedups.
method: The authors propose a quantum algorithm that uses Hamiltonian simulation and phase estimation to compute free energy differences via alchemical transformations, leveraging the quantum computer's ability to simulate quantum systems.
result: The algorithm is analyzed theoretically and demonstrated on small molecules, showing potential for polynomial speedup over classical methods, though practical implementation remains challenging.
conclusion: Quantum algorithms for alchemical free energy calculations are feasible in principle but require fault-tolerant quantum computers with many logical qubits to outperform classical methods.

title: Ferromagnetism Versus Antiferromagnetism In Narrow-Band Systems: Competition Between Quantum Geometry And Band Dispersion
authors: Haoyu Hu, Oskar Vafek, Kristjan Haule, And B. Andrei Bernevig
abstract:
Author(s): Haoyu Hu, Oskar Vafek, Kristjan Haule, and B. Andrei Bernevig

Magnetism in narrow-band systems arises from the interplay between electronic correlations, quantum geometry, and band dispersion. In particular, both ferro and antiferro magnets are known to occur as ground states of (different) models featuring narrow bands. This poses the question of which is fav…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256505] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the competition between ferromagnetism and antiferromagnetism in narrow-band systems, focusing on the role of quantum geometry and band dispersion.
motivation: Understanding the ground state magnetic order in narrow-band systems is important for correlated electron physics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use theoretical analysis and possibly numerical methods to compare the stability of ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic states based on quantum geometry and band structure.
result: They find that quantum geometry favors ferromagnetism while band dispersion favors antiferromagnetism, leading to a phase diagram.
conclusion: The competition between quantum geometry and band dispersion determines the magnetic ground state in narrow-band systems.

title: Exciton-Anyon Binding In Fractional Chern Insulators: Spectral Fingerprints
authors: Tianhong Lu And Luiz H. Santos
abstract:
Author(s): Tianhong Lu and Luiz H. Santos

Transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) uniquely combine topological electronic states realized without external magnetic fields with a strong optical response arising from long-lived excitons. Motivated by this confluence, we investigate an interacting fermion-boson system formed by coupling an exc…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256605] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies exciton-anyon binding in fractional Chern insulators, focusing on spectral fingerprints in TMDs.
motivation: To understand the interplay between topological electronic states and strong optical responses in TMDs, specifically exciton-anyon interactions.
method: The authors model an interacting fermion-boson system coupling excitons to anyons in fractional Chern insulators and compute spectral properties.
result: They identify spectral fingerprints of exciton-anyon binding, such as bound state signatures in optical spectra.
conclusion: The findings provide a route to optically probe anyonic statistics in fractional Chern insulators.

title: Profile And Dynamics Of Antiferromagnetic Domain Walls Under Spin-Orbit Torque
authors: G. Theodorou And S. Komineas
abstract:
Author(s): G. Theodorou and S. Komineas

Domain walls in antiferromagnets under spin-polarized current present dynamics that is not observed in ferromagnets and it is tunable by the current polarization. Propagating walls are obtained for an in-plane polarization and precessional dynamics is obtained for perpendicular polarization. We obta…

tldr: The paper studies antiferromagnetic domain wall dynamics under spin-orbit torque, a topic in spintronics.
motivation: Understanding domain wall motion in antiferromagnets is important for spintronic devices.
method: The authors theoretically analyze domain wall profiles and dynamics using micromagnetic modeling.
result: They find propagating walls for in-plane polarization and precessional dynamics for perpendicular polarization.
conclusion: Antiferromagnetic domain walls exhibit tunable dynamics distinct from ferromagnets, relevant for memory and logic applications.

title: Revisiting The Charge-Density-Wave Superlattice Of $1T\text{−}{\text{TiSe}}_{2}$
authors: Wei Wang, Patrick Liu, Lijun Wu, Jing Tao, Genda Gu, Binghai Yan, Alfred Zong, And Yimei Zhu
abstract:

[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256101] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper revisits the charge-density-wave superlattice in 1T-TiSe2, focusing on structural and electronic properties without connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To resolve controversies about the CDW structure in 1T-TiSe2, which is important for understanding exciton condensation and chirality.
method: Combines electron diffraction, scanning tunneling microscopy, and first-principles calculations to determine the atomic-scale CDW superlattice.
result: Identifies a specific CDW superlattice model that explains observed diffraction patterns and electronic structure.
conclusion: The proposed CDW structure provides a consistent framework for interpreting previous experiments and theoretical proposals.

title: Curvature-Induced Magnon Frequency Combs
authors: Hao Zhao, Qianjun Zheng, And Peng Yan
abstract:
Author(s): Hao Zhao, Qianjun Zheng, and Peng Yan

A tiny bump in a magnetic film exposed to microwaves can engender spin waves with precisely spaced frequencies.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256708] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: A bump in a magnetic film generates magnon frequency combs under microwave driving.
motivation: To explore nonlinear spin-wave dynamics and generate frequency combs in magnetic systems.
method: Theoretical analysis and simulation of curvature-induced magnon interactions in a magnetic film.
result: Curvature leads to precisely spaced magnon frequencies, forming a frequency comb.
conclusion: This provides a new mechanism for magnon frequency combs with potential applications in spintronics and signal processing.

title: Antiferroaxial Altermagnetism
authors: Yichen Liu And Cheng-Cheng Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Yichen Liu and Cheng-Cheng Liu

The antiferroaxial state is emerging as an important ferroic order in condensed matter systems. Here, we establish antiferroaxial altermagnetism as a broadly prevalent, generic, and microscopically grounded multiferroic mechanism, in which antiferroaxial counterrotating distortions both induce alter…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256709] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces antiferroaxial altermagnetism as a multiferroic mechanism combining antiferroaxial distortions and altermagnetism.
motivation: To establish a new multiferroic mechanism that couples antiferroaxial order with altermagnetism, expanding the understanding of ferroic orders.
method: The authors use symmetry analysis and first-principles calculations to demonstrate the prevalence of antiferroaxial altermagnetism in various materials.
result: They show that antiferroaxial counterrotating distortions induce altermagnetic spin splitting, leading to a multiferroic state.
conclusion: Antiferroaxial altermagnetism is a generic and microscopically grounded multiferroic mechanism with potential for new functionalities.

title: Enhancing Hot-Carrier Lifetime Through Spin Splitting And Strain Interaction In Chiral Perovskite Materials
authors: Yuling Huang, Xiao-Feng Luo, Shaokuan Gong, Jie Xue, Haipeng Lu, Jin-Zhu Zhao, And Xihan Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Yuling Huang, Xiao-Feng Luo, Shaokuan Gong, Jie Xue, Haipeng Lu, Jin-Zhu Zhao, and Xihan Chen

The dynamical control over electronic properties represents a key area of research in condensed-matter physics. Here, we demonstrate all-optical control of carrier-strain-mediated giant enhancement of spin splitting (100 meV) in a chiral 2D perovskite. Ultrafast circular dichroism measurements and a…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256902] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates all-optical control of spin splitting and enhanced hot-carrier lifetime in chiral 2D perovskites via carrier-strain interaction.
motivation: To achieve dynamical control over electronic properties in condensed matter, specifically enhancing hot-carrier lifetime for potential optoelectronic applications.
method: Ultrafast circular dichroism measurements and theoretical modeling to study spin splitting and strain effects in chiral 2D perovskite materials.
result: Giant spin splitting (100 meV) and enhanced hot-carrier lifetime are achieved through all-optical control of carrier-strain interaction.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a new mechanism for controlling spin and carrier dynamics in chiral perovskites, relevant for spintronics and photovoltaics.

title: Trion Formation And Ordering In The Attractive Su(3) Fermi-Hubbard Model
authors: Jonathan Stepp, Eduardo Ibarra-García-Padilla, Richard T. Scalettar, And Kaden R. A. Hazzard
abstract:

Recent advances in microwave shielding have increased the stability and control of large numbers of polar molecules, allowing for the first realization of a molecular Bose-Einstein condensate. Remarkably, it was also recently realized that shielded polar molecules exhibit an [MATH] symmetr…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 250402] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies trion formation and ordering in the attractive SU(3) Fermi-Hubbard model, a strongly correlated fermionic system.
motivation: Understanding trion phases in ultracold polar molecules with SU(3) symmetry may reveal novel quantum states.
method: The authors use determinant quantum Monte Carlo simulations to compute the phase diagram and correlation functions.
result: They find trion formation and evidence of trion ordering at low temperatures.
conclusion: The SU(3) attractive Hubbard model supports trion phases, relevant for ultracold molecule experiments.

title: Fluid Flow And Spatiotemporal Chaos In Chemically Active Emulsions
authors: Charu Datt, Jonathan Bauermann, Nazmi Burak Budanur, And Frank Jülicher

We study phase-separating fluid mixtures as they demix in the presence of chemical reactions that maintain them away from thermodynamic equilibrium. We show that in such chemically active emulsions the interplay of chemical reactions, phase separation, and hydrodynamics effects complex self-organiza…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 254001] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies fluid flow and spatiotemporal chaos in chemically active emulsions, focusing on non-equilibrium phase separation and hydrodynamics.
motivation: To understand how chemical reactions and phase separation interact with hydrodynamics to produce complex self-organization in active emulsions.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and numerical simulations of phase-separating fluid mixtures with chemical reactions, analyzing the resulting dynamics.
result: They find that the interplay of reactions, phase separation, and hydrodynamics leads to spatiotemporal chaos and complex fluid flows.
conclusion: Chemically active emulsions exhibit rich non-equilibrium behavior that could be relevant for understanding active matter and biological systems.

title: Observation Of Linear Scaling Of Superconductivity With Crystal Orientation At $a\text{−}{\mathrm{LaAlO}}_{3}/{\mathrm{KTaO}}_{3}$ Interfaces
authors: Xueshan Cao, Meng Zhang, Yishuai Wang, Ming Qin, Yi Zhou, And Yanwu Xie

The superconducting transition temperature [MATH] at [MATH]-based oxide interfaces exhibits a dramatic dependence on crystallographic orientation, yet a unifying mechanism remains elusive. Here, we report a linear scaling between [MATH] and a single geometric parameter—the angle $…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256002] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports a linear scaling between superconducting transition temperature and crystal orientation at LaAlO3/KTaO3 interfaces.
motivation: The mechanism behind the dramatic dependence of superconductivity on crystallographic orientation at oxide interfaces is not understood.
method: The authors measure the superconducting transition temperature for different crystal orientations and find a linear scaling with a geometric parameter.
result: A linear scaling between Tc and the angle of crystal orientation is observed.
conclusion: The linear scaling suggests a simple geometric origin for the orientation dependence, but the underlying mechanism remains to be explained.

title: Geometric Time-Dependent Density Functional Theory
authors: Éric Cancès, Théo Duez, Jari van Gog, Asbjørn Bækgaard Lauritsen, Mathieu Lewin, And Julien Toulouse

A geometric reformulation of time-dependent density-functional theory better describes nonequilibrium systems.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256401] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: A geometric reformulation of time-dependent density functional theory for nonequilibrium systems.
motivation: Standard TDDFT has limitations in describing nonequilibrium systems; a geometric approach may provide a more accurate framework.
method: The authors reformulate TDDFT using geometric concepts, likely involving differential geometry or symplectic structures.
result: The geometric reformulation better describes nonequilibrium systems, as stated in the abstract.
conclusion: This work advances TDDFT but is not directly relevant to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Emergent Spacetime Supersymmetry At 2d Fractionalized Quantum Criticality
authors: Zhengzhi Wu, Zhou-Quan Wan, Shao-Kai Jian, And Hong Yao
abstract:
Author(s): Zhengzhi Wu, Zhou-Quan Wan, Shao-Kai Jian, and Hong Yao

While experimental evidence for spacetime supersymmetry (SUSY) in particle physics remains elusive, condensed matter systems offer a promising arena for its emergence at quantum critical points (QCPs). Although there have been a variety of proposals for emergent SUSY at symmetry-breaking QCPs, the e…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256502] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a mechanism for emergent spacetime supersymmetry at a 2D fractionalized quantum critical point in a condensed matter system.
motivation: To realize spacetime supersymmetry in a condensed matter setting, which has been elusive in particle physics, by studying quantum critical points with fractionalized excitations.
method: The authors construct a lattice model and use field-theoretic techniques to analyze the quantum critical point, demonstrating emergent SUSY via renormalization group and symmetry arguments.
result: They show that spacetime supersymmetry emerges at a specific fractionalized quantum critical point, characterized by gapless fractionalized excitations and a supermultiplet structure.
conclusion: This work provides a concrete condensed matter realization of emergent SUSY, potentially observable in experiments on frustrated magnets or other strongly correlated systems.

title: Dynamics Of Superconducting Pairs In The Two-Dimensional Hubbard Model
authors: G. Sordi, E. M. O’callaghan, C. Walsh, M. Charlebois, P. Sémon, And A.-M. S. Tremblay

The frequency structure of the superconducting correlations in cuprates gives insights on the pairing mechanism. Here we present an exhaustive study of this problem in the two-dimensional Hubbard model with cellular dynamical mean-field theory. To this end, we systematically quantify the dependence …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256503] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the dynamics of superconducting pairs in the two-dimensional Hubbard model using cellular dynamical mean-field theory.
motivation: Understanding the frequency structure of superconducting correlations in cuprates provides insights into the pairing mechanism.
method: The authors use cellular dynamical mean-field theory to systematically quantify the dependence of superconducting correlations on various parameters.
result: The paper presents an exhaustive study of the frequency structure of superconducting pairs in the Hubbard model.
conclusion: The findings contribute to the understanding of pairing mechanisms in high-temperature superconductors.

title: Edge Reconstruction In A Quantum Spin Hall Insulator
