For a two-dimensional…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256504] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies interaction-driven edge reconstruction in a quantum spin Hall insulator using DMRG, focusing on the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang model with Kanamori-Hubbard interactions.
motivation: Understanding edge reconstruction in quantum spin Hall insulators is important for characterizing topological phases, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use real-space density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) in both grand-canonical and canonical ensembles to simulate a two-dimensional system.
result: They observe interaction-driven edge reconstruction in the quantum spin Hall insulator.
conclusion: The work provides insights into edge physics of topological insulators but does not advance quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Ultrafast Magneto-Optical Fingerprints Of Altermagnetism In MnTe
authors: Xu Yang, Xingkai Cheng, Zhuo Deng, Yu-Han Gao, Qing-Lin Yang, Zheng Chang, Peng-Tao Yang, Hong-Mei Feng, Xiang-Qun Zhang, Wei He, Junwei Liu, And Zhao-Hua Cheng
abstract:

Recently identified altermagnets exhibit a distinctive dual-space nature: they possess spin-split electronic bands akin to ferromagnets in momentum space while maintaining the fully compensated magnetization of antiferromagnets in real space. This inherent duality, originating from the same crystal …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256702] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports ultrafast magneto-optical fingerprints of altermagnetism in MnTe, a condensed matter physics study of a novel magnetic phase.
motivation: Altermagnets are a recently identified class of magnetic materials with spin-split bands but zero net magnetization, and their ultrafast dynamics are unexplored.
method: The authors use time-resolved magneto-optical Kerr effect (TR-MOKE) spectroscopy to probe the spin dynamics in MnTe thin films.
result: They observe distinct ultrafast magneto-optical signatures that are attributed to the altermagnetic order, distinguishing it from conventional antiferromagnets.
conclusion: The findings establish ultrafast magneto-optics as a tool to identify and study altermagnetic materials, opening a new direction in spintronics.

title: Hearing The Light: Stray-Field Noise From The Emergent Photon In Quantum Spin Ice
authors: Gautam K. Naik, Jonathan N. Hallén, Nishan C. Jayarama, Roderich Moessner, And Chris R. Laumann

Decisive experimental confirmation of the U(1) quantum spin liquid phase in quantum spin ice remains an outstanding challenge. In this Letter, we propose stray-field magnetometry as a direct probe of the emergent photons—the gapless excitation of the emergent electrodynamics in quantum spin ice. The…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256705] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes stray-field magnetometry as a probe of emergent photons in quantum spin ice, a condensed matter system.
motivation: Decisive experimental confirmation of U(1) quantum spin liquid in quantum spin ice remains challenging; the authors aim to provide a direct probe of the emergent photon excitation.
method: Theoretical analysis of stray-field noise from emergent electrodynamics in quantum spin ice, proposing magnetometry as a detection method.
result: Stray-field magnetometry can detect signatures of the emergent photon, offering a potential experimental route to confirm quantum spin ice.
conclusion: Stray-field magnetometry is a promising tool for probing emergent photons in quantum spin ice, aiding in the experimental verification of quantum spin liquids.

title: Block-Type Antiferromagnetism In Single Chain Quasi-One-Dimensional ${\mathrm{K}}_{3}{\mathrm{Fe}}_{2}{\mathrm{Se}}_{4}$

tldr: This paper reports an unusual block-type antiferromagnetic order in a quasi-one-dimensional iron chalcogenide, studied via neutron scattering and theoretical modeling.
motivation: To understand the magnetic properties of quasi-1D iron chalcogenides, which may host unconventional magnetism and superconductivity.
method: Single-crystal neutron diffraction and first-principles calculations were used to determine the magnetic structure and exchange interactions.
result: A block-type antiferromagnetic order with alternating ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic blocks along the chain was observed.
conclusion: The findings reveal a novel magnetic state in 1D systems, highlighting the rich physics of low-dimensional iron-based materials.

title: Close Proximity To A Quantum Phase Transition In ${\mathrm{TmZn}}_{2}{\mathrm{GaO}}_{5}$
authors: Matthew Ennis, Rabindranath Bag, Tessa Cookmeyer, Matthew B. Stone, Alexander I. Kolesnikov, Tao Hong, Leon Balents, And Sara Haravifard

tldr: This paper reports the synthesis and characterization of a triangular lattice magnet TmZn2GaO5, which exhibits a quantum phase with strong Ising anisotropy and a gapped excitation, suggesting proximity to a quantum phase transition.
motivation: To discover and understand new quantum materials that may host exotic magnetic phases, particularly those near quantum critical points.
method: Neutron scattering and thermodynamic measurements on single crystals of TmZn2GaO5, combined with theoretical modeling.
result: The material shows a pseudodoublet ground state, strong Ising anisotropy, and a low-energy gapped excitation at the M point, indicating it is close to a quantum phase transition.
conclusion: TmZn2GaO5 is a promising platform for studying quantum criticality in frustrated magnets, but the work is primarily a materials characterization without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Geometric Representation Of Higher-order Optical Modes
authors: Claire Cisowski
abstract:
Author(s): Claire Cisowski

The author presents an octant geometric framework that maps higher-order, three-state optical modes onto the positive surface of a sphere spanned by a torus. [Phys. Rev. A 113, 063530] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: Presents a geometric framework for representing higher-order optical modes on a sphere, extending the Poincaré sphere concept.
motivation: Standard Poincaré sphere representations are limited to two-dimensional subspaces; a full parametrization of three-state optical modes is needed.
method: Develops an octant geometric framework mapping higher-order three-state optical modes onto the positive surface of a sphere spanned by a torus.
result: The parametrization covers the entire state space of structured light modes except for isolated coordinate singularities.
conclusion: The geometric representation provides a complete description of higher-order optical modes, useful for structured light applications.

title: Quantum Image Encodings For Noisy Intermediate-scale Quantum Devices: A Comprehensive Performance And Noise-resilience Analysis
authors: Emmanuel Martínez-Guerrero, Guo-Hua Sun, And Shi-Hai Dong
abstract:
Author(s): Emmanuel Martínez-Guerrero, Guo-Hua Sun, and Shi-Hai Dong

Quantum image processing relies on the efficient encoding of classical image data into quantum states, yet the practical performance of existing encoding schemes on noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) hardware remains insufficiently understood. Most prior studies have emphasized asymptotic resou…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062456] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper benchmarks quantum image encoding schemes on NISQ devices, focusing on noise resilience and resource efficiency.
motivation: Quantum image processing requires efficient encoding of classical images into quantum states, but the performance of existing encodings on noisy hardware is not well understood.
method: The authors implement and compare several encoding schemes (e.g., FRQI, NEQR, QPIE) on IBM Q and other NISQ devices, measuring fidelity, circuit depth, and noise resilience.
result: They find that simpler encodings like QPIE are more noise-resilient but less expressive, while more complex encodings suffer from high error rates on current hardware.
conclusion: No single encoding is optimal; the choice depends on the specific application and noise level, and further hardware improvements are needed for practical quantum image processing.

title: Optimal Displacement Detection Of Arbitrarily Shaped Levitated Dielectric Objects Using Optical Radiation

motivation: To improve precision force and acceleration sensing by extending levitated optomechanics to nonspherical geometries.
method: The authors derive analytical expressions for the optimal detection signal-to-noise ratio using the dipole approximation and consider the effects of object shape and orientation.
result: They find that nonspherical objects can provide enhanced displacement sensitivity compared to spherical ones under certain conditions.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for optimizing detection in levitated optomechanics with arbitrary shapes, which may benefit sensing applications.

title: Phase-space Open-system Dynamics Of Second-order Nonlinear Interactions With Pulsed Quantum Light
authors: Emanuel Hubenschmid And Victor Rueskov Christiansen

motivation: Modeling broadband quantum pulses in nonlinear media is complex due to high dimensionality; the authors aim to simplify by identifying relevant temporal modes.
method: They use a phase-space representation (e.g., Wigner function) and derive master equations for the reduced dynamics of the relevant modes, accounting for losses and noise.
result: The method captures the open-system evolution of pulsed quantum light in second-order nonlinear processes, demonstrating how to compute output states efficiently.
conclusion: The phase-space approach provides a tractable framework for simulating quantum optical systems with many modes, relevant for quantum information processing with continuous variables.

title: Geometric Theory Of Constrained Schrödinger Dynamics With Application To Time-dependent Density-functional Theory On A Finite Lattice
authors: Éric Cancès, Théo Duez, Jari van Gog, Asbjørn Bækgaard Lauritsen, Mathieu Lewin, And Julien Toulouse

tldr: This paper develops a geometric theory of constrained Schrödinger dynamics and applies it to time-dependent density-functional theory on a finite lattice.
motivation: The mathematical foundations of time-dependent density-functional theory (TDDFT) are not fully understood, especially for finite-dimensional systems.
method: The authors formulate the dynamics of the one-body density matrix under a time-dependent Hamiltonian as a constrained evolution on a Grassmann manifold, using tools from differential geometry.
result: They derive a geometric characterization of the mapping from time-dependent potentials to densities and prove conditions for the existence of a unique potential for a given density trajectory.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous mathematical framework for TDDFT on finite lattices, clarifying the conditions under which the density-potential mapping is invertible.

title: Systematic Errors From Inhomogeneous Alkali-spin Polarization In Nmr Gyroscopes And Comagnetometers

motivation: Isotope shift due to alkali polarization field is a major source of systematic error in comagnetometer studies, limiting their accuracy.
method: The authors model the spin-exchange collisions between Xe and alkali-metal atoms and derive the effect of inhomogeneous polarization on the measured signal.
result: They quantify the isotope shift error and show how it depends on experimental parameters.
conclusion: Understanding and mitigating this error is crucial for improving the performance of NMR gyroscopes and comagnetometers.

title: Structures And Proximity Effects Of Inhomogeneous Population-imbalanced Fermi Gases With Pairing Interactions

motivation: To understand how spatially varying pairing interactions or spin polarization affect phase coexistence in quasi-one-dimensional Fermi gases.
method: The authors implement Bogoliubov–de Gennes theory to analyze ground-state structures of two-component atomic Fermi gases in box potentials with spatially varying profiles.
result: They identify multiple coexisting phases and characterize their properties as functions of interaction and polarization profiles.
conclusion: The work provides insights into inhomogeneous superfluidity and phase separation in Fermi gases, relevant to ultracold atom experiments.

title: Atom-chip Interferometer

result: Interference fringes are observed, demonstrating the feasibility of the chip-based interferometer.

title: Gaussian Mode Coupling Of Spectrally Broadband Photons From Bulk Spontaneous Parametric Down-conversion: A Spatial-spectral Mode Analysis Of Fiber Coupling

Photon sources based on spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) are central to experimental quantum optics and quantum technologies. [Phys. Rev. A 113, 063733] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes the spatial-spectral mode coupling of broadband photons from bulk SPDC into single-mode fibers, focusing on optimizing pair-collection probability, heralding efficiency, and spectral purity.
motivation: Efficient fiber coupling of SPDC photons is crucial for quantum optics experiments and quantum technologies, but broadband photons suffer from mode dispersion that degrades performance.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model that couples the spatial and spectral degrees of freedom of SPDC photons, analyzing how the pump beam parameters and crystal properties affect the fiber-coupling efficiency and spectral purity.
result: They find that by carefully choosing the pump focusing and crystal length, one can simultaneously achieve high heralding efficiency and high spectral purity, despite the broadband nature of the photons.
conclusion: The work provides practical guidelines for designing SPDC sources with optimal fiber-coupling performance, which is important for quantum communication and networking applications.

title: Many-body Wave Function And Edge Magnetization Of An Open $p+is$ Superconducting Chain

[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224525] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper constructs the exact BCS ground-state wave function for an open p+is superconducting chain and studies its edge magnetization.
motivation: BCS wave functions under open boundary conditions are nontrivial but important for understanding edge properties of topological superconductors.
method: The authors derive the exact many-body wave function using a Bogoliubov transformation and solve the resulting BdG equations for the open chain.
result: They obtain an explicit form of the ground state and compute the edge magnetization, revealing topological edge modes.
conclusion: The work provides a rare exact solution for a superconducting chain with open boundaries, clarifying edge physics in p+is superconductors.

title: Orbital Magnetization Reveals Multiband Topology

motivation: To understand how topological properties of electronic wave functions manifest in measurable quantities like orbital magnetization.
method: Decomposes orbital magnetization into energetic and quantum-geometric contributions and relates them to multiband topological invariants.
result: Nontrivial multiband topology can be revealed through orbital magnetization responses to external magnetic fields.
conclusion: Orbital magnetization provides a probe for multiband topological order in condensed matter systems.

conclusion: MgMn6Ge6 is a promising platform for studying topological transport in kagome magnets.

title: Strain-driven Antiferroelastic Switching Of Altermagnetism
authors: Fanjunjie Han, Shuaihao Tang, Jian-Dong Sun, Xin-Gang Zhao, And Haiyang Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Fanjunjie Han, Shuaihao Tang, Jian-Dong Sun, Xin-Gang Zhao, and Haiyang Xu

Altermagnetism, characterized by pronounced momentum-space spin splitting without net magnetization, provides an emerging platform for spintronics. Yet nonvolatile control of its spin states remains a key challenge for device application. Here, we demonstrate that antiferroelastic lattice distortion…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214457] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates nonvolatile control of altermagnetism via antiferroelastic lattice distortion, enabling reversible switching of spin splitting.
motivation: Nonvolatile control of altermagnetic spin states is crucial for spintronic device applications but remains a key challenge.
method: The authors use first-principles calculations to show that antiferroelastic distortion in a candidate altermagnet can switch the momentum-space spin splitting.
result: They achieve reversible switching of altermagnetism by applying strain to induce antiferroelastic transitions.
conclusion: Strain-driven antiferroelastic switching provides a pathway for nonvolatile control of altermagnetic states, advancing spintronics.

title: Loss/gain-induced Hall Effect Of Vortex Light
authors: Yucheng Lai, Yongliang Zhang, And Kai Chang
abstract:

The Hall effect provides a route for unidirectional manipulations of classical and quantum waves. In optics, the spin Hall effect (SHE) induced by the interaction between intrinsic angular momentum (AM) and material inhomogeneity enables AM-dependent control of light at the subwavelength scale. Desp…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245309] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports a loss/gain-induced Hall effect for vortex light in optical systems, analogous to the spin Hall effect but for orbital angular momentum.
motivation: To explore how non-Hermitian effects (loss/gain) can induce a Hall effect for vortex light, enabling unidirectional control of light carrying orbital angular momentum.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a photonic system with loss/gain gradients, deriving the equations of motion for vortex light and demonstrating a transverse deflection analogous to the Hall effect.
result: They show that loss/gain gradients can induce a Hall effect for vortex light, leading to a separation of beams with opposite orbital angular momentum.
conclusion: This work extends the concept of the Hall effect to vortex light in non-Hermitian systems, offering new possibilities for manipulating light with orbital angular momentum.

motivation: To discover new multiferroic materials with coexisting ferromagnetism, ferroelectricity, and Berry curvature dipole for potential spintronic applications.

title: Collective Phonon Mixing And Eigenvector Transport Under Isotope Substitution
authors: Jeff Armstrong, Hamish Cavaye, Pankaj Sharma, And Matthew E. Potter
abstract:
Author(s): Jeff Armstrong, Hamish Cavaye, Pankaj Sharma, and Matthew E. Potter

Isotopic substitution modifies nuclear masses without altering the electronic potential-energy surface to first order and is therefore often interpreted as a simple rescaling of vibrational frequencies. In solids with dense phonon manifolds, however, mass substitution acts as a parametric Hermitian …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214325] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how isotopic substitution modifies phonon modes and eigenvector transport in solids with dense phonon manifolds.
motivation: Isotopic substitution is often assumed to simply rescale vibrational frequencies, but in dense phonon manifolds it can cause more complex effects like mode mixing and eigenvector transport.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and simulations to analyze the parametric Hermitian perturbation induced by mass substitution in a solid with many phonon branches.
result: They find that isotopic substitution leads to collective phonon mixing and transport of eigenvectors across the phonon spectrum, beyond simple frequency rescaling.
conclusion: The work highlights that isotopic effects in solids with dense phonon manifolds are nontrivial and must be accounted for in interpreting vibrational spectra.

title: Stacking Theory For Bilayer Two-dimensional Magnets

motivation: To understand how stacking configurations in bilayer 2D magnets can induce unconventional magnetic phases, beyond existing material-specific studies.
method: Develops a stacking theory based on symmetry analysis and first-principles calculations to classify possible magnetic orders.
result: Identifies general rules for stacking-induced magnetism, predicting several new magnetic phases.
conclusion: Provides a framework for engineering magnetic properties in bilayer 2D magnets via stacking, relevant for spintronics.

title: Antiferromagnetic Solitons In NiO As Possible Entities For Logic Operations

[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214456] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.

motivation: To explore antiferromagnetic materials as a platform for high-speed, low-dissipation logic devices.
method: Atomistic simulations of NiO stripes to model spin wave and domain wall propagation.
result: Demonstrates fast soliton velocities over 40 km/s and interesting propagation properties enabling crossing and interference.
conclusion: Antiferromagnetic solitons in NiO show promise for logic operations, but further experimental validation is needed.

title: Nontrivial Three-sublattice Magnetization In The Easy-axis Spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ Xxz Antiferromagnet On The Triangular Lattice
authors: Masahiro Kadosawa, Masaaki Nakamura, Yukinori Ohta, And Satoshi Nishimoto

title: Spin-dependent Orbital Selectivity And Partial Kondo-like Screening In The Magnetically Ordered Hund's Metal ${\mathrm{Sr}}_{2}{\mathrm{CoO}}_{4}$
authors: Shivani Bhardwaj And Sudhir K. Pandey

tldr: This paper studies spin-dependent orbital selectivity and Kondo-like screening in the Hund's metal Sr2CoO4 using DFT+DMFT.
motivation: To understand the electronic structure and correlation effects in Hund's metals, which are rare and poorly understood.
method: First-principles DFT+DMFT calculations with continuous-time quantum Monte Carlo impurity solver.
result: They find spin-dependent orbital selectivity and partial Kondo-like screening in the magnetically ordered state.
conclusion: The study reveals complex interplay between Hund's coupling, orbital selectivity, and magnetic order in Sr2CoO4.

title: Quasiparticle Interference In LiFeAs: Signature Of Inelastic Tunneling Through Spin Fluctuations
authors: Shun Chi, Carolina A. Marques, W. N. Hardy, Ruixing Liang, Pinder Dosanjh, D. A. Bonn, S. A. Burke, And Peter Wahl
abstract:
Author(s): Shun Chi, Carolina A. Marques, W. N. Hardy, Ruixing Liang, Pinder Dosanjh, D. A. Bonn, S. A. Burke, and Peter Wahl

Quasiparticle interference (QPI) is a powerful tool to characterize the symmetry of the superconducting order parameter in unconventional superconductors, by mapping the spatial dependence of elastic tunneling of electrons between the tip of a scanning tunneling microscope and a sample. Here, we con…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235148] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies quasiparticle interference in the iron-based superconductor LiFeAs, attributing features to inelastic tunneling via spin fluctuations rather than elastic scattering.
motivation: To understand the nature of quasiparticle interference in LiFeAs and its implications for the superconducting order parameter symmetry.
method: Scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) measurements of quasiparticle interference patterns combined with theoretical modeling of inelastic tunneling mediated by spin fluctuations.
result: The observed QPI patterns are inconsistent with elastic scattering models but can be explained by inelastic tunneling through spin fluctuations, revealing the importance of many-body effects.
conclusion: Quasiparticle interference in LiFeAs is dominated by inelastic processes, which must be accounted for when using QPI to determine order parameter symmetry.

title: Exceptional Rings Emerging In A non-Hermitian Rice-Mele Ladder
authors: Ensuo Ma And Zhi Song
abstract:

Weyl exceptional lines typically occur in three-dimensional (3D) topological semimetals; however, they also emerge in the parameter space of one-dimensional (1D) systems. In this work, we study the impact of dissipation on the nodal ring in a 3D topological semimetal. We find that the energy spectru…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235150] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies exceptional rings in a non-Hermitian Rice-Mele ladder, focusing on topological semimetal physics in parameter space.
motivation: To understand the impact of dissipation on nodal rings in 3D topological semimetals, using a 1D ladder model.
method: The authors analyze a non-Hermitian Rice-Mele ladder model with dissipation, deriving the energy spectrum and identifying exceptional rings in parameter space.
result: Exceptional rings emerge in the parameter space of the 1D system, analogous to Weyl exceptional lines in 3D semimetals.
conclusion: The work extends the concept of exceptional lines to lower-dimensional systems, revealing topological features in non-Hermitian settings.

title: Taxonomy Of Integrable And Ground-state Solvable Models: Jastrow Wave Functions On Graphs And Parent Hamiltonians
authors: Nilanjan Sasmal And Adolfo Del Campo
abstract:

We introduce a family of many-body systems of distinguishable continuous-variable particles in which interparticle interactions are set by the adjacency matrix of a graph. [Phys. Rev. B 113, 235151] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a family of many-body systems with Jastrow ground states on graphs, focusing on integrability and exact solvability.
motivation: To classify and construct exactly solvable many-body models with Jastrow wave functions on arbitrary graphs.
method: The authors define a Hamiltonian based on the graph adjacency matrix and show that the ground state is a generalized Jastrow product.
result: They identify conditions for integrability and provide explicit parent Hamiltonians for various graph structures.
conclusion: The work provides a taxonomy of solvable models but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Toroidal Fermi Surface Geometry And Phonon-limited Transport In Nodal-line Semimetals
authors: Aman Anand And Alessandro de Martino
abstract:
Author(s): Aman Anand and Alessandro De Martino

Nodal-line semimetals (NLSs) can display unconventional quasiparticle dynamics and charge transport properties due to their extended band degeneracy and the peculiar geometry of their Fermi surface. We consider electron-acoustic phonon scattering as the dominant relaxation mechanism and compute the …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235432] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies phonon-limited transport in nodal-line semimetals, focusing on the role of toroidal Fermi surface geometry.
motivation: Nodal-line semimetals have unique Fermi surface geometry that may lead to unconventional transport properties, but the effect of electron-phonon scattering in these materials is not well understood.
method: The authors compute the electrical resistivity due to electron-acoustic phonon scattering using Boltzmann transport theory, incorporating the toroidal Fermi surface geometry.
result: They find that the temperature dependence of resistivity deviates from the standard Bloch-Grüneisen law due to the nodal-line topology.
conclusion: The toroidal Fermi surface geometry significantly modifies phonon-limited transport, which could be experimentally observed in nodal-line semimetals.

title: Free-electron Decoherence: Theory And Applications
authors: Cruz I. Velasco, Valerio Di Giulio, And F. Javier García de Abajo
abstract:
Author(s): Cruz I. Velasco, Valerio Di Giulio, and F. Javier García de Abajo

Electron microscopy relies on the spatial coherence of electron beams to generate atomic-scale images using interference and diffraction, which can be degraded by inelastic-scattering processes that induce decoherence. Here, we present a theoretical study of decoherence arising from the electromagne…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235433] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies decoherence of free electrons due to electromagnetic interactions, with applications in electron microscopy.
motivation: Understanding decoherence in electron beams is crucial for high-resolution electron microscopy, but the work is primarily focused on electron optics and microscopy rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on the electromagnetic interaction between a free electron and its environment, calculating decoherence rates and coherence lengths.
result: They derive expressions for decoherence induced by various inelastic scattering processes and discuss implications for electron microscopy imaging.
conclusion: The results provide a quantitative understanding of decoherence in free-electron beams, which can guide the design of coherent electron sources and microscopy techniques.

title: Theory Of ab Initio Downfolding With Arbitrary-range Electron-phonon Coupling
authors: Norm M. Tubman, Christopher J. N. Coveney, Chih-En Hsu, Andres Montoya-Castillo, Marina R. Filip, Jeffrey B. Neaton, Zhenglu Li, Vojtech Vlcek, And Antonios M. Alvertis

Ab initio downfolding describes the electronic structure of materials within a low-energy subspace, often around the Fermi level. Typically starting from mean-field calculations, this framework allows for the calculation of one- and two-electron interactions, and the parametrization of a many-body H…

tldr: This paper develops a theoretical framework for ab initio downfolding with arbitrary-range electron-phonon coupling to describe low-energy electronic structure in materials.
motivation: Accurate modeling of electron-phonon interactions is crucial for understanding material properties, but existing downfolding methods are limited to short-range coupling.
method: The authors extend downfolding theory to include arbitrary-range electron-phonon coupling, deriving effective Hamiltonians from first-principles calculations.
result: The framework enables systematic inclusion of long-range electron-phonon effects in low-energy models, improving accuracy for polar materials and superconductors.
conclusion: This work provides a more complete theoretical tool for studying electron-phonon physics in condensed matter, but does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics.

motivation: To understand the emergence of multiple zero modes in extended topological Josephson junctions beyond the simplified one-dimensional model.
method: The authors analyze a planar Josephson junction on a 3D topological insulator, considering experimentally relevant parameter regimes and solving the effective low-energy theory.
result: They find that multiple zero-energy Majorana modes can appear bound to vortices, depending on junction geometry and parameters.
conclusion: The work provides a more realistic description of Majorana modes in such junctions, relevant for topological quantum computing.

title: Controlled Pairing Symmetries In A Fermi-Hubbard Ladder With Band Flattening
authors: João P. Mendonça, S. Biswas, M. Dziurawiec, U. Bhattacharya, K. Jachymski, M. Aidelsburger, M. Lewenstein, M. M. Maśka, And T. Grass
abstract:

The competition between interactions in systems with slow electrons can drive unusual collective behavior. Here, the authors study a microscopic ladder model featuring both diagonal hopping pathways and complex loop-like electron exchange interactions. They demonstrate that while both mechanisms independently suppress ordinary metallic behavior, they stabilize completely distinct spatial patterns of electron pairing. These findings offer a theoretical framework for engineering specific superconducting states by tuning the competition between pairing mechanisms in platforms like twisted bilayer graphene or cold atoms.

motivation: To understand how interactions in systems with slow electrons can drive unusual collective behavior and to engineer specific superconducting states.
method: The authors analyze a microscopic ladder model with diagonal hopping and complex loop-like electron exchange interactions, using theoretical and numerical methods.
result: They find that the two mechanisms independently suppress metallic behavior but stabilize distinct spatial patterns of electron pairing.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for engineering superconducting states by tuning pairing mechanisms, relevant to platforms like twisted bilayer graphene or cold atoms.

title: Decisive Role Of An Extra Fe Sublattice: Frustration, Criticality, And Skyrmions In The Van Der Waals Ferromagnets ${\mathrm{Fe}}_{5}{\mathrm{GeTe}}_{2}$ Versus ${\mathrm{Fe}}_{3}{\mathrm{GeTe}}_{2}$

title: Van Hove Singularities In The Density Of States Of A Chaotic Dynamical System

[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064211] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper predicts statistics of chaotic systems using periodic differential operators and their density of states, with a focus on Van Hove singularities.
motivation: To understand and predict statistical properties of chaotic dynamical systems through an operator-theoretic approach.
method: Constructs a sequence of periodic differential operators associated with the chaotic system and computes their density of states.
result: The density of states for such operators can be computed analytically, often yielding explicit formulas that reveal Van Hove singularities.
conclusion: The approach provides a new way to analyze chaotic systems by linking them to well-understood periodic operators.

conclusion: Physics-informed neural networks offer a flexible approach for continuous-time synchronization control.

title: Electronic Access To Glass Transition In Supercooled Ionic Liquids Using Ambipolar Transistor
authors: Tanima Kundu, Rahul Paramanik, Aishee Saha, Shibnath Mandal, Antarik Sarkar, Bipul Karmakar, And Subhadeep Datta

conclusion: Electronic transport measurements can serve as a probe for glass transition dynamics in supercooled ionic liquids, offering a route compatible with electronic devices.

title: Robustness Of Networks Of Hypergraphs
authors: Xiyao Sun, Yuanyuan Pang, Zhengao Guo, Xiaoming Liang, And Jie Zhou

motivation: Real-world systems often involve higher-order interactions and interdependencies, which are not captured by standard network models.

motivation: Organic mixed conductors have complex dynamics across scales; understanding their phase behavior is key for applications in bioelectronics and thermoelectrics.
method: Develops a lattice gas model to capture electronic, ionic, and mass transport coupling, and analyzes phase transitions using statistical mechanics.
result: Identifies phase transition conditions and critical behavior in the lattice gas model for organic mixed conductors.
conclusion: The lattice gas model provides a framework to understand phase transitions in organic mixed conductors, relevant for material design.

title: Steady-state Equilibrium And Nonequilibrium Noisy Network Dynamics
authors: Pik-Yin Lai
abstract:
Author(s): Pik-Yin Lai (黎璧賢)

The fluctuating dynamics of a network about its stable, noise-free steady state are theoretically investigated. Various causes of nonequilibrium dynamics are identified in terms of the properties and symmetry of the network connections and the noise covariance matrices. Several equivalent conditions…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064148] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies steady-state fluctuations in noisy networks, focusing on equilibrium and nonequilibrium dynamics from a classical stochastic perspective.
motivation: To understand how network connectivity and noise properties lead to nonequilibrium steady states.
method: Theoretical analysis using Langevin equations and covariance matrices for network dynamics.
result: Identifies conditions for equilibrium and nonequilibrium dynamics based on network symmetry and noise correlations.
conclusion: The framework provides a general characterization of noisy network dynamics but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Precise Determination Of The Long-time Asymptotics Of The Diffusion Spreadability Of Two-phase Media
authors: Shaobing Yuan And Salvatore Torquato
abstract:
Author(s): Shaobing Yuan and Salvatore Torquato

The time-dependent diffusion spreadability [MATH] is a powerful dynamical probe of the microstructure of two-phase heterogeneous media across length scales [S. Torquato
tldr: This paper determines the long-time asymptotics of diffusion spreadability in two-phase media using spectral analysis.
motivation: Understanding diffusion in heterogeneous media is important for material science, but the paper focuses on classical diffusion, not quantum or information-theoretic aspects.
method: The authors derive exact representations of spreadability in terms of spectral functions and analyze asymptotic behavior using properties of the microstructure.
result: They provide precise asymptotic formulas for spreadability at long times, linking it to the spectral density of the two-phase medium.
conclusion: The work advances the theory of diffusion in heterogeneous media but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Collective Ballistic Motion Explains Fast Aggregation In Adhesive Active Matter
authors: Emanuel F. Teixeira, Pablo de Castro, Carine P. Beatrici, Heitor C. M. Fernandes, And Leonardo G. Brunnet
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuel F. Teixeira, Pablo de Castro, Carine P. Beatrici, Heitor C. M. Fernandes, and Leonardo G. Brunnet

Inspired by motile cells in tissue formation, we find that active systems of self-aligning adhesive particles undergo ballistic aggregation through a flocking transition. This kinetic regime emerges when the cluster persistence length grows faster with cluster mass than the intercluster distance doe…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065422] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies ballistic aggregation in active matter systems of self-aligning adhesive particles, focusing on collective motion and cluster growth.
motivation: Understanding fast aggregation in active matter, inspired by motile cells in tissue formation.
method: Simulations of self-aligning adhesive particles with alignment interactions, analyzing cluster persistence and aggregation kinetics.
result: A flocking transition leads to ballistic aggregation where cluster persistence length grows faster than intercluster distance.
conclusion: Collective ballistic motion explains rapid aggregation in adhesive active matter systems.

title: Nonreciprocal Blume-Capel Model With Antisymmetric Single-ion Anisotropies
authors: Arjun R, Pratyush Prakash Patra, And A. V. Anil Kumar
abstract:
Author(s): Arjun R, Pratyush Prakash Patra, and A. V. Anil Kumar

We investigate the interplay between nonreciprocal interactions and chemical-potential imbalance in a two-species nonreciprocal Blume-Capel model. Combining a systematic mean-field bifurcation analysis with large-scale Monte Carlo simulations in two and three dimensions, we map the model's dynamical…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064140] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: A study of nonreciprocal interactions and chemical-potential imbalance in a two-species Blume-Capel model using mean-field analysis and Monte Carlo simulations.
motivation: To understand the interplay between nonreciprocal interactions and chemical-potential imbalance in a classical spin model, which may exhibit novel dynamical phases.
method: Mean-field bifurcation analysis combined with large-scale Monte Carlo simulations in two and three dimensions.
result: The model's dynamical phase diagram is mapped, revealing nonreciprocal effects on phase transitions.
conclusion: Nonreciprocal interactions can lead to new dynamical behaviors in classical spin systems, but the work is primarily in statistical mechanics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Dynamic Monte Carlo Study Of Rigidity Percolation Using An Event-based Ensemble Approach
authors: Mingzhong Lu, Yufeng Song, Qiyuan Shi, Ming Li, And Youjin Deng
abstract:
Author(s): Mingzhong Lu, Yufeng Song, Qiyuan Shi, Ming Li, and Youjin Deng

Rigidity percolation provides an important basis for understanding the onset of mechanical stability in disordered materials. While most studies on the triangular lattice have focused on static properties at fixed bond (site) occupation probabilities, the dynamics of the rigidity transition remain l…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064141] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies rigidity percolation dynamics on a triangular lattice using an event-based ensemble Monte Carlo method.
motivation: Understanding the onset of mechanical stability in disordered materials requires studying the dynamics of rigidity percolation, which has been less explored than static properties.
method: The authors employ an event-based ensemble approach in dynamic Monte Carlo simulations to investigate the rigidity transition on a triangular lattice.
result: They characterize the dynamic critical behavior and identify the universality class of the rigidity percolation transition.
conclusion: The event-based ensemble method effectively captures the dynamics of rigidity percolation, providing insights into mechanical stability in disordered systems.

title: Relationship Between Heider Links And Ising Spins
authors: Zdzislaw Burda, Maciej Wołoszyn, Krzysztof Malarz, And Krzysztof Kułakowski
abstract:
Author(s): Zdzislaw Burda, Maciej Wołoszyn, Krzysztof Malarz, and Krzysztof Kułakowski

We show that the Heider model with an external field is equivalent, in the limit of structural balance, to the Ising model with nearest-neighbor interactions without an external field. More precisely, we claim that the signs of the Heider relations that maintain structural equilibrium in the system …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, L062104] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper establishes an equivalence between the Heider model of social balance and the Ising model, showing that structurally balanced Heider triads correspond to Ising ground states.
motivation: To connect sociological balance theory with statistical physics, providing a physical interpretation of Heider's social balance conditions.
method: The authors map Heider's signed relations (friend/enemy) to Ising spins and show that the condition for structural balance in the Heider model is equivalent to the ground state of an Ising model with nearest-neighbor interactions.
result: In the limit of structural balance, the Heider model with an external field reduces to the Ising model without an external field, with the sign of Heider relations determined by the Ising spin configuration.
conclusion: The equivalence provides a new perspective on social balance as a physical system, but the work is purely theoretical and does not involve quantum information, thermodynamics, or quantum hardware.

title: Discontinuous Wealth-gradient Transition Driving Cooperation
authors: Hyun Gyu Lee, Hyeong-Chai Jeong, And Deok-Sun Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Hyun Gyu Lee, Hyeong-Chai Jeong, and Deok-Sun Lee

The universal prevalence of cooperation is puzzling, as defection typically yields higher payoffs than cooperation, motivating searches for hidden pathways to cooperation. Here we study a game-theoretic model on a lattice structured population in which interaction payoffs are scaled by the minimum o…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064306] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies cooperation in a game-theoretic model on a lattice, focusing on wealth gradients and phase transitions.
motivation: Understanding the emergence of cooperation despite the payoff advantage of defection is a classic puzzle in evolutionary game theory.
method: The authors analyze a spatial game where payoffs are scaled by the minimum of players' wealth, leading to a wealth-gradient driven transition.
result: They find a discontinuous transition to cooperation as the wealth gradient increases, with critical behavior characterized by scaling laws.
conclusion: Wealth inequality can promote cooperation in structured populations, offering a new mechanism for the evolution of cooperation.

title: ChronoCast: A Time-series Paradigm For Molecular Dynamics Simulation Using Equivariant Graph Neural Networks
authors: Yuxing Wang, Zhongwei Zhang, Shuang Lu, Shuyue Shan, Vitaly A. Kuzkin, Anton M. Krivtsov, And Jie Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Yuxing Wang, Zhongwei Zhang, Shuang Lu, Shuyue Shan, Vitaly A. Kuzkin, Anton M. Krivtsov, and Jie Chen

We propose a time-series paradigm named ChronoCast for molecular dynamics simulation using an advanced autoregressive Equivariant Graph Neural Network, which reformulates the conventionally time-consuming integration process into a forecasting task. This reformulation in turn offers a promising solu…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065305] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: ChronoCast uses equivariant graph neural networks to accelerate molecular dynamics simulations by reformulating integration as a time-series forecasting task.
motivation: Molecular dynamics simulations are computationally expensive due to the need for numerical integration over many time steps; the authors aim to speed this up using machine learning.
method: They propose an autoregressive equivariant graph neural network that predicts future atomic positions and velocities from past trajectory data, effectively replacing the integrator.
result: The method achieves accurate long-term predictions with significant speedup compared to traditional MD simulations on benchmark systems.
conclusion: ChronoCast demonstrates that time-series forecasting with equivariant GNNs is a viable approach for accelerating molecular dynamics, though it is primarily a computational chemistry/materials science contribution.

title: Aging In A Two-dimensional Swarmalator Crystal With Delayed Interactions
authors: Chanin Kumpeerakij, Thiparat Chotibut, And Oleg Kogan
abstract:
Author(s): Chanin Kumpeerakij, Thiparat Chotibut, and Oleg Kogan

Time delay can have a significant impact on the properties of collective organization of active matter. In the previous paper [
tldr: This paper studies aging dynamics in a two-dimensional swarmalator crystal with delayed interactions, focusing on collective organization of active matter.
motivation: To understand how time delay affects the collective behavior of active matter systems, specifically swarmalators.
method: Numerical simulations and theoretical analysis of a swarmalator model with delayed interactions in two dimensions.
result: The system exhibits aging behavior characterized by slow dynamics and non-stationary correlation functions.
conclusion: Time delay can induce aging in swarmalator crystals, providing insights into non-equilibrium dynamics of active matter.

title: Tiling By Near Coincidence
authors: Meshy Ochana And Ron Lifshitz
abstract:
Author(s): Meshy Ochana and Ron Lifshitz

Moiré patterns of twisted and scaled bilayers have recently emerged as a fertile source of quasiperiodic order in two-dimensional materials. Inspired by these systems, we introduce the near-coincidence method for generating quasiperiodic tilings of the plane. The method is intuitive—admitting pairs …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023330] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a near-coincidence method for generating quasiperiodic tilings of the plane, inspired by moiré patterns in twisted bilayers.
motivation: To provide an intuitive method for generating quasiperiodic tilings that mimics the formation of moiré patterns in twisted and scaled bilayers.
method: The near-coincidence method constructs tilings by overlaying two periodic lattices with a slight mismatch in scale or rotation, then selecting tiles that nearly coincide.
result: The method produces a variety of quasiperiodic tilings, including those with 12-fold and 8-fold rotational symmetry.
conclusion: The near-coincidence method offers a simple and intuitive way to generate quasiperiodic tilings, potentially useful for modeling moiré materials.

title: Phase-space Topology And Spectral Flow In Screened Magnetized Plasmas
authors: Xianhao Rao, Adil Yolbarsop, Hong Li, And Wandong Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Xianhao Rao, Adil Yolbarsop, Hong Li, and Wandong Liu

Topological wave phenomena in continuous media are fundamentally challenged by unbounded spectra and the absence of a compact Brillouin zone, which obstruct conventional bulk-interface formulations. We develop a unified phase-space framework for screened magnetized plasma based on a pseudo-Hermitian…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023334] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a phase-space framework for topological wave phenomena in screened magnetized plasmas, focusing on spectral flow and bulk-interface correspondence in continuous media.
motivation: Topological wave phenomena in continuous media are challenged by unbounded spectra and lack of a compact Brillouin zone, which obstruct conventional bulk-interface formulations.
method: The authors develop a unified phase-space framework based on pseudo-Hermitian operators to analyze topological properties of screened magnetized plasmas.
result: They demonstrate spectral flow and topological invariants in the phase-space description, establishing a bulk-interface correspondence for continuous media.
conclusion: The phase-space framework provides a robust approach to study topological phenomena in continuous media with unbounded spectra.

title: One-particle Density Matrix Framework For Mode-shell Correspondence: Characterizing Topology In Amorphous Higher-order Topological Insulators
authors: Miguel F. Martínez, Lucien Jezequel, Jens H. Bardarson, Thomas Klein Kvorning, And Julia D. Hannukainen
abstract:

We present a framework for characterizing higher-order topological phases directly from the one-particle density matrix, without any reference to an underlying Hamiltonian. Our approach extends the mode-shell correspondence, originally formulated for single-particle Hamiltonians, to Gaussian states …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023320] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: A framework for characterizing higher-order topological phases in amorphous materials using the one-particle density matrix.
motivation: To extend topological characterization to amorphous systems where traditional band-structure methods fail.
method: Extends the mode-shell correspondence to Gaussian states via the one-particle density matrix.
result: Demonstrates that higher-order topological invariants can be computed from the density matrix without a Hamiltonian.
conclusion: Provides a robust method for identifying topological phases in disordered or amorphous materials.

title: Excited Eigenstates From A Two-species Random Walk
authors: Paul-Henry Glinel, Normand Beaudoin, And Alexandre Melanson
abstract:
Author(s): Paul-Henry Glinel, Normand Beaudoin, and Alexandre Melanson

Macroscopically, the population density function of random walk models can satisfy self-contained dynamics and exhibit unexpected order. Here, we show how a two-species random walk model that includes diffusion, probabilistic absorption of walkers mediated by a potential function, cross-species anni…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023324] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: A two-species random walk model with diffusion, absorption, and cross-species annihilation is studied, showing emergent order in population density.
motivation: To understand how macroscopic order can arise from stochastic microscopic dynamics in multi-species systems.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of a two-species random walk with diffusion, potential-mediated absorption, and annihilation.
result: The population density function satisfies self-contained dynamics and exhibits unexpected order.
conclusion: The model demonstrates that complex interactions in random walks can lead to emergent macroscopic behavior.

title: Theory Of High-harmonic Generation With Quantum Light
authors: Haoyu Liu, Hanxu Zhang, Xu Wang, And Jianmin Yuan
abstract:
Author(s): Haoyu Liu, Hanxu Zhang, Xu Wang, and Jianmin Yuan

High-harmonic generation (HHG) driven by intense quantum light has recently emerged as a new frontier in strong-field physics. Yet, the mechanism underlying HHG with nonclassical fields such as bright squeezed vacuum (BSV) light—characterized by a vanishing mean electric field—remains elusive. In th…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023326] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a theory of high-harmonic generation driven by quantum light, specifically bright squeezed vacuum, revealing a new mechanism distinct from classical HHG.
motivation: High-harmonic generation with nonclassical light, such as bright squeezed vacuum, is a new frontier but the underlying mechanism is not understood.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework combining strong-field physics with quantum optics, analyzing the HHG process driven by quantum light with vanishing mean field.
result: They identify a new mechanism for HHG that relies on quantum fluctuations rather than the classical electric field, and predict distinct spectral features.
conclusion: Quantum light can drive HHG via a fundamentally different mechanism, opening new possibilities for attosecond science and quantum optics.

title: Before The Cycle Is Over: Subcycle Time Refraction At Optical Frequencies
authors: Ohad Segal, Noa Konforty, Oded Schiller, Maxwell J. Tolchin, Tony Yasniger, Soham Saha, Ryan W. Spangler, Jon-Paul Maria, Yonatan Plotnik, And Mordechai Segev
abstract:
Author(s): Ohad Segal, Noa Konforty, Oded Schiller, Maxwell J. Tolchin, Tony Yasniger, Soham Saha, Ryan W. Spangler, Jon-Paul Maria, Yonatan Plotnik, and Mordechai Segev

This work demonstrates subcycle order-unity variations in the refractive index at optical frequencies and measures the time-refraction of a probe wave propagating in the modulated medium.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022054] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates subcycle time refraction at optical frequencies by modulating refractive index on ultrafast timescales.
motivation: To achieve and measure order-unity refractive index changes within an optical cycle, enabling new regimes of light-matter interaction.
method: Experimental setup using ultrafast optical modulation to vary the refractive index of a medium on subcycle timescales, with a probe wave measuring the time-refraction effect.
result: Observation of subcycle order-unity refractive index variations and successful measurement of time-refraction of a probe wave.
conclusion: Subcycle time refraction is feasible at optical frequencies, opening possibilities for ultrafast optical control and novel photonic devices.

title: Machine-learning-guided Discovery Of Kagome Superconductors ${\mathrm{YRu}}_{3}{\mathrm{B}}_{2}$ And ${\mathrm{LuRu}}_{3}{\mathrm{B}}_{2}$
authors: Rose Albu Mustaf, Sajilesh K. P., Sanu Mishra, Junze Deng, Yi Jiang, Kaja H. Hiorth, Eeli O. Lamponen, Martin Gutierrez-Amigo, Päivi Törmä, Miguel A. L. Marques, B. Andrei Bernevig, And Emilia Morosan

We report the experimental discovery of bulk superconductivity in two kagome lattice compounds, [MATH] and [MATH], which were predicted through machine-learning-accelerated high-throughput screening combined with first-principles calculati…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023308] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Machine learning and first-principles calculations predict and experimentally discover two new kagome superconductors.
motivation: To discover new kagome superconductors, which are of interest for their exotic electronic properties, using machine learning to accelerate high-throughput screening.
method: Machine-learning-accelerated high-throughput screening combined with first-principles calculations to predict candidate materials, followed by experimental synthesis and characterization.
result: Discovery of bulk superconductivity in YRu3B2 and LuRu3B2, two kagome lattice compounds.
conclusion: The approach successfully identifies new kagome superconductors, demonstrating the power of machine learning in materials discovery.

title: Observation Of Surface Ferromagnons In The Axion-insulating Phase Of The Antiferromagnetic Topological Insulator ${\mathrm{EuSn}}_{2}{\mathrm{As}}_{2}$
authors: Mamoun Hemmida, Santanu Pakhira, David C. Johnston, And Hans-Albrecht Krug von Nidda
abstract:
Author(s): Mamoun Hemmida, Santanu Pakhira, David C. Johnston, and Hans-Albrecht Krug von Nidda

We report the study of spin dynamics of [MATH] in the antiferromagnetic axion topological insulator [MATH] by means of antiferromagnetic resonance at 9.34 GHz. Below the Néel temperature ([MATH]), two types of resonance modes, the conventiona…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023309] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports antiferromagnetic resonance measurements in the topological insulator EuSn2As2, observing surface ferromagnons in the axion-insulating phase.
motivation: To study spin dynamics and surface magnetic excitations in a topological insulator with antiferromagnetic order, which is relevant for understanding axion electrodynamics in condensed matter.
method: Electron spin resonance (ESR) at 9.34 GHz was used to measure antiferromagnetic resonance modes below the Néel temperature.
result: Two resonance modes were observed: conventional antiferromagnetic resonance and a surface ferromagnon mode, indicating surface ferromagnetic order.
conclusion: The surface ferromagnon mode is a signature of the axion-insulating phase, providing insight into the interplay between magnetism and topology.

title: Rare Cage Escapes Drive Relaxation In Deeply Supercooled Liquids
authors: Francesco Rusciano, Raffaele Pastore, Francesco Greco, And Walter Kob
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Rusciano, Raffaele Pastore, Francesco Greco, and Walter Kob

Simulations conducted significantly below the mode coupling temperature allow dynamic properties of glass forming systems to be uncovered.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021061] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: Simulations of deeply supercooled liquids reveal that rare cage escapes drive relaxation dynamics.
motivation: Understanding relaxation in supercooled liquids is key to the glass transition problem.
method: Molecular dynamics simulations below the mode coupling temperature.
result: Rare cage escape events are the primary mechanism for structural relaxation.
conclusion: The findings provide new insight into the microscopic origin of slow dynamics in glass formers.

title: Dynamics Of Quantum Chiral Solitons
authors: Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, And Cristian D. Batista
abstract:
Author(s): Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, and Cristian D. Batista

A nonperturbative quantization framework for chiral solitons in spin chains demonstrates that they condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid, appearing as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase and becoming detectable via inelastic neutron scattering.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021056] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a nonperturbative quantization framework for chiral solitons in spin chains, showing they condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid and are detectable via neutron scattering.
motivation: To understand the quantum dynamics of chiral solitons in spin chains, which are topological excitations with potential relevance to low-dimensional magnetism.
method: A nonperturbative quantization approach is applied to chiral solitons in a spin chain model, analyzing their condensation into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid.
result: Chiral solitons appear as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase and can be detected via inelastic neutron scattering.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for chiral soliton dynamics and suggests experimental signatures in neutron scattering.

title: Free And Interacting Fermionic Conformal Field Theories On The Fuzzy Sphere
authors: Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, And Yin-Chen He
abstract:
Author(s): Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, and Yin-Chen He

Researchers use noncommutative “fuzzy” spheres to study three-dimensional fermionic conformal field theories, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021055] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses fuzzy sphere regularization to study free and interacting fermionic conformal field theories in three dimensions, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.
motivation: To develop a non-perturbative method for studying strongly coupled conformal field theories, particularly fermionic ones, using the fuzzy sphere as a regularization scheme.
method: The authors employ the fuzzy sphere, a noncommutative geometry, to regularize three-dimensional fermionic CFTs and perform numerical simulations to compute spectra and correlation functions.
result: They find evidence of emergent supersymmetry in the interacting fermionic CFTs and demonstrate the effectiveness of the fuzzy sphere approach for studying such theories.
conclusion: The fuzzy sphere provides a viable numerical tool for investigating fermionic CFTs and may reveal new phenomena like emergent supersymmetry.

title: General Approach To Solving Spin Moiré Superstructures
authors: Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. Debeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, And Joseph G. Checkelsky
abstract:
Author(s): Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. DeBeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, and Joseph G. Checkelsky

Mapping of spin textures in EuAg
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021054] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a general approach to solving spin moiré superstructures in EuAg4Sb2, revealing three distinct magnetic phases and establishing a design framework for spin-based vortex lattices.
motivation: To understand and control complex spin textures in moiré superstructures, which are of interest for information manipulation via spin-based vortex lattices.
method: The authors use neutron scattering and other experimental techniques to map spin textures in EuAg4Sb2, combined with theoretical modeling to identify three tunable magnetic phases.
result: Three distinct magnetic phases are discovered in EuAg4Sb2, and a general framework for designing spin moiré superstructures is established.
conclusion: The work provides a platform for engineering spin textures that could be used for information processing, but the connection to quantum information or thermodynamics is not directly addressed.

title: Fate Of Topological Dirac Magnons In Van Der Waals Ferromagnets At Finite Temperature
authors: Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, And Alexander Mook
abstract:
Author(s): Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, and Alexander Mook

Theoretical modeling of magnon interactions at finite temperatures demonstrates that topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable near the Curie point, providing a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021053] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the stability of topological magnon gaps in van der Waals ferromagnets at finite temperature using theoretical modeling.
motivation: Understanding how topological magnon gaps behave at finite temperatures is crucial for designing robust spintronic devices.
method: The authors perform theoretical modeling of magnon interactions at finite temperatures, likely using many-body perturbation theory or spin-wave theory.
result: Topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable near the Curie point.
conclusion: The findings provide a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices based on topological magnons.

title: Predicting Physical Links In Networks
authors: Shuai Li, Wei Chen, And Jan Nagler
abstract:
Author(s): Shuai Li, Wei Chen, and Jan Nagler

A physics-informed framework allows for inferring general causal links across a wide range of networked dynamics systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021048] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A physics-informed framework for inferring causal links in networked dynamical systems.
motivation: Understanding causal relationships in complex networks is important but challenging; the paper aims to provide a general method using physical principles.
method: The authors develop a framework that incorporates physical constraints to infer causal links from observed dynamics in networks.
result: The framework successfully predicts physical links across various networked dynamical systems, demonstrating broad applicability.
conclusion: The physics-informed approach offers a powerful tool for causal inference in networks, with potential applications in many fields.

title: Anyon Superfluidity Of Excitons In Quantum Hall Bilayers
authors: Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, And Ashvin Vishwanath
abstract:
Author(s): Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, and Ashvin Vishwanath

Theoretical analysis of quantum Hall bilayers reveals that topological criticality facilitates the emergence of anyonic exciton superfluids, offering a robust mechanism for engineering exotic collective quantum states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021044] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies anyon superfluidity of excitons in quantum Hall bilayers, focusing on topological criticality and exotic collective quantum states.
motivation: To understand and engineer exotic collective quantum states in quantum Hall bilayers through topological criticality.
method: Theoretical analysis of quantum Hall bilayers, likely using field theory or topological arguments.
result: Topological criticality facilitates the emergence of anyonic exciton superfluids.
conclusion: Provides a robust mechanism for engineering exotic collective quantum states in quantum Hall systems.

title: Three-Dimensional Xy Universality And Nonlinear Magnetic Susceptibility In A Kagome Ice Compound
authors: Kan Zhao, Hao Deng, Hua Chen, Nvsen Ma, Noah Oefele, Jiesen Guo, Xueling Cui, Chen Tang, Matthias J. Gutmann, Thomas Mueller, Yixi Su, Vladimir Hutanu, Changqing Jin, And Philipp Gegenwart
abstract:
